items.title: Addressable transversal CCZ gates on almost good quantum LDPC codes and nearly optimal magic state protocols
items.summary: Assuming uniform subfield product expansion, we construct quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes with distances $Ω_ε(N/\log^2N)$ and at least $N^{1-ε}$ individually addressable logical CCZ gates on pairwise disjoint triples of logical qubits, for every fixed $0<ε<1$. With all logical qubits outside these triples initialized to $|0\rangle$, any subset of the corresponding logical CCZ gates can be implemented with a transversal physical CCZ circuit. As applications, we obtain two nearly optimal magic state protocols: CCZ distillation with arbitrarily small overhead exponent $γ\rightarrow 0$ and error suppression of nearly linear order, and a magic state fountain that directly prepares $N^{1-ε}$ encoded CCZ magic states with nearly linear distance $Ω_ε(N/\log^2N)$.
items.author: Shi Jie Samuel Tan, Guanyu Zhu

items.title: Physics-Guided Crystal Structure Elucidation from Powder X-Ray Diffraction with Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
items.summary: Determining unique atomic coordinates from powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) remains challenging because peak overlap, weak scattering from light elements, limited scattering contrast between elements with similar atomic numbers, and experimental noise render the inverse problem underdetermined. Here, we present XCAPE (XRD-Constrained Accelerated Prediction Engine), a crystal structure prediction (CSP) framework that integrates experimentally derived composition, unit cell parameters, space group, and PXRD data into a symmetry-aware evolutionary search. XCAPE explores Wyckoff-site configurations using tailored mutation operations, evaluates candidates by both energetic stability and diffraction agreement, and accelerates geometry optimization using a universal machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP). The framework recovered 71 of 77 database-derived benchmark structures (92.2%) from simulated PXRD patterns and all 12 reference structures from experimental PXRD patterns.
items.author: Yunsung Lim, Seungwoo Hwang, Seungwu Han

items.title: Parity Push Post-Selection with Soft Parity Constraints for Quantum LDPC Codes
items.summary: Post-selection lowers the logical error rate of a quantum error-correcting code by rejecting unreliable shots. For a code with $K$ logical observables, the logical gap, a standard post-selection criterion, involves $2^K$ logical classes, and existing approximations to it suffer from a non-convergence error floor or a shielding effect. We introduce a decoder-agnostic post-selection strategy for quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes, called parity push post-selection (PPPS), which re-decodes a shot once per logical observable with a push toward the opposite parity. Each push adds one check node and one variable node to the Tanner graph of the detector error model, and we accept a shot only when every re-decoding returns a solution in the original logical class.
items.author: Hong Jun Kim, Gun Sik Min, Seok-Hyung Lee et al.

items.title: Charged Schrödinger blocks in $1+1$ dimensions from the quartic Casimir and endpoint equations
items.summary: We construct charge-two Schrödinger conformal blocks in one spatial dimension, independently of any dynamical realization. We consider ordered vacuum four-point functions of fundamental fields of dimension $1/2$, with homogeneous Schrödinger equations at the earliest and latest insertions and interactions allowed in the intermediate two-particle interval. For reduced blocks analytic in signed spatial coordinates and even under simultaneous spatial inversion, two functions of the time cross-ratio determine the full spatial dependence: the collinear value and a rescaled mixed spatial derivative. An exact Kummer lift, built from confluent hypergeometric functions, gives this reconstruction. An operator identity reduces the quartic Casimir equation, modulo the endpoint equations, to an equivalent coupled system for this pair.
items.author: Hirohiko Shimada

items.title: Gopakumar-Vafa invariants and Mordell-Weil lattices
items.summary: Let $X\to B$ be a Weierstrass fibration with integral fibers from a smooth Calabi--Yau threefold to a del Pezzo surface. For a smooth curve $D\subset B$ with smooth inverse image $Y$, we decompose the moduli fiber of stable sheaves with Euler characteristic one and projected cycle $D$. In fiber degree $k$, its components are indexed by all sections $C$ of $Y\to D$ with $\tfrac12\langle C,C\rangle\leq k$, where $\langle\, ,\,\rangle$ is the Mordell--Weil height pairing. For infinitesimally rigid sections we compute the GV contributions, recovering the $E_8$ theta product over a $(-1)$-curve. We formulate the corresponding conjecture for families of sections.
items.author: Lutian Zhao

items.title: XANES-Guided Molecular Structure Generation via Conditional Diffusion and Forward Spectral Prediction
items.summary: Reconstructing complete molecular structures from X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra remains challenging because the spectra primarily encode local chemical environments, with overlapping contributions from multiple absorbing sites. Here, we develop an inverse-forward framework combining XANES-conditioned diffusion-based molecular structure generation with forward spectral prediction for candidate selection. The inverse model generates atomic species, bond connectivity, and three-dimensional coordinates from C, N, and O K-edge XANES, given only the total atom count without molecular formulas or element-specific atom counts. Combining all three absorption edges substantially improves structural recovery, achieving a best-of-10 exact-match rate of 56.6% across 2,888 test molecules. The generated candidates also reproduce functional groups and structural motifs, achieving a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.951 across 21 categories.
items.author: Yu Fujikata, Teruyasu Mizoguchi

items.title: M 5.8 - 150 km SW of Merizo Village, Guam
items.summary: A magnitude 5.8 earthquake was recorded 150 km SW of Merizo Village, Guam. The event happened on 18 November 2026 at 02:22 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 10 km. About 8 people reported feeling it. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data. The agency event page has the map, updates and safety information.
items.author: USGS

items.title: Fast closed-loop STEM navigation using vision-language models with typed decisions
items.summary: Closed-loop scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), in which each acquired image determines the next field of view and magnification, offers a route to autonomous atomic-scale materials analysis. Such a loop would automate navigation to defects and grain boundaries, a task that has long relied on operator judgment, and would enable systematic analysis of diverse local structures at scale. Realizing it hinges on the decision step, which must translate each acquired image into the next operation both quickly and correctly; yet which decision method can deliver both remains unclear. Here, we isolate this decision step. Using simulated atomic-resolution STEM images of a substitutional W dopant and a grain boundary in monolayer MoS$_2$, where the true target position is known and every method starts from identical conditions, we compared four vision-language models (VLMs) and three decision methods.
items.author: Shuichiro Ozawa, Izumi Takahara, Fumihiko Uesugi et al.

items.title: Structured Extraction of Diffraction Data from Covalent Organic Frameworks
items.summary: Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) is the primary structural evidence for covalent organic frameworks (COFs) and many other materials. Yet decades of measured patterns exist only as images in published figures. Automatic recovery is difficult, because PXRD figures vary widely in format, from a single curve to crowded stacks with labels, insets, and neighboring plots that challenge traditional computer vision. This work presents a pipeline in which a vision large language model (LLM) interprets the layout of each figure, locating the diffraction plot and its curves and sketching a coarse trace of each, while classical computer vision (CV) refines every trace to pixel-level accuracy.
items.author: Shenghan Gao, Zhiling Zheng

items.title: Simultaneous spectral measurement and programmable filtering on a universal silicon photonic chip
items.summary: Spectral measurement and spectral filtering are two fundamental operations in optics, yet they are conventionally implemented using separate optical systems, hindering their simultaneous and programmable operation on a common platform. Here, we demonstrate a universal silicon photonic chip that unifies spectral measurement and programmable filtering within a single integrated architecture. The chip comprises two 8 * 8 programmable unitary transformation circuits interconnected through optical intensity modulators, forming a universal linear optical circuit. In contrast to conventional universal circuits employing equal-length interconnections, we deliberately introduce different optical path lengths between the two unitary circuits. The resulting wavelength-dependent phase evolution provides spectral diversity while preserving the programmability of the universal circuit, enabling parallel spectral measurement and programmable filtering.
items.author: Yangyang Wan, Rui Tang, Kazuhiro Ikeda et al.

items.title: M 5.3 - 17 km ESE of Comandău, Romania
items.summary: A magnitude 5.3 earthquake was recorded 17 km ESE of Comandău, Romania. The event happened on 18 November 2026 at 00:48 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 132 km. About 419 people reported feeling it. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data. The agency event page has the map, updates and safety information.

items.title: M 5.3 - 7 km SE of Karakenja, Tajikistan
items.summary: A magnitude 5.3 earthquake was recorded 7 km SE of Karakenja, Tajikistan. The event happened on 18 November 2026 at 00:46 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 10 km. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data. The agency event page has the map, updates and safety information.
items.author: USGS

items.title: Long-lasting chromatin and transcriptional states shape the maintenance of memory ensembles
items.summary: Memories of recent events are stored within minutes in neuronal ensembles in the hippocampus. Over days to weeks, these memories undergo consolidation, and later retrieval depends on reactivation of a subset of neurons within the ensemble. However, how transient experiences produce lasting molecular and cellular changes in hippocampal ensemble neurons remains unknown. Here, we profile the functional, transcriptional, and gene regulatory states of hippocampal memory ensemble neurons at single cell resolution across multiple remote timepoints following single trial contextual fear conditioning. We uncover long lasting, cell type specific chromatin and gene expression changes after learning that coincide with sustained shifts in synaptic plasticity.
items.author: Vogel, I. R., Kruettner, S., Guzikowski, N. J. et al.

items.title: Transcriptomic and Lipidomic Profiling of Human iPSC-Derived Microglia Reveals TREM2-Dependent and -Independent Processes
items.summary: TREM2 has been implicated in AD as a critical regulator of microglial functions and loss of function mutations in TREM2 increases one's risk of developing AD. Given the diverse functional roles of TREM2, we sought to unravel how it affects downstream pathways using human iPSC-derived microglia-like cells (iMGLs) derived from TREM2 knockout (KO) and isogenic control lines and assessing the response to oligomeric amyloid-{beta} 42 (oA{beta}42). While previous studies have primarily used fibrillar A{beta}, we focused on microglial responses to oA{beta}42 given their disease relevance and potent cytotoxic effects. At baseline, we identified a set of TREM2-dependent genes, which corresponded to the DAM signature in mice and disease-associated signatures in humans.
items.author: Cardona, C. L., Patel, R., Finan, G. M. et al.

items.title: In vivo crosslinking and cryo-EM analyses suggest a revised model of conjugative pilus biogenesis
items.summary: Bacterial conjugation requires elaboration of a conjugative pilus by membrane-embedded transport machineries known as Type IV Secretion Systems (T4SSs). Recent structural findings suggested a model of conjugative pilus biogenesis in which the pilus is assembled from the VirB6-base of the T4SS Stalk, while the VirB5-apex is projected at the pilus tip. In this study, we show that in vivo crosslinking of these two Stalk segments within the R388 T4SS has only a modest effect on conjugative transfer efficiency, inconsistent with them separating during pilus elaboration. Combined with cryo-electron microscopy analyses of the homologous pKM101 T4SS, this leads us to propose a revised model, in which the sixfold-symmetrical inner membrane complex of the T4SS serves directly as a base for assembly of the fivefold-symmetrical pilus.
items.author: Bloch, M., Vadakeppat, A., Zenezini Chiozzi, R. et al.

items.title: In the non-canonical NF-κB pathway, binding of the initiating kinase NIK to the pathway's target, p100, serves a nonenzymatic "licensing" role
items.summary: The non-canonical NF-{kappa}B pathway plays pivotal roles in adaptive immunity. It is initiated by NIK-mediated phosphorylation of IKK1, which phosphorylates p100 and promotes processing of newly synthesized p100. However, IKK1 can also be activated by other kinases to mediate distinct functions. Why IKK1-induced p100 processing occurs efficiently downstream of NIK but not of other kinases is unknown. Here, we show that whereas pre-existing p100 can be phosphorylated by IKK1 without NIK, phosphorylation of newly synthesized p100 critically depends on additional non-enzymatic functions of NIK's C-terminal portion. NIK binds IKK1 and restrains its kinase activity, while its binding to p100 enhances p100 phosphorylation.
items.author: Liang, X., Scheerer, D., Bogdanov, K. et al.

items.title: Development of synthetic genetic arrays for studying interactions between the mitochondrial and nuclear genomes
items.summary: Mitochondria, the central axis of metabolism and energy transformation has emerged as a focal point for understanding the aging process and a plethora of human diseases. Yet, how the mitochondrial and nuclear genomes communicate is still unclear. This work aims to allow the analysis of such crosstalk by developing a genome-wide platform for studying genetic interactions between the mitochondrial and nuclear genomes. Using yeast as a model system in which mitochondrial homoplasmy and stable alterations in the mitochondrial genome can be generated by biolistic bombardment, we created a genome-wide library of yeast cells carrying nuclear deletions and temperature-sensitive mutations together with a superfolder-GFP reporter for the expression of the mitochondrial-encoded COX2 gene.
items.author: Schneider, K. L., Braam, S., Hao, X. et al.

items.title: Single-molecule tracking in the psychrophile Psychrobacter cryohalolentis reveals heat-shock-induced changes in ClpX dynamics
items.summary: Psychrophilic organisms display a series of physiological adaptations which enable them to thrive in cold environments, yet the dynamics of these processes in living cells remain largely unexplored. Here, we establish super-resolution microscopy and single-molecule tracking (SMT) in the cold-adapted bacterium Psychrobacter cryohalolentis, enabling the investigation of protein dynamics in vivo at high spatiotemporal resolution. For controlled expression of HaloTag fusions in this organism, we developed an inducible plasmid expression system based on a galactose-inducible promoter. As a proof of concept, we followed the AAA+ unfoldase ClpX during steady-state growth and heat shock. At 22 {degrees}C, ClpX diffused as a single population with a media apparent diffusion coefficient of 0.25 m2/s, suggesting that most molecules reside in large complexes.
items.author: Nery, E. T., Sui, Y., Mäkelä, J.

items.title: Sidetrak: a de novo-designed miniprotein targets the kinesin-1 coiled-coil stalk to inhibit MAP7 binding and disrupt mitochondrial transport
items.summary: The coiled-coil domains of cytoskeletal motors contain regulatory surfaces that offer largely unexploited targets for manipulating intracellular transport. The microtubule-associated protein MAP7 promotes kinesin-1 motor activity, binding a coiled-coil surface that overlaps the TPR docking site (TDS), a regulatory interface involved in autoinhibition. Starting from an AlphaFold3 model of this relatively feature-poor surface, we used BoltzGen to design Sidetrak, a 36-amino acid miniprotein that binds kinesin-1 with nanomolar affinity. Binding requires the TDS and is abolished by mutation of the predicted Sidetrak interface, supporting the modelled local geometry of the targeted coiled-coil region. Sidetrak inhibits MAP7 binding, reduces MAP7-dependent kinesin-1 recruitment to microtubules in cells and causes perinuclear redistribution of mitochondria, a kinesin-1 cargo.
items.author: Cross, J. A., Bristow, S. A., Babuji, T. et al.

items.title: Repeated regeneration prolongs the juvenile stage and extends lifespan in the annelid Platynereis dumerilii
items.summary: Regeneration restores tissues lost to injury, but its consequences may extend beyond local repair. Whether regeneration produces lasting systemic effects on developmental timing and lifespan remains poorly understood. Here we investigated the long-term consequences of repeated regeneration in the marine annelid Platynereis dumerilii. To determine these consequences, we repeatedly amputated juveniles at monthly intervals, removing approximately half of the body after each regenerative cycle, and compared them with control unamputated siblings. Repeatedly regenerating worms lived approximately 1.5-fold longer than controls and showed delayed sexual maturation, including delayed gametogenic progression at the morphological and transcriptional levels. Somatic progression was also delayed, as indicated by slower accumulation of pigmentation associated with developmental progression, while regenerative competence was maintained across amputations.
items.author: Ribeiro, R. P., Hong, K., Krawczynski, A. et al.

items.title: A unifying framework for structured population dynamics in modern coexistence theory
items.summary: Variation within populations is ubiquitous in nature, yet many models and frameworks in community ecology assume that all individuals within a population interact with the community identically. Modern coexistence theory is no exception; however, several subfields of ecology have independently been integrating coexistence theory, each asking the same underlying question: how do structured population dynamics shape coexistence outcomes? Here, I propose a unifying framework for integrating population variation into modern coexistence theory that is applicable across all fields of ecology. The application of this framework is presented in three case studies: niche overlap and fitness differences between influenza substrains, mutual invasibility between competing perennial plants, and fluctuation-dependent invasion outcomes in apparently competing prey with a foraging-predation risk tradeoff.
items.author: Brennan, J.

items.title: Microeukaryotic indicators of freshwater ecosystem condition from a national river monitoring network
items.summary: Microeukaryotes are a diverse and functionally important component of river biofilms, including primary producers, consumers, decomposers, and parasites and symbionts. However, their diversity is likely underestimated, and their composition, environmental drivers, and seasonal dynamics have rarely been studied at large spatial scales. Microbiological monitoring of freshwater ecosystems has historically focused almost entirely on diatoms, so the potential of the wider microbial community as indicators of river condition is unknown. Here, we used 18S rRNA gene metabarcoding of more than 1,600 biofilm samples from 700 sites across England's River Surveillance Network. We show that communities were dominated by diatoms, chlorophytes, ciliates, and fungi, and shifted from phototroph-dominated biofilms in spring towards more diverse, heterotroph-rich biofilms in autumn.
items.author: Thorpe, A. C., Busi, S. B., Warren, J. et al.

items.title: Genetic nurture and shared environmental effects across cognitive, educational, and mental health outcomes
items.summary: Genetic nurture, in which parental genotype predicts offspring outcomes independent of offspring genotype, operates at the between-family level, corresponding to the shared environmental effect (C) in the classical twin design. Genetic nurture represents a portion of C captured by parental genotype. The link between genetic nurture and C has not been systematically quantified across multiple trait domains. Using 2559 families with genotyped parents and 6710 twin pairs, we estimated genetic nurture using polygenic scores (PGS) and C using the twin design for 40 educational, cognitive, and anthropometric outcomes from age 7 to 26, and for 8 psychopathology symptoms at age 26.
items.author: Lin, Y., Ayorech, Z., Kawakami, K. et al.

items.title: A large-scale multi-omics study of cortical miRNA dysregulation in Alzheimer's disease
items.summary: MicroRNAs regulate gene expression, but their roles in Alzheimer's disease pathology and downstream molecular changes remain incompletely characterized. We integrated cortical small RNA-sequencing data from seven datasets across six postmortem cohorts comprising 1,738 individuals with transcriptomic, proteomic, genetic, and single-nucleus data. Meta-analysis of 405 microRNAs identified 16 associated with advanced and four with intermediate neurofibrillary tangle pathology, with miR-132-3p significant in both comparisons. Five microRNAs (miR-132-3p, miR-212-3p, miR-212-5p, miR-146b-5p, miR-3200-3p) showed evidence of mediating associations between target mRNA and protein expression and tau pathology. Consensus co-expression network analysis linked the miR-132/212 family to opposing neuronal/synaptic and oligodendrocyte/myelination-related programmes. Mediated targets were enriched among tau-associated differentially expressed genes across glial cell types, particularly astrocytes.
items.author: Pishva, E., Kouhsar, M., Aslam, M. M. et al.

items.title: The genetic regulation of thyroid hormones on immune and hematopoietic homeostasis: an integrative Mendelian randomization and colocalization study
items.summary: Background: Hematological traits are closely linked to immune and inflammatory processes implicated in thyroid dysfunction. Although observational studies have reported associations between blood-cell traits and thyroid disorders, whether these relationships reflect causal mechanisms remains unclear. Methods: We performed a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis to investigate the causal effects of 25 genetically predicted hematological traits on hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism using genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics from the UK Biobank. Independent single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were selected as instrumental variables and harmonized before analysis. Causal estimates were primarily obtained using the inverse-variance weighted (IVW) method and complemented by MR-Egger, weighted median, weighted mode, simple mode, MR-PRESSO, and MR-robust adjusted profile score (MR-RAPS) analyses.
items.author: Ansah, E. O., Fosu, K., Adu, I. K. et al.

items.title: 'Silent Spring' revisited: sublethal neonicotinoid exposure suppresses birdsong
items.summary: Neonicotinoids are widely used pesticides linked to impaired reproduction and population decline in birds. However, the behavioral mechanisms connecting exposure to reduced reproduction remain unclear. Here, we examined the effects of imidacloprid, one of the most commonly used neonicotinoids, on singing in male zebra finches. Birds received sublethal doses of imidacloprid through drinking water over 30 days, followed by a 30-day washout. Using continuous acoustic monitoring and female-presentation assays, we quantified non-courtship and female-directed courtship song and assessed body mass, locomotion, non-vocal displays, and song structure. During the 30-day drinking-water exposure, imidacloprid reduced daily non-courtship singing, with effects persisting into washout.
items.author: dos Santos, E. B., Lee, J., Lee, S.-i. et al.

items.title: The impact of tail-cup handling as an alternative method for picking up laboratory mice
items.summary: The way that laboratory rodents are handled has a significant impact on their welfare. Picking up mice by the tail increases anxiety, reduces voluntary interaction with handlers, and reduces behavioural test reliability compared to more refined handling methods, such as picking up mice inside a handling tunnel or cupping freely on the hand. An alternative in use by the community is to restrain a mouse by the tail-base while scooping it up on the hand and supporting its weight (tail-cup method). Here, we assess whether tail-cup handling is a welfare refinement compared to picking up mice by tail or tunnel, using both sexes of two strains (BALB/c, C57BL/6).
items.author: Nolan, R., Leach, M., Rowe, C. et al.

items.title: Coordinated remodeling of NAD⁺ metabolic networks across the lifespan of Caenorhabditis elegans
items.summary: Changes in the metabolic network that sustain NAD+ during aging remain poorly understood. Analysis of steady state levels is insufficient to reveal whether biosynthetic or consumption pathways are perturbed or preserved. Here, we address this gap in understanding by integrating metabolomics, proteomics, gene-expression profiling, and stable-isotope tracing across the Caenorhabditis elegans adult lifespan. NAD abundance increases with age despite reductions in selected biosynthetic components. Tracing reveals reduced mid-adult incorporation of nicotinamide and nicotinic acid into NAD, alongside declining nicotinamide riboside abundance and loss of detectable nicotinic acid-derived labeling into this precursor. Early mitochondrial Complex I remodeling accompanies sustained changes in redox and energetic indices.
items.author: Alshaheeb, A. A., Yahia, M. S., Argento, I. A. et al.

items.title: Daphniphyllum macropodum genome assembly and multiplexed screening unveils alkaloid modifying enzymes
items.summary: Daphniphyllum macropodum, a small shrub or tree native to East Asia, produces bioactive polycyclic alkaloids of remarkable complexity and variety, making them long-standing, attractive targets for chemical synthesis. However, the biosynthetic origins of Daphniphyllum alkaloids remain unknown, and no pathway-associated enzymes have been identified to date. Here, we report the chromosome-level genome assembly of D. macropodum, representing the first genome assembly for the Daphniphyllaceae, a family in the Saxifragales woody clade. To discover alkaloid-modifying enzymes, we developed a highly combinatorial, multiplexed screening approach which enabled testing multiple enzyme candidates with multiple substrates in a single reaction. Deconvolution and characterisation identified two cytochrome P450 enzymes that catalyse the hydroxylation of the yuzurimine-type alkaloid daphhimalenine B.
items.author: Swamidatta, S. H., Radzikowska, B. A., Taylor, D. J. et al.

items.title: Visually guided analysis of single cell proteomics data with SCP-Viz
items.summary: Single cell proteomics (SCP) is a specialized, but expanding, field of research today. One of many challenges slowing SCP adoption is the inherent instability of the proteome and the changes that can occur before getting cells to a lab for preparation and analysis. Additionally, all current interpretation tools require experienced bioinformaticians to make the step from data to interpretation. Here, we present a visual toolkit that can accept SCP data from any instrument or common data processing algorithm. To demonstrate the capabilities of this tool we apply it to the analysis of dried digests of single human cancer cells following long room temperature storage.
items.author: Ruiz, S., Braswell, C., Orsburn, B.

items.title: Location of maximum bending stress in tapered hollow plants: A case study on Moso bamboo (Phyllostachys edulis)
items.summary: Many slender plants, such as trees and bamboo, have naturally tapered, axially graded forms to withstand wind loads; however, while trees feature solid cross-sections, bamboo culms are hollow. Although tapered hollow stems improve mechanical efficiency, the location at which the maximum bending stress develops remains unclear. As failure in such structures is driven by the bending-induced stress state, identifying this location is essential for understanding their structural capacities. This study aimed to (1) identify the location of the maximum bending stress of a tapered hollow beam made from an axially functionally graded material under various load profiles, (2) verify the consistency between linear and large deflection analyses, (3) investigate the effect of taper ratio on this location, and (4) apply the analysis to Moso bamboo (Phyllostachys edulis) as a case study.
items.author: Chalermsin, C. L., Tsugawa, S., Sato, M.

items.title: MetaboRx: R Shiny application for quality assessment and preprocessing of mass spectrometry-based metabolomics data
items.summary: Introduction Metabolomics datasets offer deep insights into biological systems, yet the multi-step analytical workflow, from sample preparation through instrumental analysis, introduces unwanted variation. This variation, including signal drift and batch effects can confound true biological signals. Although rigorous quality control (QC) and data preprocessing are prerequisites for downstream analysis, existing workflows are often fragmented, time-consuming, and inaccessible to non-experts. Objectives To develop a user-friendly software tool for rapid quality assessment and rigorous preprocessing of metabolomics feature tables. Methods MetaboRx is an R Shiny application that integrates orthogonal quality metrics into a single workflow, enabling systematic and transparent evaluation of metabolomics data before and after preprocessing.
items.author: Guppy, B. K., Merrill, R. A., Brown, R. F. et al.

items.title: TS-Zarr: a cloud-optimized Zarr layout for viewing and analyzing biomedical time series
items.summary: Background: Biomedical time series are recorded at high sampling rates for hours to days across tens to hundreds of channels. Each recording occupies gigabytes to terabytes of storage. FAIR data sharing requirements often place recordings in cloud storage. Visual analysis requires downsampling windows wider than a few seconds to the pixel width of the screen. Visualization tools therefore either read a local copy of the recording or query a dedicated resampling server in front of the data. Findings: We present TS-Zarr, a Zarr v3 layout for time series data. It stores the samples of each channel alongside a pyramid of summary statistics at progressively coarser levels.
items.author: Shah, R., Garai, S., De Freitas, D. D. et al.

items.title: Combined nelfinavir and cisplatin treatment promotes inflammatory signaling and immunogenic cell death in ovarian cancer cells
items.summary: Platinum (Pt) based chemotherapy remains central to ovarian cancer (OC) treatment, but recurrent disease frequently develops Pt resistance and responds poorly to immune checkpoint inhibitors. Immunogenic cell death (ICD) links tumor cell killing to antitumor immunity; however, cisplatin (CDDP), widely used in OC, is an incomplete ICD inducer. We previously demonstrated that the HIV protease inhibitor nelfinavir (NFV) enhances CDDP induced OC cell death and promotes a lytic, pyroptosis associated phenotype. Here, we investigated whether NFV enhances the immunogenic consequences of CDDP treatment. RNA seq analysis of OC cells treated with CDDP, NFV, or their combination revealed enrichment of interferon (IFN) associated, cytoplasmic DNA sensing, inflammatory chemokine, and antigen presentation pathways following NFV containing treatments.
items.author: Forgie, B., Ferrier, S., Goyeneche, A. A. et al.

items.title: Multiomic analysis of a pleural mesothelioma organoid biobank defines gene dependencies and therapeutic vulnerabilities
items.summary: Pleural mesothelioma (PM) remains an incurable cancer with few effective therapeutic options and limited understanding of its targetable dependencies, owing in part to a scarcity of clinically relevant, scalable models. Here, we describe establishment of an annotated biobank of 26 patient-derived PM organoids that faithfully recapitulate the clinical, genomic and histopathological landscapes of their parent tumours, including driver mutations, copy-number alterations and mutational signatures. By integrating these organoid models with a complementary collection of low-passage primary PM cell lines, we generate a functional precision oncology platform for PM. Genome-scale CRISPR-Cas9 screening across 23 patient-derived PM models uncovered 1,150 core fitness genes, including 638 not shared with pan-cancer core essentials, highlighting critical requirements for proteostasis, DNA repair, RNA processing and cell-cycle control.
items.author: Valer, J. A., Herranz-Ors, C., Arnedo-Pac, C. et al.

items.title: CD38-NAMPT-p21 signaling promotes stress adaptation in CLL
items.summary: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is the most common adult leukemia in the United States, accounting for ~30% of new diagnoses and ~4,000 deaths annually. High CD38 expression is a well-established marker of poor prognosis, yet the mechanistic basis of CD38-mediated treatment failure has remained incompletely understood. Here, we demonstrate that CD38 functions not merely as a prognostic biomarker but as a metabolic and signaling regulator that equips CLL cells to withstand cytotoxic and hypoxic stress. Using MEC-1 cells engineered to express CD38, we identified a CD38-NAMPT-p21 survival axis that confers resistance to fludarabine and hypoxia. CD38 NADase activity promoted NAMPT upregulation and AKT activation and was associated with accumulation of cytoplasmic p21.
items.author: HAN, B., Chini, C. C., CICCIO LOPEZ, G. et al.

items.title: CD3⁺CD4-CD8- (Double-Negative) T-cells Provide Inflammatory Signals That Influence Myeloid Cells and Enhance Survival in Glioblastoma
items.summary: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains resistant to immunotherapy, in part because of a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. While investigating the consequences of conventional T-cell depletion in a murine glioma model, we unexpectedly identified a population of double-negative T-cells (DNTs; CD3CD4-CD8-) that persisted following combined depletion of CD4 and CD8 T-cells. DNT enrichment was associated with significantly prolonged survival and revealed a distinct inflammatory transcriptional program characterized by activation-associated gene expression. Single-cell transcriptomic analyses demonstrated extensive remodeling of the glioma myeloid compartment, including enrichment of inflammatory signaling pathways and reduced expression of immunosuppressive markers. In complementary human studies, unmodified healthy donor-derived DNTs suppressed glioma stem cell viability, enhanced macrophage phagocytic activity, and reduced expression of the inhibitory myeloid receptor LAIR1.
items.author: McDonald, M. F., Patel, R., Tremblay, J. et al.

items.title: B7-H3 Orchestrates Fibro-Immune Spatial Organisation in Pancreatic Cancer
items.summary: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the most lethal cancers in the western world and is largely resistant to treatment. A major barrier to effective treatment is the highly desmoplastic and immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment, where the organisation of tumour, stromal and resident immune cells limit immune infiltration. B7-H3 (CD276) is an emerging immune checkpoint marker investigated in phase I and Ib/2 clinical trials in PDAC, yet its biological role within the tumour environment remains poorly understood. We performed an integrated multiscale spatial profiling study to map B7-H3 expression across regional and single-cell spatial contexts in treatment-naive resected human PDAC.
items.author: Legrini, A., Zhang, T., McGuigan, M.-C. et al.

items.title: Common early-life exposure of the colorectal epithelium to the microbiome-derived mutagen colibactin
items.summary: Colibactin is a mutagen produced by bacterial strains in the colorectal microbiomes of some healthy people. It generates somatic mutations characterised by the mutational signatures SBS88 and ID18 in normal human colorectal epithelial cells in vivo. Increasing prevalence of colibactin mutagenesis during the 20th century is hypothesised to have caused recent international increases in early-onset colorectal cancer incidence. Here, we establish the early-life prevalence, timing, mutation burdens and distribution through the colon of colibactin mutagenesis by sequencing normal colorectal epithelial cell genomes to detect SBS88 and ID18 in 90 healthy and inflammatory bowel disease affected children and adolescents. Colibactin-induced mutagenesis was present in ~43%, with or without inflammatory bowel disease.
items.author: Marshall, H. N., Pham, M. H., Jung, H. et al.

items.title: ARIPA: Agentic Reasoning for Image-based Pathology Analysis
items.summary: Nuclear segmentation across patient-derived organoids (PDOs) is complicated by differences in morphology, staining, image scale, and acquisition format. We present ARIPA, an automated human-in-the-loop (HITL) system that coordinates pre-trained segmentation tools through a vision-language model (VLM)-based agentic planning, verification, and refinement loop for hematoxylin and eosin images of formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded PDOs. In contrast to existing tools, ARIPA does not require training and achieves good performance. Tissue-aware tiling and image-derived calibration initialize segmentation; optional expert corrections guide configuration search and light-weight object-level rules without retraining or fine-tuning the pre-trained segmentation networks. We evaluated initial ARIPA predictions on more than 50,000 nuclei from 19 images of breast, head and neck, and lung patient-derived cancer PDOs, where nuclear segmentation was challenging due to its 3D structure and variation in imaging layers and malignant cell morphology.
items.author: Gu, Q., Xia, R., Doerfler, R. et al.

items.title: Morphological Changes and Mechanistic Analysis in Osteoblasts Induced by Long-Term Exposure to Radioactive Strontium
items.summary: Radioactive strontium-89 (89Sr) is preferentially deposited in bone tissue, where it directly interacts with osteoblasts; however, the morphological and molecular consequences of sustained 89Sr exposure remain poorly characterized. In this study, mouse pre-osteoblast MC3T3-E1 cells were induced to differentiate into osteoblasts and continuously exposed to 3.7 x 103 Bq/mL 89Sr for nine consecutive passages. Morphological alterations were monitored throughout the exposure period, and the cells were subjected to RNA transcriptomic sequencing, non-targeted GC/MS-based metabolomics, and non-targeted LC/MS-based lipidomics, followed by integrative bioinformatics analysis. Prolonged 89Srr exposure markedly enlarged the cell nuclei and increased the number of intracellular vesicles in osteoblasts.
items.author: gao, j., Wei, Z., Wu, Z. et al.

items.title: Integrating redox dynamics and gene networks reveals ROS-mediated control of Arabidopsis seed germination under water stress
items.summary: Seed germination is a critical step of plant development that is highly sensitive to water availability. During this delicate transition, water stress responses are tightly regulated by multilevel molecular networks that integrate environmental cues into developmental adaptations. Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) play a positive signaling role in seed germination, yet their influence on germination under water stress remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the involvement of ROS in Arabidopsis thaliana seed germination upon reproducibly reducing water potential using polyethylene glycol (PEG). The data show that delayed germination under water stress is not simply a consequence of reduced water uptake. Instead, water stress triggers coordinated reprogramming events characterized by altered H2O2 homeostasis, particularly in peroxisomes, which functionally mediates a rebalancing of ABA and GA metabolism toward developmental slowdown.
items.author: Bailly, C., Vidal, A., Wagner, S. et al.

items.title: Male bumblebees are capable of providing brood care and impacting nest development in incipient nests.
items.summary: Brood care is a core component of some social systems and a defining feature of eusocial insects. A recurring theme in eusocial Hymenoptera is that males are non-contributing members of social groups. Males are instead viewed solely as reproductives who leave their natal nest shortly after emergence to mate, then die thereafter. There is, however, some evidence across eusocial hymenopteran lineages that males do contribute to the nest. Here, we show that in the bumblebee Bombus impatiens , males incubate developing brood in lab-reared nests, and the presence of males positively contributes to nest development during the early nesting stage.
items.author: Moore ME, Woodard SH.

items.title: Dominance hierarchies are structured similarly in females and males across primate groups.
items.summary: Classic socioecological theory predicts that males and females experience different sources and mechanisms of social competition. Whether these differences translate into sex‑specific structural properties of dominance hierarchies remains unclear. Here, we compiled 156 dominance interaction matrices from 80 studies and extracted three commonly used metrics-hierarchy steepness, linearity and the directional consistency-to investigate the structural characteristics of male and female dominance hierarchies across primates. All three metrics were strongly affected by methodological and demographic variables. Steepness increased with the number of recorded interactions and group size, linearity decreased as matrices became sparser, and directional consistency declined with increasing numbers of interactions.
items.author: Spicher L, Huchard E, Lukas D.

items.title: Synthesis of C12-C18 fatty acid isobornyl esters and their plasticizing properties in PVC.
items.summary: Using camphene, C12-C18 fatty acids and titanium sulphate as raw materials, long-chain fatty acid isobornyl esters were synthesized. Tensile property tests, thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) were employed to investigate their plasticizing performance as plasticizers for polyvinyl chloride (PVC). The experimental results show that, compared with pure PVC, when the synthesized long-chain fatty acid isobornyl esters are applied as PVC plasticizers, the tensile strength of the material decreases. Most formulations exhibited improved elongation at break relative to the neat PVC matrix, while some samples showed no plasticizing effect, presenting obvious formulation-dependent characteristics. TGA results indicate that the prepared isobornyl esters volatilize prior to the thermal decomposition of PVC molecules, with a peak temperature difference of 40°C-50°C between the two, accompanied by partial decomposition of the isobornyl esters.
items.author: Qin R, Liu W, Wen R, Xie J, Meng Z.

items.title: Molecular structure aspects of 4,4'-oxydianiline and 4,4'-thiodianiline as corrosion inhibitors for carbon steel in 1 M HCl: an electrochemical and DFT investigation.
items.summary: This study investigates the corrosion inhibition performance of 4,4'-Oxydianiline (DDE) and 4,4'-Thiodianiline (DDS) on carbon steel in 1 M HCl using a combined electrochemical and theoretical approach. The primary idea of this work lies in its systematic, multi-level molecular structure analysis as the central framework for interpreting corrosion inhibition. Motivated by the need to understand how specific structural features govern inhibition behaviour, we conducted a comprehensive analysis integrating Hirshfeld, electrostatic potential (ESP) and natural bond orbital (NBO) atomic charge calculations, Fukui reactivity indices, NBO hybridization, frontier molecular orbital theory and molecular electrostatic potential mapping, complemented by potentiodynamic polarization, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and electrochemical frequency modulation measurements.
items.author: Al-Odail F, Bedair MA, Alkhalifah MA, Alqahtany FZ, Abuelela AM.

items.title: BeeHive: a flexible open electronics platform for controlling research equipment and teaching electronics principles.
items.summary: In this manuscript, we present BeeHive, a standardized, open-source hardware electronics ecosystem designed to address challenges faced by researchers when developing custom scientific equipment. BeeHive is flexible and interoperable, since it is organized around minimal design rules. It consists of a microcontroller-based main board and function-specific daughter boards (DBs) for controlling actuators or reading sensors, allowing researchers to rapidly combine and repurpose components to build complex, specialized systems. This modular approach significantly reduces the time and cost associated with instrumentation development, promoting effective collaboration through shared, standardized solutions. The platform's versatility is demonstrated across several neuroscience applications, including a reward delivery system for head-fixed mice, a modular mouse maze and an odour stimulator, alongside a dedicated training DB and curriculum designed to teach electronics and MicroPython programming in an integrated, project-based manner.
items.author: Sobianin I, Roald-Arbøl M, Ngotho SG, Ellison L, Riad IF, Al Balushi S, Carriero A, Spector MB, Vignal E, Perinetti CL, Eley M, Cozan M, Demirbatir C, Dominiak SE, Moubarak E, Janiak F, Kemenes G, Lagnado L, Schröder S, Nowotny T, King S, Baden T, Maravall M, Chagas AM.

items.title: In silico identification of marine natural products as potential ABCG2 ligands.
items.summary: Breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) is an ABC (ATP-binding cassette) superfamily transporter commonly associated with multidrug resistance (MDR) in cancer cells. Although no BCRP-targeted drug is currently approved, several candidates have undergone preclinical or clinical evaluation. Herein, a marine natural product (MNP) database was computationally screened to identify compounds with favourable binding to the BCRP/ABCG2. AutoDock Vina, OEDocking and AutoDock were first evaluated against experimentally derived ligand-BCRP binding information to establish a reliable docking protocol. Top-ranked MNPs were subsequently subjected to 200 ns molecular dynamics simulations and MM-GBSA binding-energy calculations. UMHMNP164176323, UMHMNP164176312, UMHMNP147769504 and UMHMNP114066501 showed more favourable predicted binding energies than BWQ/MZ29, with Δ G binding values of -128.1, -108.4, -89.7, -84.4 and -60.5 kcal mol -1 , respectively.
items.author: Abdelrahman AHM, Sidhom PA, Han Y, Tallima H, Shoeib T, Ibrahim KE, Ibrahim MAA.

items.title: Comparative genomics reveals contrasting candidate adaptive signatures in two ecologically similar plateau fishes.
items.summary: Plateau aquatic environments expose fishes to chronic cold, hypoxia, ultraviolet radiation and low productivity, providing natural systems for studying genomic features associated with environmental adaptation. Whether related fishes inhabiting similar cold-water plateau environments exhibit comparable or divergent genomic responses remains unclear. We compared two plateau cypriniform fishes, Aspiorhynchus laticeps and Diptychus maculatus , within a 12-species phylogenomic framework, integrating orthogroup inference, gene-family turnover, coding-sequence divergence, chromosome-scale synteny and duplicated gene-pair divergence profiling. The strongest contrasts occurred in species-specific orthogroups and gene-family turnover. Aspiorhynchus laticeps had a larger set of apparent species-specific orthogroups, enriched mainly in oocyte and reproductive processes, and its expanded families and elevated- ω orthogroups were associated with immune, receptor-mediated and membrane-associated functions.
items.author: Wang Y, Huang Y, Sun W, Zhang H, Matsui M.

items.title: Trade Policy Review: Peru
items.summary: The sixth review of the trade policies and practices of Peru takes place on 18 and 20 November 2026. The basis for the review is a report by the WTO Secretariat and a report by the Government of Peru.

items.title: Contact-induced molecular reorganisation in a model Escherichia coli lipid membrane.
items.summary: The nanoscale composition, molecular organisation and mechanics of biological membranes underpins their function for cellular compartmentalisation, signalling, and mechanical integrity. Eukaryotic membranes can readjust their molecular content and structural organisation in response to specific interactions or changes in their environment, including through the formation of more ordered and solid-like nanodomains - lipid rafts. Recent studies have shown that bacterial membranes also possess significant lipid diversity and can form functional microdomains reminiscent of eukaryotic lipid rafts, despite lacking sterols and sphingolipids. In all cases, the role of biochemical interactions between lipids has long been recognized as determinant for the membrane molecular organisation and physical properties.
items.author: Tormena N, Pilizota T, Voïtchovsky K.

items.title: Molecular mechanisms of deposit control additive inhibition by biofuels.
items.summary: Blending biofuels into gasoline can have several environmental and performance benefits. However, high ethanol concentrations are known to reduce the effectiveness of deposit control additives (DCAs) that operate by adsorption onto deposit surfaces. The fundamental physicochemical difference between fossil fuels and biofuels is that the former are mostly non-polar hydrocarbons, while the latter are predominantly oxygen-containing polar species. Here, we use molecular modelling to reveal how the presence of ethanol molecules affects the binding strength of three DCAs with markedly different chemistries to a model carbonaceous deposit from surrogate fuel blends. For a zwitterionic DCA, ethanol forms a structured solvation shell around the charged head-group, which reduces its adsorption free energy on the model deposits by around 75%.
items.author: Corral-Casas C, Gattinoni C, Brewer M, Smith A, Dini D, Ewen JP.

items.title: Matrix materials as functional enablers in metabolite sensing: from mechanistic demands to translational potential.
items.summary: The performance of metabolite sensors is strongly shaped by the physicochemical properties of the matrix that governs analyte transport, interfacial stability, and signal coupling, yet the role of the matrix has largely been overlooked, often being viewed as a passive support rather than an active design parameter. This review analyses how matrix architecture controls sensing behaviour across polymeric, inorganic, carbon-based, and supramolecular material classes, examining mechanistic trade-offs between diffusion and binding, conductivity and biocompatibility, and structural stability and responsiveness in the context of electrochemical, optical, and electrical transduction modes. Particular emphasis is placed on operation in complex biological media, where protein adsorption, ionic fluctuations, mechanical mismatch, and dynamic metabolite flux impose constraints rarely captured in buffered laboratory systems.
items.author: Varga M, Risi G, Stepanova S, Nasehi M, Bahtiyar C, Rousakis E, Witthauer L.

items.title: A mesoporous electrode strategy for probing ions at the electrode-electrolyte interface using in situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy.
items.summary: Electrolyte ions present at the electrode-electrolyte interface critically influence electrocatalytic reactions, yet direct, quantitative detection of interfacial ions under operating conditions remains challenging due to dominant bulk electrolyte signals. Here, we present an interface-sensitive soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) approach that enables quantitative tracking of interfacial ion behavior at electrified platinum (Pt) surfaces. Mesoporous Pt films with high surface-area-to-volume ratios were fabricated via soft-templated electrodeposition onto SiN x windows, strongly enhancing the relative contribution of the interfacial electrolyte within nanoscale pores while effectively attenuating signals from the bulk. Using Na + as a model cation, Na K-edge XAS measurements reveal pronounced dependencies of interfacial ion concentration on applied potential, electrolyte pH, and bulk concentration.
items.author: Rodriguez JSD, Larsson A, Deka N, Jorritsma R, Javed H, Kolmeijer K, Cuprija A, Liu W, Barber N, Squires AM, Teschner D, Ghafari A, Chuang CH, Mom RV.

items.title: First-principles prediction of the thermoelectric properties of Sn(S 0.2 Se 0.8 ) alloys.
items.summary: Thermoelectric power is an efficient and flexible technology for improving energy efficiency, but widespread applications require cost-effective and sustainable materials with a high figure of merit zT . Alloying is a common strategy for optimising zT , but predicting and understanding its impact on the material properties is made challenging by the structural disorder. In this work, we develop a practical and rigorous approach to predicting the zT of alloys, by combining first-principles electrical-transport and lattice thermal-conductivity calculations with approximate models for the electron and phonon scattering, and apply it to study the Sn(S 0.2 Se 0.8 ) alloy. We compare predictions obtained by averaging over the full set of unique configurations in a 32-atom supercell with those obtained from special quasi-random structure (SQS) structures with supercell sizes up to 256 atoms.

items.title: Optical Neural Networks Should Be Evaluated by Function, Not Only Physics
items.summary: Optical neural networks (ONNs) are attracting significant attention as alternative platforms for machine learning (ML). In an ONN, an optical module often takes over part of the computation inside a digital ML pipeline. How much of the task does the optical module itself perform, and how much does it contribute to any claimed system-level advantages, such as throughput or energy? This paper offers a simple, function-oriented evaluation methodology. Whatever its internal physics, the optical module appears to the surrounding digital pipeline as a mapping between real-valued tensors. We therefore evaluate it in three steps: (i) define its boundary in the pipeline, as real-valued tensors in and out; (ii) replace it with standard digital modules to identify those that match the optical system's performance on the same task and metric; and (iii) state system-level claims, such as speed or energy, per inference against the performance-matched digital module.
items.author: Shi-Yuan Ma, Xingjian Bai, Ryan Hamerly et al.

items.title: Retinal arterial velocity-proxy waveforms from differential spectral broadening in laser Doppler holography
items.summary: Laser Doppler holography (LDH) records pulsatile spectral broadening in retinal arteries. We compare vessel and local-background measurements to extract a signed differential-broadening waveform, $Δσ$. A minimal Gaussian convolution model motivates quadratic subtraction, and Doppler scaling relates the added width to a characteristic blood velocity. Real arteries show pulsatile waveforms, whereas identically processed imaginary arteries show only low-amplitude fluctuations around zero. We interpret the empirically scaled signal as a velocity proxy for waveform shape and within-vessel changes during a single acquisition under stable conditions.
items.author: Zacharie Auray, Yann Fischer, Olivier Martinache et al.

Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data. The agency event page has the map, updates and safety information.

items.title: Comment on "Exact, nonsingular black holes from a phantom DBI field as primordial dark matter"
items.summary: We demonstrate that the metric and scalar configuration proposed in Ref.~[1] do not satisfy the complete set of field equations of the Dirac-Born-Infeld (DBI) field theory minimally coupled to general relativity on a radial domain containing the event horizon. The physical DBI branch for this gravitational setup terminates outside the event horizon. Thus, the proposed configuration does not describe a black hole solution of that theory.
items.author: Mustapha Azreg-Aïnou, Marco A. A. de Paula

items.title: Cold Magnetized Quark Matter under Compact-Star Conditions
items.summary: We investigate the phase structure of cold magnetized two-flavor quark matter under compact-star conditions within a nonlocal chiral quark model with separable interactions. Electric charge neutrality and beta equilibrium are imposed in order to describe matter under realistic neutron-star conditions, while nonlocality is implemented through a Gaussian form factor. We find that low and moderate magnetic fields reduce the critical chemical potential for chiral symmetry restoration, signaling inverse magnetic catalysis. For stronger magnetic fields, the critical chemical potential becomes nearly independent of the magnetic field strength, Compared with the isospin-symmetric case, the combined effects of charge neutrality and beta equilibrium shift the first-order chiral transition to slightly higher chemical potentials, indicating that compact-star constraints delay the onset of chiral symmetry restoration.
items.author: S. A. Ferraris, J. P. Carlomagno, G. A. Contrera et al.

items.title: Fuzzy Dark Matter as a diffractive barrier: Wave-optics Signatures of Ultralight Fields on Lensed Gravitational Waves
items.summary: Gravitational waves (GWs) propagate through the universe from sources at high redshift, experiencing the gravitational fields of the intervening matter distribution. Halos composed of ultralight dark matter (ULDM) contain strong density fluctuations, reflecting the interference pattern in the field distribution of the ultralight bosons. In the wave-optics regime, ULDM fluctuations act as a diffractive grating, imprinting frequency-dependent modulations of GWs, in addition to magnification and other gravitational lensing effects. Since lensing depends on the projected surface density, we derive its approximate probability distribution and show how it departs from a Gaussian distribution depending on the halo profile and coherence length.
items.author: Manish Tamta, Han Gil Choi, Diego Blas et al.

items.title: Perspective on Proton Transversity Distribution Functions
items.summary: Using available information on proton tensor charges and constraints from perturbative quantum chromodynamics (QCD), Ansaetze are introduced for hadron-scale in-proton valence-quark transversity distributions functions (DFs). The concept of a QCD effective charge, which defines an evolution scheme for collinear parton distribution and fragmentation functions that is all-orders exact, is then used to deliver predictions for the $x$-dependence of these DFs at the scale $ζ_{2} = 2\,$GeV. Although the approach is largely algebraic, its predictions remain viable after comparisons with results obtained using computationally intensive methods. Thus, given the scarcity of data that can today be used for inference of proton transversity DFs, it may be worth using the results herein to inform and constrain related experiments and phenomenological fits.
items.author: Ke-Xin Zeng, Peng Cheng, Yang Yu et al.

items.title: Machine-learned acceleration of earthquake sequence simulations
items.summary: Earthquake sequence simulations involve slow interseismic processes and rapid dynamic ruptures. During interseismic periods, a numerical solver can take large time steps efficiently. During seismic periods, in contrast, the solver must drastically reduce the time step, and elastodynamic wave-mediated memory effects become significant; long-term simulations are therefore computationally expensive. We investigate the use of neural operators to accelerate earthquake sequence simulations. We train a Fourier neural operator (FNO) on data from high-fidelity, fully dynamic simulations to learn a jump map that advances the system state from before a seismic rupture to after it. We propose a hybrid modeling framework in which a conventional quasi-dynamic solver simulates the slow interseismic evolution, and the trained FNO replaces the solver during the computationally intensive seismic periods with wave-mediated inertial effects.
items.author: Reo Yanagi, Taeho Kim, Kaushik Bhattacharya et al.

items.title: NASA Launches Nuclear Power Systems Student Contest
items.summary: NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge kicked off Tuesday, Nov. 17. The science, engineering, technology, and mathematics (STEM) challenge invites kindergarten through 12th grade students in the United States to learn about space nuclear power systems and illustrate how these nuclear “batteries” could help power their lunar exploration vision. Students are also invited to write […]

items.title: Fe$^{2+}$:forsterite Qubit System
items.summary: Quantum Computing uses quantum mechanical phenomena, such as superposition and entanglement of quantum bits (qubits), to represent and manipulate information in multidimensional state spaces. This approach allows complex mathematical functions to be executed simultaneously rather than sequentially, making them much more efficient than classical computers. However, current quantum computers suffer from quantum decoherence, where small changes to their environment, such as thermal fluctuations and vibrations, affect the systems' fragile states. The goal of this study is to discuss the functionality of a proposed Fe$^{2+}$:forsterite qubit system by solving the unitary time-evolution of a quantum state vector for the system's Hamiltonian, using known axial and traverse anisotropy terms at temperatures up to 10 K.
items.author: Dishaanth S. Pillai, G. M. Wysin

items.title: NASA Space Apps Challenge Breaks Global Hackathon Records
items.summary: On Nov. 14 and 15, NASA held the annual Space Apps Challenge with a record-breaking 181,835 registered participants taking part in 593 events around the world. The annual hackathon invites participants to use NASA’s open data to address one of 14 challenges focused on space exploration or Earth science. This year, the hackathon drew 59% […]

items.title: Application of Pretrained Universal Machine Learning Force-Fields for Phase Transitions Prediction in ZrO2
items.summary: Pretrained universal machine-learning force fields can reduce the cost of finite-temperature molecular dynamics relative to density functional theory. However, most benchmarks test only static properties and do not assess whether these models reproduce the correct phase-transition sequence. Here, we benchmark ten open-source universal machine-learning force fields for zirconia (ZrO$_2$) using phonon dispersion calculations and variable-cell isothermal-isobaric molecular dynamics. Zirconia is a useful test because it has three thermodynamically stable crystalline phases prior to melting, following the sequence monoclinic-tetragonal-cubic. Four models reproduce this sequence: 7net-l3i5, MatterSim-v1.0.0-1M, MACE-mpa, and MACE-D3. Models with orthorhombic-tetragonal energy errors above about 10 meV/atom (7net-0, CHGNet, and MACE) instead produce an orthorhombic intermediate and predict monoclinic-orthorhombic-tetragonal-cubic-liquid upon heating.
items.author: Rajan Khadka, Axel van de Walle, Patrick Tepesch

items.title: The production of lepton pairs in heavy-ion collisions at SPS and RHIC energies
items.summary: We perform a quantitative study of dilepton production and elliptic flow in In+In collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=17.3$ GeV and isobar collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=200$ GeV, concentrating on the low and intermediate invariant mass regions. The medium evolution is simulated event-by-event with the multistage iEBE-MUSIC framework, and the electromagnetic emission combines for the first time quark-gluon plasma (QGP) emission calculated at next-to-leading order (NLO) in the strong coupling with in-medium radiation calculated with hadronic many-body theory. Freeze-out and surviving primordial $ρ$ decays are also included. The calculations are compared with the high-precision dimuon spectra measured by the NA60 Collaboration, and with STAR preliminary measurements of dielectron spectra and elliptic flow.

As NASA prepares for long-duration deep […]
