items.summary: A new album from NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory collects snapshots of baby stars across the galaxy and beyond and transforms that data into sound. Four new sonifications use data of stars that are actively forming, captured by Chandra and other NASA telescopes By studying places in the universe where stars are currently being born and […]

items.title: Quantum Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport in spacetime through spatiotemporal Kirkwood-Dirac distributions and spatiotemporal states
items.summary: Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport is a mathematical framework that determines the most efficient way to transform one probability distribution into another while minimizing a given cost function. Its central constructions include the Wasserstein distances, which quantify the space of probability distributions, and dual formulations that link to convex analysis. Its standard quantum generalization replaces probability distributions with density operators and cost function with positive semidefinite cost operator, which should be regarded as spatial quantum optimal transport. In this work, we propose the quantum optimal transport problem in spacetime through the spatiotemporal phase-space Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distribution and spatiotemporal states and through spatiotemporal state.
items.author: Zhian Jia

items.title: Folded out-of-time-order correlators in double-scaled SYK
items.summary: Harlow and Zhao arXiv:2607.14215 have identified ``anti-scrambling'' as a characteristic signature of cosmological horizons in de Sitter space, and proposed that it can be realized in a quantum system with bounded energy by Euclidean time ``folding" of out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs). We implement this prescription in the DSSYK model. We use arXiv:2303.03474 to define an infinite-temperature ($β=0$) DSSYK OTOC that in the semiclassical limit of small values of the double-scaling parameter $λ$ reproduces the usual AdS eikonal shockwave behavior with its characteristic time delay, and then apply the Harlow-Zhao fold with the ``fake'' DSSYK inverse temperature $β_f$ playing the role of $β$.
items.author: Joseph D. Lykken, Madeline Mooney, Maria Spiropulu

items.title: Dynamics of a spinning body with scalar multipoles
items.summary: We construct an effective worldline action for a spinning compact object in theories of gravity with massless, non-minimally coupled scalar fields. To this end, we generalize the standard skeletonized approach used in General Relativity to model the stress-energy tensor of a small body in a background spacetime, dressing its multipolar structure with the scalar field. Within a pole-dipole approximation, we derive a modified set of Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations of motion for the spinning body, together with the field equations for the scalar field and the metric. We consider both parity-even and parity-odd scalars. We tailor this formalism to model the evolution of asymmetric binaries, such as Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals (EMRIs), by systematically expanding the relevant equations in powers of the binary mass ratio and deriving the dynamics up to first post-adiabatic (1PA) order, along with the self-force equations needed to determine the particle's acceleration.
items.author: Jacopo Lestingi, Thomas P. Sotiriou, Andrew Spiers et al.

items.title: NASA to Cover 35th SpaceX Resupply Mission Space Station Departure
items.summary: NASA and its international partners are set to receive scientific research samples and hardware as a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft departs the International Space Station no earlier than Wednesday, Nov. 18, for its return to Earth. Pending weather conditions, the Dragon spacecraft will undock from the Harmony module’s space-facing port at 11:05 a.m. EST, following a […]
items.author: Lauren E. Low

items.title: ER=EPR and IMP wormholes in quantum gravity
items.summary: We analyze and refine the ER=EPR conjecture by studying IMP (Isenberg, Mazzeo and Pollack \cite{Isenberg:2001qe}) wormholes in QFT and quantum gravity, in the AdS/CFT context. IMP wormholes are solutions to the Einstein equations constructed from another general solution of Einstein's equations by gluing a handle on a Cauchy slice with a constant mean curvature, so that the initial data on the slice does not change in the regions away from the handle. This is made possible by using what is called the conformal method. This same method also enables one to recover a well defined perturbation theory in quantum gravity, and particularly for asymptotically AdS spacetimes \cite{Witten:2022xxp}.
items.author: Eyoab Bahiru

items.title: Twist-4 QCD Factorization for One-Point Correlators at Next-to-Leading Order in Electron-Ion Collisions
items.summary: Energy and charge correlators have emerged as powerful, infrared- and collinear-safe (IRC-safe) observables for probing QCD dynamics in the vacuum, established within the leading-twist factorization formalism. However, their IRC safety and factorization properties in a nuclear medium, where higher-twist contributions are critically enhanced, remain unproven. In this letter, we present the first proof of next-to-leading order QCD factorization for one-point energy and charge correlators (OPEC and OPCC) in electron-ion collisions at twist-4. Working within the higher-twist expansion framework, we calculate the twist-4 power corrections to the angular widths of the OPEC and OPCC, and explicitly demonstrate that the IRC singularities cancel and fragmentation-function dependence reduces to momentum and charge moments for final-state medium-enhanced observables in semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering.
items.author: Omar Elgedawy, Zhong-Bo Kang, Hongxi Xing

items.title: Scalar/axion Wormholes and Boundary Conditions in Gravitational Path Integrals
items.summary: Recent work noted that whether or not a given class of spacetime wormholes contributes to the gravitational path integral can depend strongly on the choice of boundary conditions. In particular, for asymptotically-AdS scalar/axion wormholes with spherical boundaries it was suggested that there are regimes where the same wormhole contributes to a Euclidean low-energy effective field theory computation of the partition function $Z_N$ defined by imposing Neumann boundary conditions on the scalar/axion field, while it fails to contribute to a corresponding partition function $Z_D$ defined by imposing Dirichlet boundary conditions on this field. Here we investigate toy models of related wormholes associated with JT gravity coupled to a scalar field, asymptotically-AdS gravity coupled to an axion/scalar with toroidal boundary conditions, and asymptotically flat gravity coupled to an axion/scalar.
items.author: Jason Hallsten, Jesse Held, Zhenyu Heng et al.

items.title: Capturing Ultralight Dark Matter Around Black Holes
items.summary: Ultralight dark matter (DM) can form hydrogen-like bound states around black holes (BHs), that can be perturbatively described at small gravitational fine-structure constant alpha=G*M*mu<<1, where M and mu are the masses of the BH and the DM scalar, respectively. We show that self-interactions lead to the formation of a 2p-halo around a Schwarzschild BH, with the final cloud density as high as 10^5 times the background density. We also show that for the case of a Kerr BH with a superradiant cloud, the decay of the 211 state can populate the ground state faster than it decays into the BH.
items.author: Salvatore Bottaro, Viktor Firsov, Gilad Perez et al.

items.title: Collective Superconducting-Qubit Interfaces for Microwave-to-Optical Quantum Transduction
items.summary: Microwave-to-optical quantum transduction is essential for connecting superconducting quantum processors through optical networks. Mechanically mediated transducers, however, remain limited by weak electromechanical coupling, dissipation, and added noise. In this work, we study a transducer in which an ensemble of superconducting qubits couples collectively to a shared optomechanical resonator. For weak signals, we show that ensemble size and optical pump strength together set the conversion efficiency, added noise, and bandwidth, with pump heating limiting efficiency to a finite optimal pump strength. Near half excitation, the collective coupling grows nearly linearly with ensemble size, accelerating transfer of an excitation into the mechanics.
items.author: Nicolas Dirnegger, Matthew Guibord, William Munizzi et al.

items.title: CFTs with Large Virasoro Primary Gaps
items.summary: We construct the first explicit examples of compact unitary bosonic full conformal field theories (CFTs) in two dimensions with a unique vacuum and an all-spin Virasoro-primary gap greater than two. Our constructions use asymmetric orbifolds of lattice CFTs built from even unimodular lattices of sufficiently large minimum norm, ensuring that no charged state lies below the desired gap. The gauged symmetries combine a common orthogonal action on the left- and right-moving currents with independent sign reversals; the latter project out the dimension-two scalar primary $\sum_i J_L^iJ_R^i$ that survives when the symmetry acts identically on both chiral halves. We prove that the gauging is anomaly-free and determine the exact gaps by analyzing the invariant untwisted spectrum and all twisted sectors.
items.author: Ziming Ji, Jiahua Tian

items.title: Ambient LLMs: Data-Efficient Supervised Fine-tuning via Temperature Matching
items.summary: Collecting large-scale, diverse, and high-quality post-training datasets for autoregressive language models is challenging. Consequently, Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) is typically applied to datasets significantly smaller than those used for pre-training, which leads to overfitting and the catastrophic forgetting of the tails of the data distribution. To prevent this collapse, we introduce Ambient SFT, a principled framework for leveraging imperfect predictions to augment the fine-tuning set. In our method, a "frozen" version of the pre-trained model serves as a noisy teacher that the fine-tuned model must match at a coarse level. In particular, we require that the high-temperature versions of the conditional distributions produced by the post-training model should match the high-temperature versions of the pre-training ones.
items.author: Giannis Daras, Marios Papachristou, Adam Klivans et al.

items.title: Spool: Low-Latency Streaming Inference for Hybrid Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Applications such as visual accessibility agents and robotics require answering questions about recent video content promptly, over a bounded window of past frames (e.g., the last two minutes). Hybrid vision-language models (VLMs), which interleave attention with linear recurrent layers such as Gated DeltaNet (GDN), are attractive for this setting, but maintaining a sliding window is expensive. The reason is that recurrent layers combine all past frames into a shared state, so expiring old frames normally requires re-running the entire window through the model. We observe that the recurrent update is affine in the state with input-dependent coefficients, so the effect of each frame can be captured as a transformation that composes associatively.
items.author: Rui Ning, Om Chabra, Hari Balakrishnan

items.title: Expressivity of two-dimensional Gaussian fermion tensor network states
items.summary: Tensor network states (TNS) provide a family of efficiently compressed approximations to physically relevant many-body quantum states. An important quantity that characterizes the computational resources required by a TNS is its bond dimension. While in one dimension an area law for the Renyi-0 entropy guarantees an exact matrix product state representation with a bond dimension independent of the system size, an analogous statement does not hold for general states in two dimensions (2D). This leaves open the question of how the expressivity of 2D TNS is related to the entanglement properties of the states they represent. In this work, we focus on two families of 2D translation-invariant Gaussian fermionic states: single-band BCS superconductors and half-filled two-band insulators (including semimetals).
items.author: Pok Man Tam, William Musk, Zhehao Dai

items.title: StringQFT: A Multiuse Textbook Resource for AI-Assisted Theoretical Physics
items.summary: We present StringQFT as a textbook collection for string constructions of quantum field theory and as infrastructure for AI-assisted theoretical physics. The collection comprises 18 volumes, 190 chapters and 3,795 pages, covering brane probes, brane webs, geometric engineering, F-theory constructions, wrapped M5-branes and exact worldsheet constructions. Its open-book benchmark inventory contains 1,073 items, including 499 with automatic finite-answer checking. For retrieval-augmented generation, it provides 1,371 section records linked to textbook sources and PDF locations, together with a local lexical retriever. Training-data preparation is illustrated by 21 private, source-linked examples. For agents, it exposes 19 calculation tools with specified inputs and finite domains, connecting tool use to textbook derivations.
items.author: Xingyang Yu

items.title: From nonlocal correlations to local symmetry breaking: Asymmetry dynamics of crosscap states
items.summary: Under unitary dynamics preserving a global symmetry, bipartite entanglement typically grows while an initially broken symmetry is locally restored. Here, we show that this conventional scenario can be reversed when symmetry-breaking coherence is initially encoded in long-range entanglement. We investigate this phenomenon in a family of charge deformed crosscap states, characterized by antipodal entangled pairs with tunable entanglement and symmetry breaking. We first characterize their static properties, finding a Page-like entanglement profile and an entanglement asymmetry that vanishes for subsystems smaller than half the system size, but grows logarithmically for larger subsystems. For symmetric subsystems, we also analyze the symmetry-resolved entanglement and investigate how it evolves as the subsystem is continuously deformed away from a symmetric partition.
items.author: Konstantinos Chalas, Pasquale Calabrese, Colin Rylands

items.title: An inexact stochastic variance-reduced gradient method for constrained convex finite-sum optimization
items.summary: In this paper, we study a class of constrained convex finite-sum optimization problems. In many practical applications, all or some of the constraints are hard constraints that represent imperative requirements. Consequently, any desirable approximate solution must (nearly) satisfy these constraints. Motivated by this, we focus on computing an $ε$-$surely\ feasible\ stochastic\ optimal$ ($ε$-SFSO) solution, in which the constraint violation is deterministically bounded by $ε$, and the expected optimality gap is at most $ε$. While a recently proposed stochastic variance-reduced first-order penalty method can compute an $ε$-SFSO solution, there remains a significant gap between its first-order oracle complexity for computing an $ε$-SFSO solution and that for computing an $ε$-$expected\ feasible\ stochastic\ optimal$ solution, where both the expected constraint violation and the expected optimality gap are bounded by $ε$.
items.author: Zhaosong Lu, Yifeng Xiao

items.title: Complete Cosmological Collider Signatures from Right-handed Neutrino Loops
items.summary: We study the complete cosmological collider (CC) signatures from right-handed neutrino loops with chemical-potential enhancement. These CC signals are induced by the inflaton-right-handed-neutrino interaction and can be extracted in the collinear squeezed configuration, which allows the right-handed-neutrino triangle loop to be factorized into the hard and soft parts. We precisely compute the soft part of the fermion loop for the first time by using the complete mode functions and the full loop integral, and treat the hard part as a tree-level subdiagram. We subtract the large-momentum asymptotic terms of the soft loop integrand and retain their finite contributions to the oscillation.
items.author: Linghao Song, Jingtao You, Ming Cheng et al.

items.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
items.summary: LLM agents increasingly drive their own learning. Self-improvement methods delegate various components of model optimization to the models themselves. As models become more capable, this motivates a basic question: do these increasingly capable models still need us to specify how they should self-improve? In this paper we study an autonomous paradigm in which, given basic primitives, resources, and a general goal for self-improvement, agents construct their own self-learning algorithm for context-based optimization. Using the setting of gameplay as a testbed, a frozen LLM agent is given a compute budget and tools for collecting experience and updating text documents, and allowed to freely experiment without an externally imposed loop or access to real-world data.
items.author: Shobhita Sundaram, Cansu Sancaktar, Phillip Isola

items.title: What Does a Bias Head Measure? Non-Identifiability in Head-Level Bias Attribution
items.summary: Methods that localise social bias in large language models to individual attention heads and remove it by ablation are validated by their effect on a fairness metric, never by evidence that the statistic selecting the heads measures bias. We audit this on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The head map correlates at $ρ= -0.950$ and $-0.768$ with a label-blind response-length map, apparently identifying a surface confound. An intervention that breaks the length-label coupling rejects this reading: with the prompt held fixed, response length explains 1% of the statistic's variance. What does explain it is prompt identity, at 64% of variance, in an ordering that is not monotonic in length.
items.author: S. M Seefat Alam

items.title: Higher-Scoring Coding Models Did Not Get More Work Done
items.summary: New coding models advertise themselves on score improvements of coding benchmarks. Yet no study has tested if a model that scores higher on these benchmarks gets more real work done. On June 12, 2026, a U.S. export control directive banned access to Claude Fable 5 for 19 days, which forced users to switch to other models. During this time, most former Fable 5 users switched to Opus 4.8 (11 points lower on SWE-Bench Pro compared to Fable 5). We treat this suspension as a natural experiment, where the people and projects stayed the same and only the model changed, so we could isolate the effect of Fable 5 on user productivity.
items.author: Yining Hua

items.title: Feedback-Linearised Trajectory Tracking via Model-Informed Robust Geometric DDPC
items.summary: Data-driven predictive control (DDPC) predicts system responses from recorded trajectories, but nonlinear dynamics can limit the accuracy of fixed linear predictors. This paper studies geometric robust DDPC for trajectory tracking of a fully actuated manipulator using model-based feedback linearisation. A mechanical model maps virtual acceleration commands into joint torques, while recorded data capture residual dynamics arising from imperfect model parameters. The controller minimises worst-case prediction error over an open Grassmannian ball centred at the fitted trajectory subspace. Simulations on a planar 2R manipulator under gravity compare the proposed method with double-integrator model predictive control (MPC) and direct regularised data-enabled predictive control (DeePC).
items.author: Pranav Gupta, Deepan Muthirayan, Ravi Banavar

items.title: Modeling quantum information scrambling in realistic protein NMR experiments
items.summary: Out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) are important probes of operator spreading and information scrambling, and have recently been proposed as a means of extracting molecular structural information through nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). Realizing this potential requires accurate modeling of OTOCs in complex molecular environments within experimentally relevant settings. Here, we develop an end-to-end computational pipeline connecting molecular structures to OTOC dynamics in protein systems. Our framework incorporates molecular motion through molecular dynamics simulations, orientational averaging appropriate for powder samples, and spin-network truncation, using an experimentally realizable double-quantum effective Hamiltonian. We apply this framework to a dataset of over 350 carbon-carbon spin pairs across 10 protein systems, spanning interspin distances of 5-17 A.
items.author: Alec F. White, Joseph Haslehurst, Daniel R. Moberg et al.

items.title: Multimodal Masked Diffusion Autoencoder for Modeling Impaired Driving
items.summary: Human cognitive state (e.g., distraction, stress), gaze, and behavior interact with the driving environment in subtle ways that AI could use to assist drivers, but ground-truth labels for human cognitive state levels are costly to obtain at scale. We propose a multimodal masked-diffusion autoencoder, ID-MAE, that adds a self-supervised objective to impairment prediction: alongside predicting the impairment label as a masked token, it reconstructs masked gaze and trajectory. To probe the effects of different modalities and types of impairments on model inference, we introduce DIVERT, a driving-simulator dataset containing 103 hours of driving data (n = 109) with ten impairment inductions spanning cognitive, visual, and emotional states, recorded with gaze, vehicle state, and scene video.
items.author: John Gideon, Anshul Gupta, Megan Applegate-Kenton et al.

items.title: Distortion-Free Semantic Watermarks for Black-Box Generative Models
items.summary: We present a provably distortion-free semantic watermarking algorithm that requires only black-box sampling access to a generative model and black-box access to a semantic embedding. A watermark is called distortion-free if, averaged over its secret detection key, it leaves the generator's output distribution unchanged; this provides a formal guarantee that watermarking does not reduce output quality. Conventional such watermarks are often brittle to transformations. This is especially problematic for images, where benign operations such as compression, cropping, or resizing change the entire pixel representation. Semantic watermarks therefore require detection to be robust to content-preserving transformations. Previous methods combining these properties rely heavily on specific white-box properties of the underlying model: either to autoregressive text generation or to diffusion-specific access, such as control of the initial noise or diffusion inversion.
items.author: Aviv Yossef, Or Patashnik, Or Zamir

items.title: Local interference algorithms for observables in large random circuits
items.summary: In quantum dynamics, it is generally believed that interference effects lead to a sign problem for classical Monte Carlo sampling methods, rendering sampling ineffective. In this paper we show that this is generically not the case for the task of simulating the evolution of observables in random instances of circuit dynamics. Specifically, we consider two examples of observables which give large signals despite the randomness of the dynamics: first order out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) in unstructured random circuits without conservation laws and time-ordered charge-charge correlators (TOCs) in particle number-preserving random circuits. We show that these observables can be approximated by classical stochastic processes and that these approximations can be systematically improved with a series expansion that incorporates coherent corrections associated with clusters of gates.
items.author: Philippe Suchsland, Brayden Ware, Vladislav D. Kurilovich et al.

items.title: Reading Scene States: Uncovering Safety Failures in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) can provide harmful assistance by interpreting visual events, even without an explicit request for the underlying harmful objective. We identify this \textbf{scene-state safety vulnerability} and introduce \textbf{SceneSafetyBench}, comprising 375 image--question pairs spanning Initial, Medium, and Ultimate scene states and five visual presentations. Across eight VLMs, scene-state inputs elicit harmful assistance with attack success rates (ASRs) of 45.6--72.3\%. Comparative analysis across three VLMs shows that scene-state inputs most closely resemble QR-related images in their layer-wise safety-related signal profiles, while exhibiting lower average late-layer readouts and distinct signal dynamics during generation. To turn this vulnerability into a systematic attack, we propose \textbf{S3TA}, which translates harmful objectives into scene states, queries image--question pairs independently, and assembles the responses.
items.author: Tongxi Wu, Yuyang Cheng, Jiacheng Xian et al.

items.title: Fine-Tuning Gemma 4 Edge Models for MATLAB Signal-Processing Code with SFT and QLoRA on a Laptop iGPU
items.summary: Small language models that run on a laptop are attractive for writing signal-processing code offline, but they make systematic errors on digital signal processing (DSP) conventions. We apply supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to the Gemma 4 edge models E2B and E4B with 66 checked examples covering 11 signal-processing MATLAB subtasks, using low-rank adaptation (LoRA) and quantized LoRA (QLoRA) on the integrated GPU (iGPU) of a laptop, and deploy the 8-bit integer (int8) models with the adapters through OpenVINO. On held-out variants scored by deterministic checkers, the pass rate rises from 18/66 to 37/66 (LoRA) and 37/66 (QLoRA) for E2B and from 32/66 to 47/66 for E4B (QLoRA).
items.author: Mehmet Altan Toksöz

items.title: Agent Trust Infrastructure (ATI): A Federated Identity, Trust, Attestation, and Accountability Architecture for Cross-Organization Autonomous AI Agents
items.summary: AI agents increasingly collaborate across organizational boundaries, invoking tools and interacting with agents operated by independent entities. Although existing agent frameworks support planning and coordination, they lack a common mechanism for verifying cross-organizational agent identity, execution integrity, and authorization. We propose the Agent Trust Infrastructure (ATI), a framework-independent security architecture built on Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA), and remote attestation. ATI establishes federated trust through peer organizational certificate authorities (AgentCAs), eliminating the need for a shared root authority. Before executing requests, ATI validates agent certificates, verifies approved model, tool, and system-prompt configurations, and enforces authorization through three policy checks.
items.author: Viet K. Nguyen, Mohammad I. Husain

items.title: A Universal Ratio Linking Cosmic Expansion and the Growth of Structure
items.summary: We identify a universal relation between the onset of cosmic acceleration ($z_t$) and the turnover ($z_{\rm pk}$) of the linear growth observable $fσ_{8}$. In a spatially flat $Λ$CDM Universe, these two redshifts obey $R \equiv (1+z_t)/(1+z_{\rm pk}) = 1.1596$, independent of the present matter fraction and the overall expansion and growth normalisations. This provides a new consistency test for $Λ$CDM, linking both background and growth dynamics. We further establish the conditions under which this extends to broader classes of dark energy and modified gravity theories.
items.author: Anjan A Sen, Purba Mukherjee

items.title: Learned versus Kinematic Trajectory Prediction under Reduced Observation Frequency
items.summary: Trajectory prediction models for automated driving are usually trained on data with a fixed sampling frequency, while positions received via vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication arrive at 1-10 Hz. We study whether a learned predictor that uses only the observation history keeps its advantage over constant velocity (CV) and constant acceleration (CA) models when the history frequency drops. On the Argoverse 2 motion forecasting dataset, the 5 s history of the focal agent was downsampled from 10 Hz to 5, 2, and 1 Hz, and the 6 s future was predicted without maps or neighboring agents. An LSTM-based recurrent neural network (RNN) trained for each frequency was compared with the same network trained at 10 Hz and applied to sparse histories after linear interpolation.
items.author: Nukhbala Gadzhiev, Alexander Morochko

items.title: Structure--Residual Inductive Biases for Language Model Pretraining
items.summary: Next-token prediction is relied upon to learn both predictive behavior and internal representations. We ask whether representation structure itself should be an explicit inductive bias. Motivated by the two-part coding view of Kolmogorov complexity, we study a structure--residual principle in which a representation separates structure from realization detail. We instantiate this principle in two complementary ways. Boundary Bottleneck Concept (BBC) routes information from token segments through boundary carriers while preserving local autoregressive computation. Continuous Concept (CC) regularizes representation geometry and induces a spectral decomposition into low-frequency structure and high-frequency residual. We derive coding bounds for both views and show that multiplicity-corrected boundary attention becomes exact as the within-segment path energy vanishes.
items.author: Hai Huang, Bartosz Żuk, Rassul Magauin et al.

items.title: Nonlinearity-preserving quantum simulation of flows in the early fault-tolerant regime
items.summary: Ensemble prediction of nonlinear dynamics propagates a probability density whose linear transport equation retains the nonlinear drift, but grid-dependent circuit costs leave end-to-end feasibility in early fault-tolerant quantum computing unresolved. We couple polynomial reduced-order models fitted by sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics to Walsh-synthesized Koopman-von Neumann (KvN) transport and surface-code resource estimation. At fixed model dimension and drift degree, per-step transport rotation counts scale polylogarithmically with cells per reduced coordinate. Balancing model accuracy against circuit costs makes reduced-model polynomial degree a design variable for early fault-tolerant quantum simulation. For a cylinder wake approaching saturation, preparation, propagation and sampling to 1% relative root-mean-square field error against the radial model are estimated to take 1.62 h on about 560,000 physical qubits.
items.author: Hansol Noh, Unam Oh, Sangkyu Baek et al.

items.title: Performance analysis of a Rydberg atom THz radiometer concept
items.summary: THz receiver technology lies between electronics and photonics; as such, its implementation is not as mature. This warrants investigation into alternative THz receivers such as Rydberg atom sensors, which are highly susceptible to electric fields. In particular, the conversion architecture has been demonstrated to coherently transduce thermal radiation. This system offers room-temperature operation and does not necessarily require a local oscillator at the frequency of the input signal. We provide an assessment of the feasibility of such sensors for THz radiometry within the context of Earth observation.
items.author: Richard J. Murchie, Petronilo Martin-Iglesias, Julian Hofmann et al.

items.title: WoRD: Diffusion-Based Posterior Inference for Online Goal Recognition
items.summary: Goal recognition is the task of inferring an agent's intended goal from its observed behavior. Most existing work focuses on high-level symbolic recognition, abstracting away the continuous motion through which agents reach their goal. Methods that do reason over continuous trajectories rely on an explicit dynamics model that is hard to acquire and rarely transfers across settings. Neither approach explicitly learns how agents move toward each candidate goal, limiting accuracy on ambiguous trajectory prefixes where such knowledge is most needed. We present WoRD (Waypoint Recognition with Diffusion), which uses a learned trajectory prior to infer the agent's goal from partial observations.
items.author: Almog Anschel, Sarah Keren

items.title: Quantum amplification with a linear quantum coupler
items.summary: Josephson parametric amplifiers (JPAs) are essential components for quantum-limited microwave measurement, but their dynamic range is often constrained by Kerr and other pump-induced nonlinear effects. In this work, we systematically study the performance of a parametric amplifier based on the linear inductive coupler (LINC). Starting from the driven-circuit Hamiltonian, we derive the effective three-wave-mixing amplifier model, including leading flux-driven nonlinear corrections relevant to realistic operation. We analyze the resulting gain response, saturation behavior, and intermodulation distortion, comparing them with representative state-of-the-art JPA designs. Our results show that the symmetry-protected structure of the LINC suppresses static Kerr nonlinearity. Moreover, suitable circuit-parameter optimization can further reduce the dressed-squeezing and driven-Kerr effects, leading to considerable improvements in power-handling metrics.
items.author: Changqing Wang, Yao Lu

items.title: Integral Tensor Isomorphism via Cubic Rings and Lattice Methods
items.summary: We prove that isomorphism of integral $2\times3\times3$ tensors under $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\times\mathrm{GL}_3(\mathbb{Z})\times\mathrm{GL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ is decidable in bounded-error quantum polynomial time. For a tensor $T=(A,B)$ with nonzero determinant form $\det(xA-yB)$, we use the parametrization of Wood by balanced modules to reduce the isomorphism problem to principality tests for compatible lattices, and use the algorithms of Bley, Hofmann, and Johnston to solve this in BQP. When the determinant form vanishes identically, we get either an integral $2\times2\times2$ core, or a polynomial kernel vector of degree one or two. The linear-kernel case yields another compatible lattice problem, while the quadratic-kernel case reduces to a fixed system of polynomial congruences and unimodular lifting.
items.author: Thomas Huffstutler

items.title: Effect of superplastic deformation on the intergranular corrosion resistance of austenitic steel 321 with different types of UFG structure: A case of homogeneous and heterogeneous microstructure obtained by ECAP
items.summary: The effects of superplasticity (SP) on the structure, hardness, and intergranular corrosion (IGC) resistance of UFG 321L steel are reported. By increasing the number of the ECAP cycles (N) and varying the ECAP temperature, and annealing temperature, the degree of the microstructural heterogeneity was changed. Regardless of the microstructural homogeneity degree, UFG steels demonstrated the possibility of realizing the SP effect at temperatures below the onset temperature of dynamic recrystallization. The dependence of ductility of the UFG steel on the test temperature is non-monotonic with a minimum at 450-600C. The maximum elongation to failure (~250%) was achieved at a SP temperature of 800C.
items.author: A. V. Nokhrin, V. I. Kopylov, M. K. Chegurov et al.

items.title: The Pfaffian sector of $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ BPS cohomology: brane excitations, triality and fortuity
items.summary: We study the classical $\frac{1}{16}$-BPS cohomology of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang-Mills theory with gauge group $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ in the BMN sector, including the operators built with one $ε$-tensor. These operators are odd under the reflection in $\mathrm{O}(2N)$, carry the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ charge of a D3-brane wrapped on $\mathbb{RP}^3\subset\mathbb{RP}^5$, and form the Pfaffian sector. For $\mathrm{SO}(8)$ we determine this sector through level $j=18$, where the level is twice the total charge of an operator. All but one of its $106$ $\mathrm{SU}(3)_R$ multiplets are products of trace gravitons and excited Pfaffians. The exception is a singlet, represented by the singlet projection of the rank-four member of a four-term family of $ε$-tensor operators.
items.author: Zheng Miao, Yuezhang Tang

items.title: An Effective Theory for Hot Lines
items.summary: We develop a high-temperature effective theory for spatial conformal line defects in theories with thermal screening. The defect partition function admits a local geometric expansion, whose leading terms describe the effective tension and bending response of the line. Using a convergent bulk OPE for heavy-state defect matrix elements, we derive asymptotic relations for averaged products of defect one-point coefficients and bulk OPE coefficients in the regime $1 \ll Δ_χ\ll Δ^{1/d}$. We compute the leading EFT coefficients for a twisted free scalar and for the magnetic line at the $\mathrm{O}(N)$ Wilson-Fisher fixed point, large-$N$ Gross--Neveu model and $\mathcal N = 2$ Chern-Simons-matter theory.
items.author: Julien Barrat, Alessio Miscioscia, Fedor K. Popov

items.title: Dynamics of a Single-Domain Dissipative Magnetic Gyroscope in Electric and Magnetic Fields
items.summary: We formulate the coupled spin--rotation dynamics of a single-domain symmetric top ferromagnetic needle (a magnetic gyroscope) in static magnetic and electric fields. The conservative Hamiltonian contains the rotational kinetic energy, the magnetocrystalline and shape anisotropy, the Zeeman energy, the electrostatic energy of the dipole induced in the conducting needle, the linear magnetoelectric coupling, and the relativistic motional (spin-orbit) coupling. Gilbert damping is introduced, and in an electric field, Debye relaxation of the induced electric dipole of the conducting needle also results in dissipation. We give the equations of motion in the laboratory and body-fixed frames, with singularity-free quaternion kinematics.
items.author: Y. B. Band, Igor Kuzmenko

items.title: NICER Status Updates
items.summary: November 17, 2026 NASA’s NICER Telescope Ends Science Operations After studying the universe for six and a half years beyond its initial mission, NASA’s NICER (Neutron star Interior Composition Explorer) telescope on the International Space Station has ended science operations. The mission and space station teams are now focused on plans to finalize NICER’s 8-year […]
items.author: Jeanette Kazmierczak

items.title: M 4.5 - 26 km NW of Port-Vila, Vanuatu
items.summary: A magnitude 4.5 earthquake was recorded 26 km NW of Port-Vila, Vanuatu. The event happened on 17 November 2026 at 18:15 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 10 km. items.author: USGS

items.title: Localized corrosion resistance of ultrafine-grained austenitic steel 321 obtained by Rotary Swaging: The role of annealing conditions
items.summary: The object of this study was austenitic steel 321, which has an ultrafine-grained (UFG) structure formed by Rotary Swaging (RS). RS leads to the formation of a two-phase macroscopically heterogeneous and, at the same time, a microscopically homogeneous UFG structure with an increased content of martensite. It has been shown that secondary TiC nanoparticles form in the annealing at 450-550C, the reverse transformation of martensite into austenite occurs at 550-650C, and recrystallization begins at 700C. Electrochemical studies of the resistance of the UFG steel to general corrosion, intergranular corrosion (IGC), and pitting corrosion (PC) have been carried out. It has been shown that the UFG steel after RS has a reduced IGC resistance.
items.author: A. V. Nokhrin, M. K. Chegurov, N. V. Melekhin et al.

items.title: Quantum simulation of neutral-meson mixing and decay on a reprogrammable photonic processor
items.summary: Neutral mesons oscillate into their antiparticles while decaying, so their dynamics is generated by a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian which a quantum simulator restricted to unitary operations cannot implement directly. We propose a reprogrammable photonic processor that simulates this open-system evolution through dilation and analyze it at the circuit level. The effective Hamiltonian is reconstructed exactly from measured lifetimes, mass and width differences, and the CP-violation parameter $|q/p|$. Through a singular-value decomposition and a single ancilla that encodes the total decay probability, its propagator is embedded in a four-mode unitary, which is compiled at each time step into a rectangular interferometer on a hexagonal mesh of tunable Mach-Zehnder units.
items.author: Mohd Abu Bakar Siddique, Abrar Al Shadid Abir, A. K. M. Rakib et al.

items.title: Capability Composition in Heterogeneous Teams via Barrier-Guided Diffusion Sampling
items.summary: The agents in a heterogeneous team can cooperate to accomplish tasks that exceed their individual capabilities. The team trajectories for a cooperative task can be generated by a generative model, provided that the model has been trained on demonstrations of the agents cooperating. Yet, demonstrations of cooperation are costly and may not exist for tasks that the team has never performed. The conditions under which the agents can combine their capabilities, however, are physical properties of the team and are known before any demonstration is collected. We encode the conditions as constraints on the team trajectories, and we enforce the constraints while sampling from generative models trained on demonstrations of each agent alone.
items.author: Diana Laura Morales, Ruoyu Lin, Magnus Egerstedt et al.

items.title: Bayesian Multimessenger Constraints on Self-Bound Quark Stars in Revised Perturbative QCD
items.summary: We perform a Bayesian multimessenger analysis of self-bound two-flavor $ud$ quark matter described by a thermodynamically consistent revised perturbative-QCD equation of state (EOS), incorporating the GW170817 tidal information, mass--radius measurements, and pulsar mass constraints. The resulting posterior medians and $68\%$ credible intervals are $B_0^{1/4}=137.66^{+1.72}_{-1.86}\,\mathrm{MeV}$, $M_{\max}=2.166^{+0.035}_{-0.036}\,M_\odot$, $R_{1.4}=11.778^{+0.203}_{-0.196}\,\mathrm{km}$, and $Λ_{1.4}=768^{+90}_{-81}$. The posterior-predictive support probability for interpreting the $2.59\,M_\odot$ GW190814 secondary as a self-bound $ud$ quark star is of order $10^{-5}$, strongly disfavoring this interpretation within the adopted EOS framework. The reconstructed EOS exhibits characteristic self-bound behavior, with finite energy and baryon number densities at the zero-pressure surface and a median surface energy density of $ε_{\rm surf}\simeq187\,\mathrm{MeV\,fm^{-3}}$.
items.author: Shu-Peng Wang, Ju-Xiang Li, Zhen-Yan Lu et al.

items.title: Electromagnetic form factors of the hidden-charm pentaquarks in a coupled-channel unitary approach
items.summary: We study the electromagnetic form factors of the hidden-charm pentaquarks $P_c(4312)$, $P_c(4440)$ and $P_c(4457)$ and of their four heavy-quark spin partners, treated as $\bar D^{(*)}Σ_c^{(*)}$ hadronic molecules. The states are poles of a coupled-channel unitary amplitude with a vector-meson exchange kernel that respects heavy-quark spin symmetry. The form factors are the residues at the double pole of the photon-coupled amplitude. The current consists of one-body currents and a photon--four-hadron vertex, which we construct for this channel space. Its gauged-kernel part ensures the charge normalization through the compositeness sum rule, while its contact parts contain couplings that the model does not determine.
items.author: Nongnapat Ponkhuha, Ratirat Suntharawirat, Daris Samart

items.title: TCP4D: A Unified Tool-Center-Point Tracking and Generation Model for Robot Manipulation
items.summary: Robot manipulation videos provide a rich visual experience, yet recovering robot action and gripper-state annotations from RGB observations still remains challenging. Using the embodiment-agnostic tool-center-point (TCP) pose as the action space, we present TCP4D, a unified model in which a shared 4D scene representation both tracks observed TCP motion and generates future TCP trajectories. Given a monocular video and initial 2D TCP queries, the tracker directly recovers metric TCP poses in SE(3) and gripper states alongside scene geometry and camera parameters. The generator samples local features from the same 4D representation along the recovered TCP tracks, then combines them with robot observations and language instructions to predict future TCP states.
items.author: Haosong Peng, Xiangyang Liu, Zhengshen Zhang et al.

items.title: Charge-transfer excitation drives cooperative phonon-assisted exciton self-trapping in NiPS$_3$
items.summary: Carrier self-trapping is a fundamental relaxation pathway in strongly correlated quantum materials, yet the microscopic lattice motions that drive it have remained largely inaccessible to direct observation. Here we investigate the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiPS$_3$ upon excitation across its ligand-to-metal charge-transfer gap, and reveal a nonequilibrium pathway that initially generates unbound carriers before they evolve into correlated excitonic states. Using ultrabroadband optical-pump terahertz-probe spectroscopy, we simultaneously track carrier localization and the associated lattice dynamics in real time. The transient conductive response quenches with a time constant of $\sim$109 fs and evolves into a localized exciton state, accompanied by pronounced renormalization of Ni-S optical phonons and the emergence of a transient 2.7 THz vibrational mode.
items.author: Long Cheng, Alexander Holm Ohrt, Oliver Nagy et al.

items.title: Analytic Two-Loop Classical Bremsstrahlung Amplitude in Electrodynamics
items.summary: We compute the leading long-wavelength term of the two-loop five-point amplitude for photon emission in the scattering of two massive spinless charges. Classical consistency suggests that two Coulomb exchanges dress the radiative tree amplitude. We show that this iteration accounts for the entire leading term and evaluate the resulting convolution. At fixed external transfer, the exchanges shift the momentum in the tree numerator, thereby changing the relative weights of its two polarization structures. We determine both coefficients at nonzero photon frequency and general relative velocity, with exact dependence on the spacetime dimension.
items.author: Xinguang Chen, Zhengwen Liu, Rourou Ma et al.

items.title: Pressure Drop: Gravity Vector Estimation from a Distributed Barometric Pressure Sensor Array
items.summary: While gravity is often used in mobile robotics as a global constraint for Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) algorithms, most estimation methods rely on indirect observation of the gravity vector. In this paper, we propose the use of altimeter measurements to directly observe the direction of the gravity vector. We provide a theoretical evaluation of the estimation noise and validate it through extensive experimental data, along with an evaluation of the impact of intersensor distance on our gravity vector estimates. Experimental results demonstrate that a median error of $0.87^\circ$ on the tilt estimation can be achieved with our system in semi-static scenarios.
items.author: William Dubois, Nicolas Lauzon, Johann Laconte et al.

items.title: Auditing a Learned Simulator for Legged Robots: The Robotic World Model on ANYmal D
items.summary: A legged robot can learn to walk inside a learned simulator: a neural network that predicts the robot's next state and is run forward on its own predictions. They are usually trained and checked one step ahead, although a policy uses them for a hundred steps or more. We audit one published system end to end, without a GPU: the dynamics model of the Robotic World Model (RWM) for the ANYmal D quadruped, and the uncertainty estimate of its follow-up, RWM-U. We rebuilt the model to match the released code's outputs, losses and gradients exactly, measured 101 trained simulators, 200 compressed copies and 38 simulators of three other architectures, and trained policies inside simulators that we tested in a hand-built MuJoCo model of the robot.
items.author: Joyjeet Singh

items.title: Convergence of the quasinormal-mode expansion of the Kerr Green function
items.summary: Black-hole ringdown is usually modeled as a linear superposition of quasinormal modes, and fits to gravitational-wave observations increasingly include high overtones. However, the overtone sum does not necessarily converge: overtones are more strongly damped and thus decay faster in time, but their amplitudes in the Green function (the signal at an observer produced by an impulse at a source point) grow, so the mode description may break down before a finite time. We show that for a rotating (Kerr) black hole this time has a clear geometric meaning. For highly damped modes, the amplitudes grow exponentially with the optical distance from the source and the observer to a characteristic "bounce" radius close to the black hole, defined as the location where the mode amplitude is smallest.
items.author: Davide Ciattaglia, Adrien Kuntz, Enrico Barausse

items.title: Zero mode surface of Hermitian two-by-two matrices
items.summary: We classify the zero mode surfaces, also called Clifford spectra, of Hermitian $2\times 2$ matrices. Using the covariance of the Dirac operator under the Euclidean group and its invariance under unitary conjugation, together with a singular value decomposition, every $m$-tuple of Hermitian $2\times 2$ matrices, after adjoining zero matrices if $m b_2+b_3$, of two topological spheres touching at one point if $b_1=b_2+b_3$, and of a single topological sphere if $b_1<b_2+b_3$. The topology is thus governed by the triangle inequality for $(b_1,b_2,b_3)$, which can be interpreted with Heron's formula. In particular, the Clifford spectrum of any tuple of Hermitian $2\times 2$ matrices is never empty.
items.author: Andreas Sykora

items.title: Probing Lorentz-violating electrodynamics with CMB polarization. II. Updated constraints and forecasts for the Simons Observatory and LiteBIRD
items.summary: We update the constraints on Lorentz-violating electrodynamics from the polarization of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). Within the minimal Standard Model Extension, we consider the renormalizable CPT-odd and CPT-even operators of the photon sector, which source cosmic birefringence and circular polarization, respectively. Combining Planck, Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) and South Pole Telescope (SPT) temperature and $E$-mode data with $B$-mode measurements from BICEP/Keck, SPT-3G D1 and SPTpol, we constrain the CPT-odd coefficients to $|k^{(3)}_{(V)00}|<7.75\times10^{-45}$ GeV and $|\mathbf{k_{AF}}|<3.82\times10^{-45}$ GeV at 95% credible level. These are the strongest bounds to date from any probe, and are driven by the SPT-3G D1 $B$-mode data.

items.title: Flavor-dependent quark-mass scaling and the fate of the strange-matter window in self-bound quark stars
items.summary: In the flavor-dependent QMDD model, self-bound $ud$ quark matter can be the ground state at vanishing pressure and convert into $uds$ matter through a first-order transition. So far the mass functional has used parameters $(a,C)$ common to all flavors; here we let the strange sector have its own coupling, $C_s=α\,C_{u,d}$, and map the response of the zero-pressure parameter space. The $e^0_{ud}=930\,$MeV boundary is independent of $α$ by construction, whereas increasing $α$ enlarges the self-bound $ud$ domain and pushes the $e^0_{ud}=e^0_{uds}$ line towards larger $a$. The causality boundary $c^0_s=c$ is almost frozen near $a\simeq5.5$. The competition closes the strange-matter window at \RA{$α_{\rm crit}\simeq1.136$}: above it every causal self-bound parametrization is $ud$ at zero pressure, so a first-order $ud\!\to\!uds$ transition must occur at higher pressure, though not necessarily inside a star, since the maximum mass may be reached below the transition density.

items.title: Frequency Multiplexing of Purcell-Enhanced Optically Coherent NV Centers
items.summary: Integrating optically coherent quantum emitters into nanophotonic structures is key to scalable quantum networks. Realizing them with nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond is hindered by the degradation of optical coherence accompanying nanofabrication. Here, we overcome this challenge by integrating multiple NV centers into a monolithic diamond photonic crystal nanocavity while preserving near-lifetime-limited optical coherence. We observe linewidths as narrow as 19 MHz, enabling the frequency multiplexing of spectrally distinct NV centers within a common cavity mode, while maintaining charge-state stability over several minutes under resonant excitation. Tuning the cavity into resonance with the NV zero-phonon line enhances the optical emission, consistent with Purcell enhancement predicted by finite-element simulations.
items.author: Alok Gokhale, Marco E. Stucki, Malo Bezard et al.

items.title: Spin and Orbital Angular Momentum Textures at Chiral Molecule-Metal Interfaces
items.summary: Chiral molecular adsorption can modify the spin and orbital character of metal surface states, providing an electronic-structure basis for interpreting spin-dependent interfacial phenomena. Using first-principles calculations with spin-orbit coupling, band unfolding, and an atom-projected orbital angular momentum (OAM) analysis, we investigate spin and OAM textures at chiral heptahelicene/Au(111) interfaces and compare them with clean Au (111) and an achiral coronene/Au system. Adsorption changes the orientations of the spin and OAM vectors and reduces the sampled OAM magnitudes of Au-derived surface states near the Fermi level. The two heptahelicene enantiomers exhibit textures related by mirror and time-reversal symmetries, whereas the comparison with coronene identifies changes that also occur without molecular chirality.
items.author: Gyanu P. Kafle, Amos Afugu, Zhen-Fei Liu

items.title: Imprints of Non-local Top-Higgs Interaction on Loop Induced Higgs Processes
items.summary: A composite Higgs arising from an underlying strong sector generally has non-local interactions with the elementary sector, formulated in terms of momentum-dependent form factors. We construct the minimal Ball-Chiu-type vertices consistent with gauge-invariant non-local $\bar{t}th$ couplings containing Wilson lines, where recursive Ward-Takahashi identities connect the Yukawa interaction to higher-order contact interactions. For a symmetric monopole form factor motivated by lowest-resonance dominance, we compute the top-loop contributions to $gg \to h$ and $h \to γγ$ amplitudes in closed form, and demonstrate a logarithmically enhanced deviation from the Standard Model. Current measurements at the LHC exclude the characteristic new physics scale below 3.6 TeV at $2σ$, while future colliders could extend the sensitivity to approximately 8 TeV.
items.author: Avik Banerjee, Rohan Pramanick, Tirtha Sankar Ray

items.title: Loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ at NLO+PS for LHC simulations: exact, fast scale and PDF event weights, theory uncertainties, and the limits of rescaled LO+PS
items.summary: We study loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ production with charged-lepton and neutrino $Z$ decays at next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD matched to parton showers, using public software at $\sqrt{s}=13$ and 13.6 TeV. An exact loop-amplitude cache reduces event-generation time by a factor of 26 with 450 scale and PDF weights, while Born suppression improves boosted-event statistics without changing the weighted prediction. We present inclusive results for both channels and charged-lepton differential and STXS Stage 1.3 predictions with theory uncertainties. At 13.6 TeV, fixed-order top-quark mass-scheme variations transferred to NLO+PS dominate the statistically precise central-Higgs STXS bins for $p_\mathrm{T}^V\ge150$ GeV, reaching 32-50%. An inclusive $K$ factor does not reproduce the boosted and jet-dependent NLO+PS spectra of the tested LO+PS samples, and the differences depend strongly on the shower prescription.
items.author: Licheng Zhang, Christopher Palmer

items.title: A Universal Axion in a Twin-QCD Sector
items.summary: Dark matter may consist of multiple components with distinct particle-physics origins. We investigate a scenario in which a universal axion couples to both visible and twin QCD, with twin baryons providing a possible dominant dark-matter component. The presence of a second strongly interacting sector can substantially enhance the axion mass while preserving its role in resolving the strong-CP problem, provided the physical vacuum angles are appropriately aligned. For a representative uniformly rescaled twin spectrum with a confinement scale five times that of ordinary QCD, the axion mass is enhanced by approximately a factor of 25. Using lattice-informed QCD results and a two-temperature description of the early universe, we investigate the cosmological evolution and relative abundances of the dark-sector components.
items.author: Stuart Raby, Scott Watson

items.title: Indentation of pre-tensioned cortex-like fibre networks: tension, local stretching and the signature of defect architecture
items.summary: Indentation is widely used to infer the mechanical state of biological materials like the actomyosin cortex. It reduces a single force-indentation curve to an apparent modulus. The cortex, however, is a pre-tensioned, heterogeneous fibre network. We show that this inference is ambiguous. The same amount of weakening can leave the indentation force unchanged or lower it tenfold, depending on where it lies relative to the probe. The force reflects how the probe couples to the tensioned, load-bearing structure, not the amount of weakening. We combine molecular dynamics simulations of a pressure-loaded, crosslinked fibre network indented by a rigid sphere with a continuum membrane solution.
items.author: Shubham Agarwal, Olivier Noël, Martin H. Müser

items.title: Variable-length MDI QKD under source imperfections and local randomization over horizontal links
items.summary: Quantum key distribution (QKD) provides security guarantees that hold despite device imperfections and finite-size effects. We address these challenges in measurement-device-independent (MDI) QKD, combining its intrinsic untrusted detection with an imperfection model for Alice's and Bob's sources via fidelity bounds. We establish variable-length general security under the Marginal-constrained Entropy Accumulation Theorem (MEAT), estimating the relevant Rényi entropies through conic optimization. We evaluate our model under a horizontal channel link, reporting secret keys for blocks as small as n~3x10^4 rounds under atmosphere-free conditions, and show that compensating for unequal channel attenuation through appropriately chosen transmitted amplitudes improves performance in asymmetric configurations, enabling communication distances beyond 80 km for commercial satellite systems.
items.author: Gabriele Staffieri, Martí Sales-Moragues, Carlos Pascual-García

items.title: Pair distribution function oscillations at electrostatically stabilized nanocrystal surfaces reflect nanocrystal lattice periodicity
items.summary: Nanocrystals (NCs) stabilized electrostatically by short, multivalent inorganic ligands exhibit rich interactions and phase behavior believed to hinge on the configuration of ions at the NC surface, yet these molecular details have not previously been measured. Here we use double-difference pair distribution functions (ddPDFs) of total X-ray scattering to determine the configuration of Sn$_2$S$_6^{4-}$ ligands on PbS NCs suspended in multivalent electrolyte. The measured ddPDFs exhibit a $\sim$3-$\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$ wavelength oscillation that extends $\sim$10 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$. Comparison with a PbS NC model decorated with Sn$_2$S$_6^{4-}$ ligands indicates ligands are aligned $\sim$radially, suggesting bidentate binding. Calculated partial PDFs show that the oscillatory signal is dominated by nanocrystal-Pb to ligand-Sn correlations.
items.author: Vivian R. K. Wall, Andrew Yang, Bryan A. Sanchez Monserrate et al.

items.title: Sobolev theory for the inverse problem of time-dependent density functional theory on the torus
items.summary: We show that, given a sufficiently regular time-dependent density, there exists a unique potential such that the Schrödinger equation with this external potential has the prescribed one-particle density. We treat densities that are twice differentiable in time and of finite Sobolev regularity in space; the resulting potentials are continuous in time and of finite Sobolev regularity in space. Our method of proof is to rewrite the problem as a nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a loss of derivatives, which we in turn handle with a completion-of-the-square argument. This is a refinement of our recent work [Lauritsen, Lewin, and Oldenburg, arXiv:2609.08984], which handled this loss of derivatives using the Cauchy-Kovalevskaya theorem and treated analytic-in-space densities and potentials.
items.author: Asbjørn Bækgaard Lauritsen, Mathieu Lewin, Jakob Oldenburg

items.title: Tunable Microresonator Arrays Induced by Geometric Phase
items.summary: Unlike periodic field-intensity patterns, which can be generated by interference of coherent beams, periodic material structures are usually created by periodic modification. In contrast, we show here that a millimeter-long bundle of four conventional side-coupled optical fibers with a slowly varying transverse arrangement can support a nearly periodic array of whispering-gallery-mode microresonators, whose period can be tuned mechanically down to about $100\,μ\mathrm{m}$.
items.author: M. Sumetsky

items.title: Temperature Flips the Sign of the Hydrogen Response in Nanogranular Palladium Networks
items.summary: In nanogranular palladium networks, hydrogen uptake has two opposing effects on electrical resistance. Absorbed hydrogen scatters electrons within the particles, raising their resistance, while particle expansion narrows the gaps between them and lowers the junction resistance. Such networks are widely studied as resistive hydrogen sensors, and the sign of their net response is usually treated as a fixed property of the architecture. In networks grown by atomic layer deposition on macroporous silicon, we show that changing the operating temperature can reverse this sign at a fixed hydrogen concentration. A thermodynamic model indicates that scattering contributes less as temperature rises, allowing sub-angstroem changes in gap width to dominate.
items.author: Niclas Alkazaz, Robert Zierold, Patrick Huber

items.title: Axion electrodynamics and the advection-diffusion structure of TEM modes in hollow-conductor waveguides
items.summary: We present a systematic investigation of transverse electromagnetic (TEM) modes in hollow-conductor waveguides filled with a dielectric medium described by axion electrodynamics. While such modes do not propagate in conventional single-conductor waveguides, the coupling of the axion field to an external magnetic field enables their propagation. We show that the resulting TEM modes are governed by an advection-diffusion-type equation for the transverse electrostatic potential, establishing a direct mathematical connection between axion electrodynamics and advection-diffusion phenomena. We illustrate this connection through explicit solutions and field profiles for cylindrical waveguides, considering uniform and rigid rotational drift fields, both individually and in combination, as well as different values of the parameter controlling the advection-to-diffusion ratio (Péclet number).
items.author: André H. Gomes

items.title: Oblique incidence and non-commuting limits: a remark on the convergence of Fresnel integrals
items.summary: The Gaussian integrals of quantum mechanics and of paraxial optics are oscillatory and only conditionally convergent. Textbooks usually make them converge by adding a small imaginary part to the time or by analytic continuation. We point out that the one-dimensional Fresnel integral converges by itself, while in two dimensions the result depends on the shape of the expanding domain: over squares it converges, over discs it oscillates for ever. The second case is the field of a uniformly excited plane of dipoles, which Feynman uses to explain the refractive index. Lai, Lau and Wong showed that at oblique incidence the integral converges and that normal incidence is recovered in the limit; we note that the two limits do not commute, and that this provides a transparent introduction to the regularization of the time-sliced path integral, where the ordering of the integrations in time plays the role of the physical prescription.
items.author: G. C. Reali

items.title: Dynamic functional connectivity reveals evolving neural activity states of alcohol-seeking in rats
items.summary: by Yujing Zhang, Nicholas M. Timme, Mintao Liu, Christopher C. Lapish, Joaquín Goñi The brain mechanisms underlying persistent alcohol-seeking in Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) remain incompletely understood. To investigate this behavior, we characterized the temporal evolution of neural activity states in the anterior cingulate cortex of freely behaving rats performing an aversion-resistant drinking (ARD) task. Alcohol-preferring (P) rats were assessed, as they reliably exhibit ARD when alcohol is devalued with the bitter tastant quinine. P rats were compared with Wistar rats, which progress slower to ARD, as indicated by cessation of drinking following quinine devaluation. Using dynamic functional connectivity analyses of spike-train recordings, we identified latent neural states corresponding to seeking and non-seeking phases.
items.author: Yujing Zhang, Nicholas M. Timme, Mintao Liu et al.

items.title: TopoPPI: A geometry-aware platform for visualization and low-distortion mapping of protein-protein interaction interfaces
items.summary: by Shuyu Zhong Protein–protein interfaces encode molecular recognition through spatially organized contacts, yet their buried, curved surfaces are difficult to inspect as a whole. Flattening these surfaces can expose interface organization but introduces geometric distortion and may divide individual residues into disconnected regions. We present TopoPPI, a geometry-aware platform that converts interaction surfaces into low-distortion two-dimensional atlases while retaining links to source atoms, residues and contacts. TopoPPI extends OptCuts with a contact-weighted penalty for seam-induced fragmentation of residue footprints—the surface regions assigned to individual residues—jointly balancing continuity, seam length and distortion. In a leakage-controlled benchmark of 2,236 experimental complexes, the geometry-only OptCuts foundation achieved 88.39% lower family-weighted scale-fair distortion than the next-best tested parameterization across 2,209 complete comparable outputs.
items.author: Shuyu Zhong

items.title: GapCNV: A comprehensive framework for CNV detection in low-input DNA sequencing data
items.summary: by Xuanxuan Yu, Fei Qin, Shiwei Liu, Noah J. Brown, Xiao Fan, Qing Lu, Guoshuai Cai, Jennifer L. Guler, Feifei Xiao Copy number variants (CNVs) are prevalent in both diploid and haploid genomes and contribute to genome evolution and phenotypic diversity. However, CNV detection in low-input data, including low-cell and single-cell sequencing data, remains challenging due to the shallow and highly uneven read counts and amplification bias. Another challenge lies in selecting reference samples, which are used to provide a baseline for defining copy-number losses or gains. Normalization using references containing common CNVs can lead to cancellation of true CNV signals or false CNV calls.
items.author: Xuanxuan Yu, Fei Qin, Shiwei Liu et al.

items.title: Hierarchical data-driven dynamical surrogate models of social decision-making
items.summary: by Manuel Brenner, Ismail Guennouni, Daniel Durstewitz, Stephanie N. L. Schmidt, Stefanie Lis, Peter Kirsch, Georgia Koppe Social decision making is inherently complex, shaped by dynamic trust building, biases, and adaptive strategies. Yet in laboratory settings, its study is often constrained by small datasets that nonetheless encode rich and sophisticated cognitive processes. This scarcity has historically limited modeling approaches to hand-tailored frameworks that embed strong priors about the underlying mechanisms. Recent advances in data-driven modeling of latent dynamical processes provide an alternative, extracting generative models directly from behavioral data without restrictive assumptions. Building on these methods, we derive hierarchical digital surrogates from sparse, non-Gaussian investment sequences in repeated trust games.
items.author: Manuel Brenner, Ismail Guennouni, Daniel Durstewitz et al.

items.title: A beam–membrane biomechanical vocal fold model incorporating posturing and glottal conformation
items.summary: by Mohamed A. Serry, Matías Zañartu, Sean D. Peterson The posture of the vocal folds produced by laryngeal muscle activation plays a central role in determining the dynamics of voice production. Abnormal vocal fold configurations are frequently associated with inefficient phonation and a variety of voice disorders. Although diverse glottal closure patterns have been observed clinically, the biomechanical mechanisms governing their dynamic behavior and resulting phonatory characteristics remain incompletely understood. Moreover, existing numerical models that incorporate the effects of the intrinsic musculature on posturing and glottal conformation are computationally expensive, which limits their suitability for large-scale parametric investigations. In this work, we introduce a computationally inexpensive vocal fold (VF) model wherein the body and cover VF layers are treated as a composite beam and a coupled membrane, respectively.
items.author: Mohamed A. Serry, Matías Zañartu, Sean D. Peterson

items.title: Exploring the potential of bile fluid dynamics analysis to inform clinical strategies for choledochal cysts: Experimental and numerical studies
items.summary: by Yidan Shang, Jiaying Liu, Wentao Sun, Renquan Tu, Xueren Li, Xiaojian Ni, Houbao Liu, Jiyuan Tu Surgical intervention is essential for choledochal cysts (CCs) due to their high lifetime risk of progressing to cholangiocarcinoma, yet management strategies vary worldwide. Given bile fluid’s vital role in digestion, investigating bile flow dynamics may provide surgeons with additional insights for treatment planning. In this study, one MRI-based healthy adult scan was used to reconstruct biliary system, which was then modified according to Todani classifications to generate eight CC types. Particle Image Velocimetry was used to first visualize local velocity field, followed by computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of bile emptying to analyze pathological non-Newtonian bile flow.
items.author: Yidan Shang, Jiaying Liu, Wentao Sun et al.

items.title: Ontology pre-training improves machine learning-based predictions for metabolites
items.summary: by Charlotte Tumescheit, Martin Glauer, Simon Flügel, Martin Larralde, Fabian Neuhaus, Till Mossakowski, Janna Hastings Deep learning has recently led to multiple breakthroughs in longstanding biological problems. Recent advances have shown that integration of expert knowledge can improve deep learning model predictive performance in complex domains such as biology. Bio-ontologies offer a rich source of curated biological knowledge that can be harnessed to this end. Here, we describe an intuitive and generalisable approach to embed the knowledge contained in a classification hierarchy derived from a bio-ontology into a deep learning model as an intermediate training step between general-purpose pre-training and task-specific fine-tuning: a process that we call’ontology pre-training’.
items.author: Charlotte Tumescheit, Martin Glauer, Simon Flügel et al.

items.title: Exploring the mechanism of oxfendazole in inhibiting osteosarcoma-induced osteolysis based on single-cell RNA seqsuencing
items.summary: by Jifeng Miao, Pintian Wang, Wenyu Feng, Haiyi Quan, Yunhua Lin, Gejin Wei, Fake Meng, Shanhang Li, Mingxiu Yang, Binyuan Ning, Jingxin Deng, Liang Xiong, Jianming Hu, Yun Liu, Qingjun Wei Osteosarcoma-associated osteolysis represents a major obstacle in the management of osteosarcoma. Within the osteolytic microenvironment, interactions between osteoclasts and tumor cells facilitate tumor proliferation and metastatic dissemination, and contribute to the development of pathological fractures. However, conventional osteoclast-targeting agents are insufficient to effectively suppress osteosarcoma-driven bone resorption. In this study, single-cell RNA sequencing was performed to identify critical regulators involved in osteoclast differentiation in the context of osteosarcoma. Using the Beyondcell platform, drugs targeting osteoclast-related signaling pathways were screened, and oxfendazole (OFN) was identified as a potential therapeutic candidate, with ANXA2 recognized as a key associated target.
items.author: Jifeng Miao, Pintian Wang, Wenyu Feng et al.
