items.title: CASTLE: Cell-type aware SpaTial domain detection via contrastive learning embedding
items.summary: by Lai Wei, Aoqi Xie, Yuehua Cui With advances in spatially resolved transcriptomics across platforms and resolutions, it is now possible to measure gene-expression profiles while preserving the tissue microenvironment. Spatial clustering is central to these analyses, and recent graph neural network (GNN)-based approaches have greatly improved their accuracy. Nevertheless, precisely delineating spatial domain boundaries remains a significant challenge. Here we present a novel method CASTLE (Cell-type Aware SpaTial domain detection via contrastive Learning Embedding), by leveraging cell type information for improved spatial domain detection. CASTLE first integrates spatial proximity to construct a spatial graph, refined from cell-type similarity or expression similarity when cell type information is unavailable.
items.author: Lai Wei, Aoqi Xie, Yuehua Cui

items.title: Phosphorylation-dependent LEF-6 promotes nuclear export of viral RNA polymerase transcripts to ensure the expression of viral very late genes
items.summary: by Xingyang Wang, Redaina, Tian Yang, Xinyu Zhu, Xiaofeng Wu The baculovirus late expression factor 6 (LEF-6) has long been considered as a regulator of late transcription. Our recent study found that knocking out the lef-6 gene in Bombyx mori nucleopolyhedrovirus (BmNPV) markedly down-regulates the expression of the polyhedrin gene ( polh ), but the specific regulatory mechanism remains unclear. Previous studies indicated that LEF-6 may be involved in viral mRNA nuclear export. Here, through a combination of RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq), and genetic approaches, we demonstrated that LEF-6 is crucial for the nuclear export of viral RNA polymerase mRNA, consequently affecting the transcriptional activity of very late genes, such as polh .
items.author: Xingyang Wang, Redaina, Tian Yang et al.

items.title: The complex landscape of multidrug resistance (MDR) in Zymoseptoria tritici : MFS1 promoter plasticity and beyond
items.summary: by Elza Neau, Simon Patry-Leclaire, Cécile Lorrain, Nicolas Lapalu, Anaïs Pitarch, Matéa Vencatasamy, Anne-Sophie Walker, Anaïs Lalève, Sabine Fillinger Multidrug resistance (MDR) in fungal pathogens poses a growing threat to fungicide efficacy and sustainable agriculture. In the wheat pathogen Zymoseptoria tritici , MDR is primarily linked to overexpression of the MFS1 transporter gene, driven by transposable element (TE) insertions in its promoter or their remnants. Here, we provide an extensive analysis of MFS1 promoter polymorphism and its phenotypic impact on MDR across 374 field isolates collected in Europe between 2020 and 2021. We identified six novel structural variants derived from diverse TE types, confirming that the MFS1 promoter undergoes recurrent and independent insertion events.
items.author: Elza Neau, Simon Patry-Leclaire, Cécile Lorrain et al.

items.title: c-di-AMP regulates virulence of Staphylococcus aureus via targeting the SarA-family regulator SarS
items.summary: by Haikun Wang, Qingying Fan, Huiqi Lin, Miao Yang, Huasen Wang, Heng Zhang, Lianying Mao, Lei Zhang Cyclic di-AMP (c-di-AMP) is a second messenger that plays a pivotal role in regulating many physiological processes in bacteria. The fluctuation in intracellular levels of c-di-AMP are often associated with virulence of many bacterial pathogens, but c-di-AMP receptors involved in virulence regulation and the underlying mechanisms are still largely unclear. Here, we report that the SarA-family virulence regulator SarS in Staphylococcus aureus is a c-di-AMP-responsive transcription factor. We show that c-di-AMP specifically binds to SarS at a ratio of 2:1. We further demonstrate that binding of c-di-AMP to SarS interferes with the binding of SarS to its target promoters, thereby downregulating the expression of the SarS-activated gene spa and upregulating the expression of SarS-repressed genes/operons such as hla , lukED , and lukSF-PV .
items.author: Haikun Wang, Qingying Fan, Huiqi Lin et al.

items.title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of human metapneumovirus and potential impact of respiratory syncytial virus interventions in the United States
items.summary: by Ke Li, Stephanie Perniciaro, Jiye Kwon, Nathan D. Grubaugh, Daniel M. Weinberger, Virginia E. Pitzer Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) causes acute lower respiratory infections, primarily affecting young children and older adults, with seasonal outbreaks peaking annually in March or April in the United States and other temperate regions in the Northern hemisphere. However, the factors driving HMPV seasonality in the United States remain poorly understood. We analyzed laboratory-confirmed HMPV cases and age-specific emergency department visits across 10 US regions, fitting an age-stratified dynamic transmission model to assess spatiotemporal patterns and investigate the influence of environmental variables and viral interference from RSV on HMPV transmission rates.
items.author: Ke Li, Stephanie Perniciaro, Jiye Kwon et al.

items.title: TMPRSS2 reduces antibody recognition of SARS-CoV-2 spike
items.summary: by Andrea Cottignies-Calamarte, Alejandro De Cruz, Cyril Planchais, Françoise Porrot, Daphné Rageot, Irène Misguich, Mateo Kryzpow, Martin Jungbauer-Groznica, Eva Thuillier, Amelie Wileveau, Isabelle Staropoli, Florence Guivel-Benhassine, Pierre Rosenbaum, Ignacio Fernández, Felix Rey, Julian Buschrieser, Sophie Trouillet-Assant, Hugo Mouquet, Olivier Schwartz, Timothée Bruel The serine protease TMPRSS2 acts as a cofactor for SARS-CoV-2 entry by cleaving the viral spike (S) to initiate fusion. Whether TMPRSS2 has an impact on humoral immune response against S remains poorly characterized. Here, we show that TMPRSS2 impairs antibody binding to S. In S-expressing and infected cells, TMPRSS2 decreases monoclonal antibody (mAb) and immune serum binding, as well as antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) induction.
items.author: Andrea Cottignies-Calamarte, Alejandro De Cruz, Cyril Planchais et al.

items.title: The zoonotic threat of simian arteriviruses: What do we know and what should we do?
items.summary: by Jared Compaleo, Scott Seitz, Makky Mousa-Makky, Jens H. Kuhn, Tony L. Goldberg, Cody J. Warren Simian arteriviruses ( Arteriviridae : Simarterivirinae ) are a diverse group of RNA viruses that naturally infect African nonhuman primates. Some of these viruses can cause severe disease with extremely high case-fatality rates following transmission to Asian macaques. Although human infections with simian arteriviruses have not yet been documented, increased vigilance is recommended. In this Pearl, we examine evidence relevant to evaluating the zoonotic risk of these viruses, including opportunities for human exposure, biological compatibility with human hosts, and gaps in surveillance and medical countermeasure development.
items.author: Jared Compaleo, Scott Seitz, Makky Mousa-Makky et al.

items.title: Cytolethal distending toxin promotes epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition by modulating AKT-dependent β-catenin Ser552 phosphorylation
items.summary: by Ruxue Jia, Lamia Azzi-Martin, Mariana Saraiva, Elodie Sifré, Christine Varon, Pierre Dubus, Armelle Ménard Bacterial genotoxins, Cytolethal Distending Toxin (CDT) and colibactin, cause DNA damage in intoxicated epithelial cells of the host. DNA damage influences β‑catenin signaling, altering its stability and nuclear translocation, potentially contributing to cancer development. Using non-transformed hepatocytes and cancer-derived intestinal and hepatic epithelial cell lines, we showed that CDT/CdtB induces the phosphorylation of β‑catenin at serine 552, along with the loss of β‑catenin from adherens junctions. This leads to the subsequent cytoplasmic accumulation and nuclear translocation of β‑catenin, ultimately driving TCF/LEF transcription, the crucial downstream event of Wnt/β‑catenin signaling, as well as the transcription of some β‑catenin target genes.
items.author: Ruxue Jia, Lamia Azzi-Martin, Mariana Saraiva et al.

items.title: Explainable machine learning audit of attribute rating relationships in Football Manager 2023
items.summary: by Zijian Zhang, Zhuyue Zhang, Lin Qiu Background Football Manager data contain simulated player attributes generated within a proprietary game environment. They can reveal relationships within the rating system but cannot establish real-world talent-identification validity. Objective To audit how baseline attributes predict an internal Football Manager 2023 (FM2023) rating threshold, compare four untuned models under repeated cross-validation, and examine model-specific attribute-contribution stability across categories and positions. Methods We analyzed 2,282 anonymized male player profiles aged 15–18 years. The outcome was an FM2023 overall score of at least 10. Logistic regression, random forest, radial support vector machine (SVM), and a single-hidden-layer neural network were evaluated with three repeats of stratified five-fold cross-validation.
items.author: Zijian Zhang, Zhuyue Zhang, Lin Qiu

items.title: An alcohol-solution combustion combining with gel calcination process for the preparation of Ni x Co y Cu (1-x-y) Fe 2 O 4 magnetic nanoparticles and their adsorption performances of Congo red from aqueous solution
items.summary: by Yidong Xie, Zhenghui Ge, Zhou Wang, Zhan-ao Wu Ni x Co y Cu (1-x-y) Fe 2 O 4 magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) were successfully prepared through a novel and economical strategy coupling alcohol solution combustion with gel calcination, and their physicochemical and magnetic performances were verified by XRD, TEM and VSM techniques. For larger specific surface area and saturation magnetization to apply, three key elements those affected the whole preparation process including element proportion, calcination temperature, and absolute alcohol amount, and different characterization technique were optimized, and for the adsorption of Congo red (CR) dye, Ni 0.1 Co 0.8 Cu 0.1 Fe 2 O 4 MNPs were fabricated under the conditions of 400 °C calcination for 2 hours with 65 mL absolute alcohol, the obtained product exhibited a uniform particle size of 18.9 nm and a saturation magnetization value of 76.4 emu/g.
items.author: Yidong Xie, Zhenghui Ge, Zhou Wang et al.

items.title: Perceived age-friendliness in multiethnic and multigenerational Klang Valley, Malaysia: An extended WHO Age-Friendly Cities assessment
items.summary: by Sin Meun How, Mohammad Mujaheed Hassan, Zalina Shari Malaysia’s transition towards an ageing society underscores the need for context-sensitive tools to assess urban age-friendliness, particularly in the multiethnic cities of the Global South. This quantitative cross-sectional study adapted and extended the World Health Organization’s Age-Friendly Cities framework by incorporating additional domains on technology and financial situation to assess perceived neighbourhood age-friendliness across six local authorities in Klang Valley, Malaysia. Incorporating a multigenerational perspective, the study captured perceptions from diverse age and ethnic populations. A bilingual self-administered questionnaire consisting of 15 socio-demographic items and 75 closed-ended age-friendly indicators measured on a 5-point Likert scale was administered to 511 community-dwelling adults aged 18 years and above.
items.author: Sin Meun How, Mohammad Mujaheed Hassan, Zalina Shari

items.title: Microbial community structure and functional gene profiles of drinking water treatment plant sludge in South Africa: An exploratory pilot study
items.summary: by Chimdi Mang Kalu, Memory Tekere Microbial characterization of drinking water treatment plant (DWTP) sludge helps inform sludge management strategies and supports the development of disposal policies and procedures. In South Africa, the microbial composition of DWTP sludge remains poorly documented. This study characterised the microbial communities and functional gene profiles in sludge samples collected from three DWTPs in Gauteng, Limpopo, and Mpumalanga. A shotgun metagenomic approach was employed to provide a broad assessment of microbial taxa and functional gene categories, while physicochemical analyses were conducted in an ISO/IEC 17025-accredited laboratory. Most measured physicochemical parameters complied with relevant standards, although elevated turbidity and ammonia concentrations were observed in samples from all three plants, and fluoride exceeded the guideline value in one plant.
items.author: Chimdi Mang Kalu, Memory Tekere

items.title: Prevalence of sarcopenia among community-dwelling older adults in an urban district in Penang, Malaysia and its associated factors
items.summary: by Sing Wei Low, Zhi Huang See, Norshahida Abdul Hamid, Winnie Ker Chien Oung, Yusnita Yusof, Ying Woei Chin, Azianey Yusof Abdullah Saari Background Sarcopenia refers to a progressive decline in skeletal muscle mass, strength, and physical performance that commonly occurs with ageing, and is associated with adverse outcomes such as frailty, disability, and mortality. Despite its growing public health importance in ageing populations, limited data are available on the prevalence of sarcopenia in Penang, Malaysia. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of sarcopenia and its associated factors among community-dwelling older adults in an urban district in Penang. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among community-dwelling adults aged 60 years and above in the Seberang Perai Utara district, Penang.
items.author: Sing Wei Low, Zhi Huang See, Norshahida Abdul Hamid et al.

items.title: Epidemiology of ventriculostomy-related infections after stroke and traumatic brain injury: A Vizient Database Study (2019–2024)
items.summary: by Abhijit V. Lele, Lilac V. Langaroodi, Alyssa H. Harris, Hannah R. Murphy, Samuel N. Blacker Background and Objectives To examine the prevalence and factors associated with ventriculostomy-related infection (VRI) in adults with acute ischemic stroke (AIS), spontaneous subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (s-ICH), and traumatic brain injury (TBI) across the United States. Methods In this retrospective cohort study, we analyzed patients with ventriculostomy admitted to 340 hospitals in the Vizient® Clinical Data Base (June 2019–May 2024). VRI was identified via ICD-10 codes for meningitis/device-related infection. Multivariable logistic regression identified patient- and hospital-level factors associated with VRI; hospitals with VRI rates ≥5% were classified as high-VRI.
items.author: Abhijit V. Lele, Lilac V. Langaroodi, Alyssa H. Harris et al.

items.title: Tailored isolation and metabolomic profiling of extracellular vesicles in Manila clam ( Ruditapes philippinarum ) hemolymph and insights into water-derived vesicles
items.summary: by Valentina Moccia, Giulia Dalla Rovere, Thi Tran Ngoc Minh, Andrea Zendrini, Marije Kleinjan, Marc C. Roelofs, Paola Berto, Claire M. Labrie, Tzviya Zeev-Ben-Mordehai, Esther A. Zaal, Paolo Bergese, Annalisa Radeghieri, Massimo Milan, Marca H. M. Wauben, Valentina Zappulli Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are evolutionarily conserved mediators of intercellular communication released by cells into biological fluids and the environment. Despite their increasing relevance in biomedical and veterinary research, knowledge of EVs in marine bivalves remains limited. This study first aimed to optimize protocols for EV isolation from the hemolymph of Manila clams (Ruditapes philippinarum) using density gradient ultracentrifugation (dgUC) or size exclusion chromatography (SEC).
items.author: Valentina Moccia, Giulia Dalla Rovere, Thi Tran Ngoc Minh et al.

items.title: Latent profiles of parental discipline in Singapore: Intergenerational patterns and links to adjustment in young adulthood
items.summary: by Hoi Shan Cheung, Elinor Lim, Kelly M. Y. Chan, Charlene S. L. Fu, Clarissa Choo Using a person-centered approach, this paper examined parental discipline profiles in Singapore from parents’ and young adults’ perspectives, and how these were linked to young adults’ adjustment. Two quantitative studies were conducted to explore parents’ experiences of disciplining their children (Study 1) and young adults’ experiences of receiving discipline (Study 2). Study 1 utilized the self-reported ISPCAN Child Abuse Screening Tool for Parents (ICAST-P) to document the frequency of use of 36 discipline methods. The ICAST-P was reworded for Study 2 to assess young adults’ experiences of being disciplined.
items.author: Hoi Shan Cheung, Elinor Lim, Kelly M. Y. Chan et al.

items.title: Cultural identity and behavioral participation: The role of Hakka landscapes in campus heritage education—A case study of a middle school in changting county
items.summary: by Jing Luo, Lan Yang, De-zheng Kong In the era of globalization, cultural landscapes are becoming increasingly vital for the transmission of cultural heritage. This study aims to investigate how campus landscapes embedded with cultural symbols are associated with students’ cultural identity and behavioral participation. We conducted an empirical study of 516 middle school students in Changting County using stratified convenience sampling and structural equation modeling (SEM). The research tests a conceptual model that progresses from Hakka cultural landscape perception, through cultural experience and identity, to cultural behavioral participation.
items.author: Jing Luo, Lan Yang, De-zheng Kong

items.title: Cyclic shear and damage evolution of pile–silty clay interface under CNL/CNS conditions
items.summary: by Shaoning Wang, Chien-Ta Chen To clarify the cyclic shear response and damage evolution mechanism of pile–silty clay interfaces, this study conducted a series of large-scale cyclic direct shear tests combined with numerical simulations to investigate the effects of interface texture width, soil moisture content, shear displacement amplitude, normal stress, and loading mode on the mechanical behavior of the interface. Two normal boundary conditions, including constant normal load (CNL) and constant normal stiffness (CNS), were considered. The cyclic shear stress–displacement hysteresis behavior, volumetric deformation characteristics, shear stiffness degradation, equivalent damping ratio evolution, and energy dissipation characteristics were analyzed. The results show that the interface shear strength follows the Mohr–Coulomb failure criterion.
items.author: Shaoning Wang, Chien-Ta Chen

items.title: Geotechnical assessment of the effects of blast-induced ground vibrations on structural integrity and open-pit slope stability
items.summary: by Ibrahim Ahmed Kanu, Mabinty Sarah Tholley, Arina Dmitrievna Smirnova, Wenbin Sun Blast-induced ground vibrations in surface mining threaten nearby structures and open-pit slope stability. At the Koidu Mine in Sierra Leone, evidence-based mitigation is needed to protect community infrastructure while preserving slope integrity. This study evaluates the effectiveness of trenching in reducing vibration transmission using numerical simulations in ANSYS LS-DYNA. Four trench depths (0, 10, 16, and 22 m) are assessed against a fixed blast depth of 15 m. The baseline no-trench scenario yielded a peak particle velocity (PPV) of 7.94 mm/s at the nearest surface structure (50 m from the blasthole), below the USBM RI 8507 limit of 12.7 mm/s but exceeding the stricter DIN 4150−3 guideline of 5 mm/s for sensitive structures.

items.title: Foreign-player origins in the Chinese Super League: Spatiotemporal patterns and origin-country characteristics associated with registration counts
items.summary: by Zijie Li, Maoteng Cheng, Fugao Jiang This study examined the spatiotemporal evolution of foreign-player origins in the Chinese Super League (CSL) from 2010 to 2024 and the associations between origin-country characteristics and foreign-player season registration counts. Longitudinal spatial analyses showed that CSL foreign-player origins extended across multiple continents, while registrations remained concentrated in a limited number of major origins. The spatial extent, weighted centre, and orientation of the origin distribution varied across seasons, but no persistent neighbouring spatial clustering was identified. Poisson pseudo-maximum likelihood regression analyses further showed that broader international destination reach and higher fee-weighted Hub values were positively associated with CSL registration counts.
items.author: Zijie Li, Maoteng Cheng, Fugao Jiang

items.title: "Pipe-Laying": A novel fusion of 3D MRI and health records for the early detection and diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease using deep learning
items.summary: by Arman Atalar, Nihat Adar, Savaş Okyay Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a prevalent form of dementia that impacts brain cells. Although its likelihood increases with age, there is no transitional period between its stages. In order to enhance diagnostic precision, physicians rely on clinical judgments derived from interpreting health data, considering demographics, clinical history, and laboratory results to detect AD at an early stage. While patient cognitive tests and demographic information are primarily presented in text, brain scan images are presented in graphic formats. Researchers typically use different classifiers for each data format and then merge the classifier outcomes to maximize classification accuracy and utilize all patient-related data for the final decision.
items.author: Arman Atalar, Nihat Adar, Savaş Okyay

items.title: Beyond the basics: Using nonlinear approaches to classical statistical tests to improve fit and interpretability
items.summary: by Timothy E. O’Brien, Jack W. Silcox Nonlinear models are less familiar to practitioners and can appear intimidating. However, nonlinear models often fit data better and, critically, may improve interpretability. Our previous work gave a simple introduction to nonlinear regression modeling, providing simple and straightforward examples and underscored the superiority of likelihood methods in obtaining confidence intervals. The current manuscript extends this introduction and shows how classic linear models — such as paired t-tests, analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), two-way ANOVA, and logistic regression — can benefit from using a nonlinear approach to fitting the data. Here we introduce, explore and discuss several of these approaches using important examples which highlight the benefits of the nonlinear methodology to the data analysis.
items.author: Timothy E. O’Brien, Jack W. Silcox

items.title: The utility and relative cost of using detection dogs compared to traditional methods for surveying small, cryptic mammals: A case study on the threatened Julia Creek dunnart, Sminthopsis douglasi
items.summary: by Emma L. Gray, Amanda Hancock, Ayesha Tulloch, Andrew M. Baker Accurate population monitoring is required to ensure timely conservation. However, it is often difficult to detect species that occur at low densities using traditional live-trapping survey methods, especially if they are small and/or cryptic. Here, we assessed the utility and cost efficiency of detection dogs as a rapid detection strategy by modelling a threatened Australian dasyurid marsupial, the Julia Creek dunnart ( Sminthopsis douglasi ). The detection dogs were systematically trained to discriminate the odour of S. douglasi from co-occurring small mammals and were able to detect the target species under controlled and natural field conditions.
items.author: Emma L. Gray, Amanda Hancock, Ayesha Tulloch et al.

items.title: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity and associated clinical, lifestyle and genetic factors among Ghanaian patients
items.summary: by Cyril E. K. Gavor-Kwashi, Oksana Ryabinina, Samuel Badu Nyarko, Naa Aku Addo, Joel Adu Twum, John Anyimadu, Vanessa Naa Torshie Mensah, Ebenezer Allotey Pappoe, Foster Kyei, Ansumana S. Bockarie, Richard Kojo Yankah, Ebenezer Aniakwa-Bonsu, Richmond Owusu Ateko, Dee Blackhurst, Nicholas Ekow Thomford Background Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (coexistence of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, metabolic syndrome and chronic kidney disease) is rising in sub‑Saharan Africa (SSA), but data integrating clinical, lifestyle and genetic determinants in Ghana are limited. This study aimed to characterise the burden of cardiometabolic multimorbidity among Ghanaian clinic attendees and evaluate the associations of clinical, lifestyle, and candidate genetic variants with hypertension, diabetes, metabolic syndrome, and CKD.
items.author: Cyril E. K. Gavor-Kwashi, Oksana Ryabinina, Samuel Badu Nyarko et al.

items.title: Machine learning for host-pathogen protein-protein interaction prediction: A tutorial paper
items.summary: by Jerry Emmanuel, Itunu Babatunmise, Jelili Oyelade The study of Host-Pathogen Protein-Protein Interactions (HP-PPIs) is critical for understanding mechanisms of infectious disease and for the development of therapeutic interventions. Computational prediction of HP-PPIs has become essential due to the limitations of experimental approaches, which are labour-intensive and expensive. In this tutorial, we present a step-by-step machine learning pipeline for HP-PPI prediction implemented in Google Colab. The workflow consists of six stages implemented in six Google Colab notebooks: dataset preparation, data preprocessing, feature extraction, machine learning model training, hyperparameter tuning and validation and model deployment. Six widely used classifiers, including LightGBM, Multi-layer Perceptron, Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, and XGBoost, were evaluated using balanced and imbalanced datasets from human-bacteria protein interactions.
items.author: Jerry Emmanuel, Itunu Babatunmise, Jelili Oyelade

items.title: Effects of latent feature construction and fusion strategies in deep multi-omics classification
items.summary: by Md Rayhan Khan, Masrafe Bin Hannan Siam, Md Fazla Elahe, Md Shohel Arman, S. M. Hasan Mahmud Identifying the specific subtypes of a disease is a critical step in personalizing medical treatment, yet combining the massive amounts of data from different biological layers remains a major challenge. While deep learning is great at distilling biological data into latent features, it remains to be seen if these simplified features are actually enough to represent the full complexity of a disease. In this study, we compared four distinct strategies using the BRCA and ROSMAP datasets: a View-Specific Stacked Generalization Ensemble, an End-to-End Multi-Input Deep Neural Network (Late Fusion), a Two-Stage Early Fusion Network, and our proposed Hybrid Latent-Original Feature Fusion Network.
items.author: Md Rayhan Khan, Masrafe Bin Hannan Siam, Md Fazla Elahe et al.

items.title: Correction: Self-organizing 3D human neural tissue derived from induced pluripotent stem cells recapitulate Alzheimer’s disease phenotypes
items.summary: by Waseem K. Raja, Alison E. Mungenast, Yuan-Ta Lin, Tak Ko, Fatema Abdurrob, Jinsoo Seo, Li-Huei Tsai
items.author: Waseem K. Raja, Alison E. Mungenast, Yuan-Ta Lin et al.

items.title: Individual differences in infants’ early home music environment are associated with later expressive vocabulary development outcomes
items.summary: by Talia Liu, Enikő Ladányi, Srishti Nayak, Noah R. Fram, Catherine T. Bush, Tiffany G. Woynaroski, Jennifer Zuk, Miriam Lense, Reyna L. Gordon Informal music experiences and engagement (e.g., parent-child singing activities) are common in infancy and early childhood. However, the specific role of the early home music environment in fostering infants’ development remains understudied. Recent theories and empirical evidence demonstrate shared biology between music and language processing, as well as overlapping acoustic characteristics of speech and song. Emerging yet limited work has established positive links between infants’ early home music environments and their later receptive vocabulary development. Here, we assessed whether infants’ home music environment is a significant unique predictor of infants’ expressive vocabulary development, an established early marker of children’s language outcomes.
items.author: Talia Liu, Enikő Ladányi, Srishti Nayak et al.

items.title: Transoral ultrasound added to the physical examination for suspected peritonsillar abscess – A research protocol for a multicenter cluster randomized trial
items.summary: by Amalie Hartvig Pall Posselt, Martin Garset-Zamani, Gitte Bjørn Hvilsom, Kasper Wennervaldt, Morten Matthiesen Bach Damm, Trine Nybo Ranneries, Michael F. Howitz, Thomas Kjærgaard, Tobias Todsen Introduction Peritonsillar abscess (PTA) is one of the most frequent deep neck infections that requires urgent evaluation. Distinguishing PTA from peritonsillar cellulitis (PTC) on physical examination alone is challenging, yet clinically important, as PTA is treated with surgical drainage, whereas PTC is managed with antibiotics alone. Transoral ultrasound is a promising diagnostic adjunct that may improve clinicians’ ability to differentiate between these conditions, but current evidence supporting its routine use remains limited. Objective This clinical trial examines whether the use of transoral ultrasound, as an extension of the clinical examination, improves diagnostic accuracy and treatment in patients suspected of a peritonsillar abscess.
items.author: Amalie Hartvig Pall Posselt, Martin Garset-Zamani, Gitte Bjørn Hvilsom et al.

items.title: Paint: Accurate, efficient, and sparse Model Inversion via peripheral sparsification and anchor alignment
items.summary: by Jaehyeon Choi, Minjun Kim, U Kang How can we reconstruct training data from a pre-trained model without access to the original dataset? Model Inversion (MI) attempts to synthesize samples similar to the training dataset. This capability is particularly useful in data-free applications, such as data-free quantization and data-free knowledge transfer, where synthetic data replace inaccessible training samples. For these applications, MI needs to generate high-fidelity samples to preserve semantic information while remaining computationally efficient, enabling scalable generation for reliable downstream performance. However, existing MI methods fail to achieve both high fidelity and efficiency simultaneously. In this paper, we propose Paint (Peripheral sparsification and Anchor-aligned INversion Technique), an accurate, efficient, and sparse MI framework for generating high-fidelity synthetic data.
items.author: Jaehyeon Choi, Minjun Kim, U Kang

items.title: Molecular surveillance of resistance mutations in Plasmodium vivax clinical samples from southwestern India
items.summary: by Vishnu Teja Nallapati, A. R. Manoj, Sushma Belurkar, Naveenchandra Kulal, Prashanth Bhat, Nitin Gupta, Manjunath H. Hande, Kavitha Saravu Plasmodium vivax is a major cause of malaria in India, especially in the southwest, where chloroquine (CQ) followed by 14-day primaquine is the recommended treatment; however, antimalarial drug resistance poses a significant threat, prompting this study to investigate the molecular epidemiology of drug resistance in vivax malaria clinical samples from southwestern India. A total of 93 P. vivax malaria samples were collected from symptomatic adult patients at three sites in two districts: Kasturba Medical College, Manipal (13/07/2021–30/09/2024), Udupi District Hospital (07/07/2022–30/09/2024), and the Malaria Clinic, Mangaluru District Hospital (07/07/2022–30/09/2024).
items.author: Vishnu Teja Nallapati, A. R. Manoj, Sushma Belurkar et al.

items.title: Genome-wide SNP analysis reveals genetic diversity and population structure in Ethiopian naked barley ( Hordeum vulgare L. var. nudum )
items.summary: by Tesfaye Woldesemayate Woldetsadik, Tileye Feyissa, Tilahun Mekonnen, Alemayehu Teressa Negawo, Basazen Fantahun Lakew Ethiopian naked barley ( Hordeum vulgare L. var. nudum ) represents a vital traditional cereal crop adapted to diverse and challenging highland agroecologies. Despite its agronomic and nutritional significance, high-density, genome-wide genetic characterization of this germ plasm remains limited. Therefore, the objective of this study was to investigate the genetic diversity, population structure, admixture patterns, and genomic differentiation of Ethiopian naked barley accessions. We used 222 lines and 8,072 high-quality single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) markers spanning chromosomes 1H–7H and unanchored genomic regions. Diversity parameters, including minor allele frequency (MAF), expected heterozygosity (He), and polymorphic information content (PIC), were evaluated.
items.author: Tesfaye Woldesemayate Woldetsadik, Tileye Feyissa, Tilahun Mekonnen et al.

items.title: Age as a determinant of trampoline-related oral-facial-head injuries in pediatric emergency department visits: A NEISS analysis
items.summary: by R. Constance Wiener, Christopher Waters Over the last decade trampoline use has increased. Many injuries occur that require emergency department (ED) care. The purpose of this research is to examine the role of age in trampoline-related oral-facial-head injuries that require ED care. Data from the 2024 National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS) was used. Trampoline-related injuries were extracted from the data set. Oral-facial-head trampoline-related injuries were compared with other types of trampoline-related injuries by age groups (0 to p = 0.0155] compared with children ages 12 to ≤18 years for oral-facial-head trampoline-related injuries as compared with other injuries from trampolines.
items.author: R. Constance Wiener, Christopher Waters

items.title: Beyond generalizations: Understanding adolescent social networks in American Indian communities
items.summary: by Shuwen Zhang, Michael D. Siciliano, Nancy Rumbaugh Whitesell, Katie Schultz, Jerreed D. Ivanich American Indian (AI) adolescents experience disproportionately high rates of substance use, yet the role of substance use and other individual characteristics in friendship network formation within AI-majority reservation schools remains understudied. Most existing research on adolescent networks derives from racially heterogeneous school settings, where substance use is often linked to friendship formation and popularity. This study examines the structural and relational foundations of friendship networks among AI adolescents in their unique cultural context. Using social network data from 9th and 10th-grade students (N = 247) across three schools on a Northern Plains reservation, we employed exponential random graph models (ERGMs) to analyze factors shaping friendship ties.
items.author: Shuwen Zhang, Michael D. Siciliano, Nancy Rumbaugh Whitesell et al.

items.title: Revisiting structured-light propagation in screw-dislocation geometries: Landau dynamics and gradient-induced polarization textures
items.summary: We derive the propagation of finite electromagnetic beams in the effective metric of a continuous distribution of screw dislocations from gauge-invariant, minimally coupled Maxwell theory with $F=dA$. The Burgers flux fixes the metric profile through $σ(ρ)=f'(ρ)/(bρ)$, which separates true density gradients from coordinate factors. In geometric optics, both polarizations share one light cone, and a uniform density rotates the polarization uniformly relative to the geometry-adapted frame; laboratory polarimetry also requires matching at the interfaces. At leading paraxial order, the orbital motion is of Landau type, with a closed propagator for arbitrary inputs, and for a uniform density the polarization evolution factorizes exactly.
items.author: Edilberto O. Silva

items.title: Altermagnetism-induced magneto-optical effects
items.summary: Altermagnets break time-reversal symmetry despite their zero net magnetization, enabling time-reversal-odd responses while retaining the advantages of antiferromagnets. However, magneto-optical (MO) effects are not universal among altermagnets because MO effects typically arise from magnetic dipole order (ferromagnetism), which is generally absent in altermagnets. In this work, we address this limitation by establishing octupolar MO effects, which arise from magnetic octupole order through spatial dispersion. Owing to this distinct origin, octupolar MO effects do not necessarily require spin-orbit coupling even in collinear magnets and can arise without an external magnetic field in antiferromagnets where conventional MO effects are symmetry-forbidden. Such antiferromagnets include $d$-wave altermagnets such as RuO$_2$ and KV$_2$Se$_2$O, certain $g$- and $i$-wave altermagnets, including CrSb, as well as noncoplanar antiferromagnets such as MnTe$_2$ and pyrochlore iridates with all-in-all-out magnetic order.
items.author: Jun Ōiké, Robert Peters, Koki Shinada

items.title: Thermal and Acoustic Measurements of Hybrid Bonding Stacks
items.summary: Thermal and structural characterizations of hybrid bonding structures are essential for understanding heat transport in three-dimensional integrated circuits (3D-ICs). In this work, we investigate the effective thermal conductivity of the Cu/dielectric HB layer using time-domain thermoreflectance (TDTR) combined with picosecond ultrasonic technique. Shallow-angle polishing enabled depth-resolved thermal measurements by exposing hybrid bonding layers with different remaining thicknesses, while acoustic echoes were used to identify buried interfaces and determine the thickness. The distinct waveform of the bonding interface echo compared with the Cu/dielectric interface echo suggests that its acoustic response may also reflect the interfacial bonding conditions. The extracted thermal conductivity ranges from 1.14 to 1.75 Wm-1K-1 for the bottom pad layer and from 1.76 to 4.34 Wm-1K-1 for the top pad layer.
items.author: Zirou Chen, Xinyan Xu, Zifeng Huang et al.

items.title: Development and Validation of a preCICE Based OpenMOC OpenFOAM Coupling Framework for Nuclear Reactor Analysis
items.summary: To address the long computation time required by stochastic solvers, which are applied in the coupled neutronics-thermal hydraulics (N-TH) calculations, a faster N-TH coupling framework is developed based on the multiphysics coupling library preCICE, which enables data exchange between OpenMOC and OpenFOAM. As an alternative to commonly used stochastic solvers, like OpenMC, OpenMOC is used as a neutronics solver providing much faster steady-state solution in a Picard iteration. To realize this coupling strategy, OpenMC is used for an initial one-time computation cost for multi-group cross sections data generation that is used throughout OpenMOC calculations. A preCICE library adapter for OpenMOC is also developed, allowing data exchange between neutronic power distributions and thermal hydraulic temperature fields.
items.author: Seth S. W. Choo, L. K. Ang, Zhe Chuan Tan

items.title: APOD: 2026 November 17 – Milky Way versus Aurora
items.summary: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 17 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. OriginalAnnotated Milky Way […]

items.title: Fine-Grained Japanese Clinical Named Entity Recognition: A Controlled Comparison of BERT and Open-Weight Large Language Models
items.summary: Background: Generative large language models (LLMs) offer an alternative to encoder-based clinical named entity recognition (NER), but their performance on fine-grained Japanese extraction tasks and sensitivity to generation settings remain uncertain. Methods: We compared two fine-tuned BERT-CRF baselines with nine open-weight LLMs on iCorpus, which defines 113 entity categories. The evaluation used 433 sentences from 36 test documents; 1,672 sentences were used for training. LLMs were evaluated using zero-shot prompting with and without JSON Schema constraints and three-seed QLoRA fine-tuning. Fine-tuned models were assessed under different output-token limits, including 900 and larger model-specific limits of 2,600 or 4,096 tokens. Performance was measured using sentence-level label-surface matching with relaxed and exact-surface F1.
items.author: Feng Han, Ayako Yagahara, Kenji Hirata et al.

items.title: Tossing Fireworks from Cloud to Cloud
items.summary: For many astronauts, the spectacular sight of lightning stands out when looking back at Earth from the International Space Station.

items.title: Learning Optimal Transport Plans Via Autoregressive Token Regression
items.summary: Optimal Transport (OT) provides a principled framework for finding the minimum cost coupling between probability distributions. Classical solvers remain the gold standard for this task. At the same time, OT is an ideal testbed for studying whether learning-based amortized models can internalize the structure of OT type problems. Here, ground-truth solutions are available and marginal constraints are explicitly defined. Also, exact discrete solutions have well-characterized sparsity. We describe ToR-OT, a transformer-based model that learns to predict discrete OT plans through autoregressive token regression. We reframe OT into a structured sequence generation task. ToR-OT decodes sparse transport plans as sequences instead of solving an optimization task at test time.
items.author: Ivan Jaen Marquez, Sotirios Panagiotis Chytas, Vikas Singh

items.title: Communicate the Change: Efficient Expert Parallelism via Activation Compression
items.summary: Scaling has driven the success of large language models (LLM), with sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures enabling greater parameter capacity without a proportional increase in computation. At large scales, MoE models rely on expert parallelism to distribute experts across devices. Each MoE layer requires two synchronous collective communication steps during inference: dispatching hidden states to the activated experts and combining the resulting expert outputs. As compute throughput has outpaced interconnect bandwidth, these synchronous collectives have become a major bottleneck to MoE scaling and efficiency. We address this challenge with EchoMoE, a lightweight architecture modification that retrofits existing MoE models, requiring approximately 8,500x fewer training tokens than full pretraining.
items.author: Fengyuan Liu, Jay Gala, Siva Reddy et al.

items.title: Emergence and Persistence of Maximal Atom-Field Entanglement in the Jaynes-Cummings model
items.summary: We investigate the emergence and persistence of maximal entanglement between a two-level atom and a single-mode quantized electromagnetic field inside a cavity, whose dynamics are governed by the Jaynes-Cummings Hamiltonian. Using the von Neumann entropy as a measure of entanglement, we establish a direct connection between entanglement, atomic coherence, and atomic population inversion. This establishment shows that maximal atom-field entanglement is achieved when both the atomic population inversion and the $l_1$-norm of atomic coherence simultaneously vanish. By considering the atom initially in its excited state, we further demonstrate that the persistence of maximal atom-field entanglement strongly depends on the initial state of the field.
items.author: Siva Prasanna Karri, Mounika Sri Gudipati, Nilakantha Meher

items.title: EGS: A Complementary Safety Framework for Educational LLMs
items.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer strong potential for personalized education, but adolescent-facing deployment raises risks of toxic, biased, misleading, or developmentally inappropriate content. We argue that educational safety should move beyond binary refusal: student queries are often ambiguous or curiosity-driven, requiring contextual guidance rather than simple blocking. We introduce the Educational Guardrail System (EGS), a lightweight, model-agnostic runtime framework that complements intrinsic alignment through query moderation, scenario-aware pedagogical guidance, and response moderation. EGS triages inputs by risk level, redirects gray-zone queries with category-specific educational interventions, and audits outputs before delivery. Experiments across general and education-specific benchmarks show that EGS improves moderation performance, refusal quality, and jailbreak robustness across diverse LLMs.
items.author: Zexuan Fei, Zhengnan Guo, Yiming Luo et al.

items.title: Observation of temporal routing of topological edge states
items.summary: The switching or routing of topological edge states is crucial for disorder-immune state transfer. Previous experimental observations have primarily relied on optical waveguide arrays that treat the spatial coordinate as an equivalent temporal dimension. However, direct experimental observation of the routing dynamics of topological edge states in physical time remains challenging. Here, we report the experimental observation of temporal routing of topological edge states. By constructing a lattice composed of two coupled nonlinear Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chains, the topological edge states exhibit temporal routing behavior controlled by nonlinearity. As the excitation voltage increases from the linear regime, we observe that the voltage intensity distribution transitions from periodic interchain exchange to slowed interchain exchange and ultimately to localization with strongly suppressed interchain exchange, thereby validating the phenomenon of temporal routing.
items.author: Letian Xu, Muhammad Imran, Yongtao Jia et al.

items.title: Microwave hinge states in an all-dielectric woodpile photonic crystal insulator
items.summary: Higher-order topological states are studied in a woodpile photonic crystal (PhC) having a large complete photonic bandgap. According to theoretical predictions, we fabricate a three-dimensional all-dielectric PhC with a millimeter-scale lattice period. The structure consists of two distinct lattice types that coincide through a structural displacement, where their interface intersection gives rise to hinge states. Microwave transmission measurements reveal transmission peaks and spatial localization at the intersection, demonstrating the hinge states. Furthermore, we confirm the absence of hinge states at a specific intersection. As theoretically predicted, hinge states emerge at intersections where the localized boundary polarizations are topologically different, whereas they are absent at intersections where the boundary polarizations are equivalent.
items.author: S. Takahashi, Y. Ashida, H. T. Phan et al.

items.title: Symmetry-selected entanglement death at Floquet resonances of parametrically coupled qubits
items.summary: Periodic modulation of a qubit--qubit coupling is a standard way to engineer quantum interactions, but a strong modulation also reorganizes the transitions through which the qubits dissipate into a comb of Floquet channels. We study two identical, strongly coupled qubits whose transverse coupling is modulated anharmonically, as by a nonlinear coupler, with each qubit damped by its own reservoir. The modulation raises the ground-state concurrence of the cycle-averaged Hamiltonian from 0.45 to above 0.8, yet the steady-state concurrence stays close to its undriven value except at Floquet resonances selected by symmetry. There it undergoes entanglement death, vanishing at all times in the drive cycle over a finite range of modulation depths.
items.author: Kamran Akbari, Stephen Hughes

items.title: From Imperfective Paradox to Moorean Absurdity: Single-Chain Reasoning Lock-In and Multi-Candidate Verbalization Across Aspectual and Pragmatic Ambiguity
items.summary: Natural language entailment and coherence judgments often depend on whether an event merely occurred, reached a telic culmination, satisfied a plan, or was evaluated under multiple pragmatic standards. We test observable consequences of the single-chain premature lock-in hypothesis across four preregistered, sealed formal experiments on Qwen3-8B-Q8_0 (16,640 formal units, temperature=0.0): 15 of 16 hypothesis slots retain confirmatory status (12 rejecting H0 under within-experiment Holm control at alpha_fam=0.05; E3_H3 demoted to descriptive status). In Experiment 1, Direct-CoT vs. MCU differs by 25.00 pp on telic high-confidence completion (Holm p=1.31239e-05), while NLI-CoT collapses by -91.25 pp on uninterrupted atelic items (Holm p=1.81805e-21).
items.author: An-Sheng Jhang

items.title: CueClash: Frontier Vision-Language Models Judge 3-D Relations Close to the Picture Plane
items.summary: A vision-language model (VLM) can judge 3-D relations from the picture or from the ground layout. In photographs the two usually agree. We separate them with CueClash, rendered scenes in which the 2-D cue for each of five relations is right on exactly half the statements. The shortcut gap is accuracy when the cue is right minus accuracy when it is wrong. For Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.6 Flash at low reasoning effort it is +18 to +37 percentage points. It is +7 to +29 without two relations whose cue-wrong items are confounded with borderline cases or occlusion.
items.author: Soham Dan

items.title: RAG in a Trenchcoat: When Minimal Memory Is Enough for Agentic Systems, and When It Isn't
items.summary: Agentic memory research has accumulated extraction, supersession, reflection, and graph synthesis on top of retrieval-augmented generation. However, we found that almost none of those primitives earn their cost in our tested memory benchmarks: we show this with BRIDGE, a deliberately minimal RAG memory with chained observation notes, hybrid BM25 with cosine retrieval, and chronological rendering, which reaches parity within bootstrap CI with the prior SOTA on LongMemEval-S and BEAM, and beats the best memory baseline on EverMemBench by 5.7-6.3 points at matched reader. It runs at ~5-7K reader-prompt tokens per query, using a single LLM call for each ingestion or query.
items.author: Jingyu Liu, Zongze Li, Zach Xu et al.

items.title: CorrectCast: Selective Multimodal Context for Scale-Aware Residual Correction in Precipitation Nowcasting
items.summary: Precipitation nowcasting models suffer from errors in intensity, location, and spatial structure. Addressing these errors by retraining nowcaster backbones can be computationally expensive and requires architecture-specific modifications. To overcome these limitations, we propose CorrectCast, a decoupled residual correction framework that refines completed nowcasts while keeping the base nowcaster frozen. By operating on predicted precipitation fields, CorrectCast requires training only a lightweight corrector, reducing computational overhead while providing a unified correction interface across different nowcasting models. Conditioned on the base nowcast and historical quantitative precipitation estimation (QPE) and precipitable water vapor (PWV) observations, the corrector selects multimodal context and employs scale-aware modulation to estimate residual corrections.
items.author: Henan Wang, Shengwu Xiong, Yifang Zhang et al.

items.title: Reconfigurable 2D Lateral Heterostructure Platform for Unified Detection, Emission, and Logic
items.summary: Heterogeneous integration of sensing, light generation, communication, and computation typically requires specialized devices, resulting in complex interconnects, fabrication overhead, parasitic losses, and energy penalties. Developing a monolithic, reconfigurable device capable of controlling carrier generation, transport, and recombination remains a longstanding challenge. Two-dimensional (2D) lateral heterostructures offer a promising approach by combining spatially distinct domains of different charge polarity with a dynamically tunable electrostatic landscape. Here, multifunctional bilayer MoSe2-WSe2 lateral heterojunctions are demonstrated, integrating photodetection, reconfigurable electroluminescence (EL), and CMOS logic operation within a unified platform. The photodetector exhibits a responsivity of 35 A W-1, a specific detectivity of 5 x 10^13 Jones, and a noise-equivalent power of 6.3 x 10^-18 W Hz^-1/2, enabled by efficient charge separation and photoconductive gain.
items.author: Purbasha Ray, Rupali Verma, Biswajeet Nayak et al.

items.title: Demonstration of a Qubit Control Scheme Compatible with Superconducting Digital Signals
items.summary: Superconducting quantum computing faces a critical scalability bottleneck arising from the escalating complexity of traditional analog control infrastructure. Single-Flux-Quantum(SFQ) systems operate at cryogenic temperatures and offer a potential route to addressing these challenges. Using microwave signals at qubit-dependent frequencies to trigger SFQ pulses requires many independent analog microwave sources, limiting the potential to reduce control wiring and increase integration density. A scalable SFQ control system therefore needs a scheme that can address qubits with different transition frequencies using a common clock. Here, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a control scheme for implementing both single- and two-qubit gates. The scheme uses guiding waveforms to rapidly generate bipolar high-speed pulse sequences on a common clock, providing a basis for future implementation in SFQ control systems.
items.author: Chenyin Sun, Yu Xu, Zihua Chen et al.

items.title: M 4.9 - 26 km E of Port-Olry, Vanuatu
items.summary: A magnitude 4.9 earthquake was recorded 26 km E of Port-Olry, Vanuatu. The event happened on 17 November 2026 at 03:52 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 127 km. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data. The agency event page has the map, updates and safety information.
items.author: USGS

items.title: Active Contrast-Dissipation All-Optical Encryption
items.summary: Optical encryption is meant to place secrecy in physical structure, yet adversaries can readily construct imperfect physical keys to probe the encryption system via trial-and-error iterations. Such systems inevitably leak target plaintext information and preserve invertible residual structural features, rendering the entire encryption scheme vulnerable to adversarial inversion attacks. Here, we report an active contrast-dissipation all-optical encryption architecture, which partitions wavefront modulation into M wavelength-private encryption layers and N shared decoding layers. Security rests on multi-dimensional physical keys that must match simultaneously, including illumination wavelength, precise spatial alignment and layer stacking sequence. With every key matched and authorized readout is preserved: the composite plaintext is reconstructed at a full-detector Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) of 0.997.
items.author: Dongyang Du, Zixuan Fu, Fei Dai et al.

items.title: Quantum Causal Compatibility from Spatiotemporal Correlations
items.summary: Which quantum causal structures can account for observed spatiotemporal correlations without access to an intervention-complete description of the underlying process? In particular, can such correlations distinguish a temporal chain, a common cause, and a common effect? Here, we address these questions using three-qubit pseudo-density operators constructed from experimentally accessible Pauli correlations. We derive necessary and sufficient conditions for pseudo-Markov compatibility with the chain, fork, and collider structures by relaxing complete positivity while preserving the corresponding quantum Markov constraints. Despite their distinct causal mechanisms, all three pseudo-Markov compatibility problems reduce to linear feasibility tests, without requiring full-rank marginal states. We further establish a unified semidefinite-programming approach to physical realizability and quantify the minimum violation of complete positivity through Choi negativity.
items.author: Ya-Xi Ban, Zhu-Jun Zheng, Shao-Ming Fei et al.

items.title: Swift Heavy Ion Tracks in Polymorphs of Titanium Dioxide: The Effects of Electron Beam and Crystal Structures
items.summary: Swift heavy ion (SHI) irradiation generates nanoscale damage in materials, offering opportunities for controlled modification of structural properties. Understanding the fundamental processes governing damage formation in altered regions remains a longstanding challenge. This work explores how crystal structure influences swift heavy ion-induced damage formation and evolution in rutile and anatase TiO2. Combining transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and molecular dynamics simulations, we investigate how differences in atomic arrangement govern track morphology and structural recovery. Although irradiation produces amorphous tracks in both polymorphs, their morphologies differ considerably. In rutile, tracks develop pronounced diameter variations, forming hourglass-like structures, whereas in anatase they retain a relatively uniform cylindrical shape.
items.author: Xiaoting Jia, Lijun Xu, Ruslan A. Rymzhanov et al.

items.title: Synthetic Crystal Data Generation for Diffusion Pretraining in Material Property Prediction
items.summary: Diffusion-based pretraining has emerged as a powerful strategy for learning transferable representations in graph neural networks for materials property prediction without requiring quantum-mechanical labels such as energies, forces, and stresses for every pretraining structure. However, the method retains a critical dependency: it requires structures residing near local minima of a potential energy surface, which have traditionally been obtained through costly DFT relaxations of known or physically synthesized compounds. This reliance constrains both the scale and the structural diversity of available pretraining data, leaving large regions of crystal structure space unexplored. In this work, we connect diffusion-based pretraining with synthetic structure generation to reduce this bottleneck.
items.author: Aamod Varma, Shuyi Jia, Victor Fung

items.title: Exceptional-point Sensing with Quantum Advantage
items.summary: Exceptional-point sensors exploit singular non-Hermitian dynamics to enhance their response to weak perturbations. Recently, however, a no-go result has been established for a gain-loss-balanced dimer coupled to independent, phase-insensitive reservoirs: the exceptional-point susceptibility amplifies the signal and reservoir noise equally, precluding any quantum advantage. Here, we circumvent this limitation by engineering non-Hermitian dynamics in particle-hole Nambu space. A single common reservoir acts on modes forming a quantum-mechanics-free subsystem and generates an enhanced response protected from additional noise. We demonstrate quantum-metrological advantage for weak-signal sensing and static-parameter estimation. A continuous interpolation of the operator basis at fixed exceptional-point drift, with a singular midpoint, reveals how reservoir noise vanishes toward the protected limit.
items.author: Chuming Wang, Xinyao Guo, Dezhi Zhang et al.

items.title: Two-Qutrit Quantum Battery Charging through Ising Model and Anisotropic XZ Heisenberg Interactions
items.summary: In this paper, we propose a model of a two-qutrit quantum battery composed of two spin-1 systems coupled to an external field via anisotropic Heisenberg interactions. From the Ising model, we derive an exact analytical expression of ergotropy in the parallel-charging case. However, the collective charging process offers an advantage over the parallel one. Moreover, increasing the collective exchange coupling accelerates the evolution of ergotropy and enhances the maximum average power, as measured by global coherence and mutual information. Conversely, the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interaction primarily acts as a detrimental mechanism, essentially reducing all of these quantities. In the XZ model, the obtained results show that the DM interaction is constructive when it cooperates with the longitudinal anisotropy and when the exchange coupling is sufficiently strong.
items.author: F. El Hani, I. El Aouadi, K. El Anouz et al.

items.title: Variational Relevance-Informed Sparsification of Term Measurements for Variational Quantum Algorithms
items.summary: Repeated measurements are a major bottleneck in variational quantum algorithms (VQAs). We uncover and characterize parameter-specific sparsity in the matrix of qubit-wise commuting (QWC) group contributions to parameter-shift gradients: most absolute contribution mass concentrates in a subset of groups whose relevance varies across parameters and optimization states. Building on this structure, we introduce a learned controller that predicts group relevance from Hamiltonian, circuit, light-cone, and current-state features, then selects measurements through a tunable coverage threshold. Exact contributions provide offline supervision without being required at deployment. Across 15 molecular VQE settings, our method saves 49.6% of nominal gradient-measurement shots with a mean absolute energy gap of 5.67 mHa to Full-QWC.
items.author: Yifeng Peng, Bin Yan, Harshal Shah et al.

items.title: Backward-scattering photoelectron holography of a polar molecule driven by a sub-cycle laser pulse
items.summary: We investigate photoelectron holographic interference in the polar CO molecule driven by a sub-cycle laser pulse using time-dependent Schrödinger equation simulations and a classical-trajectory-based analysis. The sub-cycle temporal confinement of the driving field enables the forward-scattering holographic (FSH) and backward-scattering holographic (BSH) interference structures in the photoelectron momentum distributions (PMDs) to be clearly distinguished. The FSH fringes exhibit a strong dependence on molecular orientation, which is associated with the orientation-dependent transverse displacement of the ionizing electron wave packet (EWP). Furthermore, the heteronuclear nature of CO results in different FSH fringe shifts for ionization occurring predominantly from the C and O sides of the molecule.
items.author: Rambabu Rajpoot, Eiji J. Takahashi

items.title: Perturbative Recovery of Stabilizer-Subspace Correlations for Quantum Computational Chemistry
items.summary: Stabilizer-based subspace methods can substantially reduce the quantum resources required for electronic structure calculations, but the resulting projection neglects Hamiltonian couplings to configurations outside the retained subspace. In this work, we introduce Stabilizer-Subspace Perturbation Theory (SSPT) to recover the associated correlation contributions, using the Contextual Subspace Variational Quantum Eigensolver (CS-VQE) as a representative application. The central idea is to exploit the Pauli terms eliminated by stabilizer projection as perturbative operators that generate an external manifold from the optimized reference state. Their energetic contributions are evaluated using an Epstein-Nesbet-type second-order correction or a resolvent-based formulation that retains couplings within the external space.
items.author: Qianjun Yao, Jie Liu, He Li

items.title: Regular/Singular Black Hole Thermodynamics from Renormalised Volume/Area
items.summary: We study the finite mismatch between the holographically and topologically renormalised Euclidean actions of the four-dimensional AdS C-metric. Starting from the relation between Renormalised Volume and the Einstein sector of Conformal Gravity, we separate the regular curvature contribution from the contributions supported on the two conical axes. After introducing the usual Euler normalisation for smooth manifolds, the residual difference between the regular action evaluations is determined by the tension-weighted Euler terms of the renormalised worldsheet area. We identify this difference with the Gauss--Bonnet entropy contribution at the polar conical points of the horizon. The ordinary Euler characteristic remains fixed, while the deficits determine how its curvature representation is divided between regular and singular contributions.
items.author: Gabriel Arenas-Henriquez, Rodrigo Olea, David Rivera-Betancour

items.title: Second Harmonic Flexoelectricity
items.summary: Flexoelectricity (polarization induced by strain gradients) is assumed to be insensitive to space inversion in all materials: flexoelectric polarization should not depend on whether a crystal is bent upwards or downwards. In this work, we show that this assumption is wrong for ferroelectrics of all thickness and at all curvatures, owing to an intrinsic quadratic contribution that persists down to strain gradients of 1 m-1 or less, which is millions of times smaller than conventional expectations for nonlinear flexoelectricity. As a consequence, ferroelectric crystals can generate second-harmonic voltage at twice the oscillation frequency of the bending.
items.author: Zhiguo Wang, Yida Yang, Shuai Yang et al.

items.title: M 5.0 - 137 km SSE of Kirakira, Solomon Islands
items.summary: A magnitude 5 earthquake was recorded 137 km SSE of Kirakira, Solomon Islands. The event happened on 17 November 2026 at 02:00 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 10 km. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data. The agency event page has the map, updates and safety information.
items.author: USGS

items.title: Electrostatic screening and nitrogen-vacancy charge states in boron-doped/nitrogen-doped diamond junctions
items.summary: Boron-doped diamond (BDD) enables the integration of electrical functionality with nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers, but the influence of junction electrostatics on NV charge-state stability remains unclear. In this study, we investigate the equilibrium electrostatics of BDD/nitrogen-doped diamond junctions using self-consistent Poisson-Fermi calculations. The results reveal two distinct electrostatic length scales in the nitrogen-doped substrate: a near-interface region of ionized donors that produces dominant band bending and determines the NV$^{0/-}$ charge-state boundary, and a much longer screening tail associated with weak donor ionization in the neutral bulk. The resulting NV$^-$ depletion depth depends strongly on the nitrogen concentration but exhibits a more moderate dependence on boron doping.
items.author: Masato Koga, Haizen Cho, El Mustapha Mansouri et al.

items.title: Apparent contact angle equation for a dielectric droplet on a conductive hydrophilic surface in an electric field
items.summary: A dielectric droplet resting on a conductive substrate elongates when a voltage is applied across the surrounding gap without touching the upper electrode. We construct a closed form theory of the equilibrium shapes by approximating the interface as a truncated spheroid with a single shape parameter and obtain the dimensionless electrostatic prefactor that corrects the free-space depolarization, based on the mirror symmetry across the substrate. Minimizing the resulting free energy along voltage ramps reproduces the boundary-element-method (BEM) equilibria, both the droplet height and the contact-line radius, with and without gravity, at negligible computational cost. An explicit apparent contact angle equation is found that collapses all the numerical calculation data.
items.author: Ren-Qiang Huang, Gao-Xiao Jiang, Zhong-Yi Li et al.

items.title: QCap: a physics-corrected graph neural network for the capacitance matrix of any planar superconducting device layout
items.summary: Electromagnetic simulations of device layouts to extract capacitance are computationally intensive, a major obstacle to accurate design of circuit devices. Machine learning models can bypass these simulations, but previous approaches have been restricted to layouts using only particular components, and require thousands of simulations of those same components as training data. We present QCap, a model that accurately predicts the Maxwell capacitance matrix of an arbitrary superconducting device layout in seconds, compared to minutes to hours of Ansys Q3D simulations. We develop a novel design-embedding algorithm that converts the layout into a universal graph format, allowing the model to work with any layout created with any tool.
items.author: Sadman Ahmed Shanto, Saikat Das, Eli M. Levenson-Falk

items.title: DSADiff: Data Structure-Aware Diffusion for Crystal Structure Prediction via Mitigating Complexity- and Imbalance-Induced Biases
items.summary: Crystal Structure Prediction (CSP) is an important step in accelerating the generation and discovery of new materials. In recent years, diffusion-based CSP methods have made significant progress. However, existing models still suffer from generation bias when facing diverse materials spaces, while systematic approaches for tracing the sources of such performance variations remain limited. To address this issue, we propose LAS (Layered Analysis Strategy), a mechanism analysis framework that identifies crystal complexity and elemental composition imbalance as two key factors affecting generation difficulty and further reveals their relationships with model generation performance. Building on these findings, we further propose DSADiff (Data Structure-Aware Diffusion), a data structure-aware diffusion model that transforms the key factors identified by LAS into a unified generation difficulty representation and uses it to jointly drive feature modeling and training strategy optimization.
items.author: Jiang Xiaobo, Dinghong Lai

items.title: Quantum Born Geometries from Modular Quantization
items.summary: A structural link between quantization and "thermal-doubled" non-commutative Born geometry (with its split-quaternionic structure) is uncovered via Tomita-Takesaki first-quantized modular theory for complexified and polarized ortho-symplectic spaces. Implications for the modular algebraic quantum gravity program (arXiv:1007.4094) hint at further deep modifications of the notions of space and geometry (thermal quantum space-time hypothesis) waiting to be further explored. Speculative suggestions in the direction of A.Sakharov and L.Boyle-K.Finn-N.Turok CPT-mirror cosmologies will be mentioned, among several others. The present work is based on the manuscript "Modular Quantization and Non-commutative Space-time" (now on alphaXiv) that has been shared, with a selected number of researchers, since end of April 2026.
items.author: Paolo Bertozzini, Roberto Conti

items.title: Double parton scattering singularities in two-loop gluon-fusion amplitudes
items.summary: Gluon fusion to two massive colour singlets can develop a double parton scattering (DPS) singularity as $p_T\to0$: each gluon splits, and its daughters fuse pairwise. We determine two-loop logarithms using a common kernel and derive finite matching functions analytically for gluon and quark splittings. Normalised to one loop, the cubic coefficient changes sign between channels. Complete $gg\to HH$, $gg\to AA$ and $gg\to ZZ$ amplitudes confirm the predicted colour, helicity and parity dependence and phase. The kernel gives leading DPS logarithms for other pairs with this DPS configuration.
items.author: Arunima Bhattacharya

items.title: Frame Based Inelasticity for Strength and Fracture in Anisotropic Media
items.summary: A field theory is presented for predicting damage and fracture in brittle materials. Four concepts are used: a new nonlocal deformation gradient for dynamic stress analysis in anisotropic media, a new type of phase field coming from a constitutive law, the evolution of material displacement from Newton's second law, and a new incorporation of scaled strength surfaces into constitutive laws for predicting dynamic and quasi-static fracture patterns. The elastic softening is governed by the strain dynamics through the constitutive law and in this way we provide the two way coupling between strain and fracture. Simulations validating the approach for both dynamic and quasi-static fracture analysis are compared to experimental results and other simulation methods.
items.author: Robert Lipton, Prakash K. C.

items.title: Long-standing Chronic Diarrhea Associated With Intestinal Spirochetosis Incidentally Diagnosed in a Rectal Adenoma Specimen Resected by Cold Snare Polypectomy: A Case Report.
items.summary: Intestinal spirochetosis (IS) is an uncommon condition that is often asymptomatic and detected incidentally but may occasionally present with chronic diarrhea. We report a case of IS incidentally identified in the adjacent non-neoplastic mucosa of a rectal adenoma specimen resected by cold snare polypectomy. We present a case of a man in his 50s who was referred for a positive fecal occult blood test and had a history of chronic diarrhea. Colonoscopy revealed a 5-mm sessile polyp in the upper rectum, which was removed by cold snare polypectomy. Histopathological examination showed a tubular adenoma. In addition, routine hematoxylin and eosin staining revealed a characteristic false brush border on the adjacent non-neoplastic colorectal epithelium, consistent with IS.
items.author: Tajika M, Takagi A, Hori M, Ito N, Tanaka T, Iwakoshi A, Sasaki E, Hosoda W.

items.title: New-onset depersonalization-derealization syndrome following semaglutide therapy.
items.summary: Semaglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist prescribed for type 2 diabetes and obesity, acts on central neuropsychiatric pathways beyond its metabolic effects, yet dissociative adverse effects have rarely been reported. We describe a 42-year-old woman with no psychiatric history who developed recurrent, distressing episodes of depersonalization and derealization approximately 7 days after her second 0.5 mg weekly dose of semaglutide prescribed for obesity. The episodes progressed from once daily to 3 to 4 times daily over 10 days, with insight and reality testing preserved throughout. Metabolic, neurological, toxicological, and psychiatric evaluations, including brain imaging, electroencephalography, and laboratory studies, excluded alternative causes.
items.author: Prasad S, Sharma A, Sharma A, Parmar V, Kothia D, Bavaria D.

items.title: Occult virilization: an elusive ovarian steroid cell tumor.
items.summary: Rapidly progressive hirsutism or virilization in a postmenopausal woman should prompt evaluation for pathological androgen excess, most commonly arising from an adrenal or ovarian tumor. We report a case of a 58-year-old postmenopausal woman with rapidly progressive severe hirsutism and virilization over 4 months. Examination revealed clitoromegaly, voice deepening, and coarse facial hair growth. Biochemistry demonstrated markedly elevated androgen levels with only slightly elevated dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate, supporting an ovarian source. Ultrasonography, computed tomography (CT), and magnetic resonance imaging were inconclusive because a large fibroid uterus obscured the adnexa. Subsequent fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/CT ( 18 F-FDG PET/CT) demonstrated a metabolically active right adnexal lesion.
items.author: Krishnasamy Naido SN, Khinder S, Dudek A, Vogazianou A.

items.title: Intestinal ischemia in 2 pediatric patients with new-onset diabetes with mixed ketoacidosis and hyperosmolar state.
items.summary: We report 2 pediatric patients-a 4-year-old male (case 1) and a 10-month-old male (case 2)-who presented in mixed diabetic ketoacidosis/hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state in the setting of new-onset diabetes, complicated by intestinal ischemia requiring bowel resection. Case 1 developed nonocclusive mesenteric ischemia requiring ileal resection, and case 2 developed thrombotic mesenteric ischemia requiring subtotal colectomy and small bowel resection, resulting in short bowel syndrome. These cases illustrate intestinal ischemia as a potential complication of pediatric hyperglycemic emergencies, underscoring the importance of prompt surgical evaluation when abdominal findings worsen despite appropriate metabolic resuscitation.
items.author: Chatterjee P, Ashmore H, Garg N, Metzinger E.

items.title: Differences of sex development associated with asymmetric overgrowth in a patient with 69,XXY/46,XX mosaicism.
items.summary: Individuals with both differences in sex development (DSD) and asymmetric overgrowth are rare. This clinical presentation may be associated with chromosomal mosaicism. Multiple methodologies may be needed to establish the diagnosis. An 11-month-old patient was referred for evaluation of DSD and segmental overgrowth. Clinical examination showed right-sided facial enlargement, predominantly left-sided limb overgrowth, macrodactyly, and hypo- and hyperpigmented skin lesions. Genital examination revealed clitoromegaly, a midline urogenital sinus, and a palpable right gonad. Pelvic ultrasonography demonstrated a left-sided hemiuterus and a left intra-abdominal gonad. Gonadal biopsy revealed a dysgenetic testis on the right and an ovary on the left. Serum estradiol was 27 pg/mL (International System of Units [SI], 99.1 pmol/L) (reference range, 7-28 pg/mL [SI, 25.7-102.7 pmol/L]), consistent with female reference values.
items.author: Vaiani E, Caino S, Marino R, Daroqui M, Belgorosky A, Berensztein E.

items.title: Novel AIP variant in aggressive somatotroph adenoma presenting as gigantism.
items.summary: Acromegaly and gigantism usually occur sporadically, but familial cases exist. Germline pathogenic variants in the aryl hydrocarbon receptor-interacting protein ( AIP ) gene are associated with familial isolated pituitary adenoma including early-onset, large, and aggressive growth hormone (GH)-secreting adenomas that often respond poorly to somatostatin analogs (SAs). A male patient presented with gigantism due to a GH-secreting pituitary macroadenoma (30 × 43 × 35 mm). Biochemical evaluation confirmed GH excess (insulin-like growth factor I standard deviation score +6.9; nadir GH 85.5 µg/L [International system of units (SI): 85.5 ng/mL]) (reference AIP variant, c.668_671del; p. (Trp223Serfs*79). Family screening revealed 4 carriers.
items.author: Arlien-Søborg MC, Stochholm K, M Christiansen TE, Korbonits M, Jørgensen JOL, Dal J.

items.title: Transient hypoparathyroidism and symptomatic hypocalcemia complicating babesiosis.
items.summary: Babesiosis, caused by Babesia microti , is a tick-borne intraerythrocytic infection with diverse manifestations, but endocrine complications are rarely reported. We describe a 60-year-old man who presented with fever, chills, and cognitive symptoms and was diagnosed with babesiosis by peripheral smear, serology, and polymerase chain reaction. Despite improvement with atovaquone and azithromycin, he developed confusion, paresthesia, and fatigue, prompting further investigation. Laboratory testing revealed hypocalcemia (total calcium, 6.8 mg/dL [SI: 1.7 mmol/L]; reference range, 8.4-10.4 mg/dL [SI: 2.10-2.60 mmol/L]); ionized calcium, 3.8 mg/dL (SI: 0.95 mmol/L; reference range, 4.7-5.5 mg/dL [SI: 1.17-1.37 mmol/L]), a low parathyroid hormone concentration of 9 pg/mL (SI: 9 ng/L; reference range, 18-88 pg/mL [SI: 1.9-9.3 pmol/L]), and hyperphosphatemia, with phosphate concentration of 5.7 mg/dL (SI: 1.84 mmol/L; reference range, 2.5-4.5 mg/dL [SI: 0.81-1.45 mmol/L]), consistent with hypoparathyroidism, with normal magnesium and vitamin D levels.
items.author: Amer B, Phillips B.

items.title: A case of 46,XY differences of sex development due to 17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 3 deficiency.
