items.summary: Seventeen β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 3 is a critical enzyme in the final step of testosterone synthesis, necessary for normal virilization of male external genitalia. Deficiency of this enzyme in 46,XY individuals leads to a broad spectrum of phenotypes, from predominantly female appearance through atypical genitalia to undervirilized male genitalia. We report a 15-month-old child, initially assigned female at birth, who was referred for endocrine evaluation due to concerns about sex development. Caregivers reported signs of virilization, including phallic growth and increased muscularity starting from 6 weeks of age, with progressive phallic enlargement prompting referral. Baseline hormonal evaluation revealed a total testosterone concentration below the laboratory age-specific reference for male infant, elevated luteinizing hormone, follicle-stimulating hormone concentration within the reference interval, and Sertoli cell function markers within the reference range.
items.author: Kahssay M, Ashraf AP.

items.title: Xanthomas revealing underlying familial hypercholesterolemia.
items.author: Sequeira RM, Sadananda S, Shetty S, Hosahithlu Keshava Bhat G.

items.title: RNA splicing is required for timely abscission and is modulated by the abscission checkpoint.
items.summary: The abscission checkpoint pauses progression of cytokinetic abscission at the intercellular bridge when various checkpoint-sustaining errors are sensed. A unique cytoplasmic organelle, the abscission checkpoint body (ACB), forms when the abscission checkpoint is active. This organelle houses proteins involved in abscission and RNA splicing. Here, we investigate the role of RNA splicing factors in abscission checkpoint maintenance. A specific subset of RNA splicing factors localizes to ACBs, while others move back into the nucleus. The key RNA splicing factor SF3b1 is aberrantly localized in the cytoplasm when ACBs are present. Timely abscission was found to rely on RNA splicing, and we have identified patterns in gene expression and RNA splicing that occur at this time in cell division.
items.author: Couldwell GC, Vincent-Mueller JN, Mackay DR, Jensen CC, Stubben CJ, Li L, Tan AC, Sundquist WI, Ullman KS.

items.title: Chronic high-fat diet disrupts the homeostatic and differentiation potential of megakaryocyte-erythroid progenitors.
items.summary: Chronic obesity induced by a high-fat diet (HFD) profoundly alters systemic metabolism; however, its impact on hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell (HSPC) lineage commitment, particularly erythroid differentiation, remains poorly understood. To address this question, C57BL/6 mice were fed an HFD for 16 weeks to establish an obesity model. HFD induced significant weight gain, hyperlipidemia, and increased bone marrow adiposity, accompanied by a marked elevation in total bone marrow cellularity. Peripheral blood analysis revealed increased white blood cell counts, together with elevated red blood cell counts and hemoglobin levels despite reduced circulating reticulocytes. Flow cytometric analysis further demonstrated a significant expansion of HSPCs and downstream progenitor populations in the bone marrow.
items.author: Lv X, Xu C, Yu W, Liang J, Zhou Y.

items.title: Understanding Sleep in Ultramarathon Runners: An Exploratory Assessment during a Training Week.
items.summary: Sleep plays a vital role in sports performance. Ultramarathon runners may experience impaired sleep during training and competition; however, further investigation is needed. The current study aimed to evaluate sleep in ultramarathon runners during a typical training week. We evaluated 15 male athletes with a mean age of 45.1 ± 10.5 years and a mean ultramarathon experience of 6.37 ± 6.49 years. Sleep was assessed using the Munich Chronotype Questionnaire, the Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, the Athlete Sleep Behavior Questionnaire, the Epworth Sleepiness Scale, and a 7-day sleep diary. Most participants were morning chronotypes (86.7%), and the mean social jetlag of was 0.60 ± 0.69 hour.
items.author: Daniel NVS, Belli T, Esteves AM.

items.title: How We Use Corticosteroids in Immune Thrombocytopenia.
items.summary: Introduction Corticosteroids remain an important first-line treatment for immune thrombocytopenia (ITP), but their benefits are accompanied by substantial toxicities across various body systems. Their use should therefore be individualised and time-limited. Methods We synthesise current guidance and published evidence concerning the selection of patients for corticosteroids treatment, choice of regimen, prevention and monitoring of treatment-related toxicity, recognition of response and non-response, and structured tapering and discontinuation in adults with ITP. Results Corticosteroids should be avoided when observation is clinically appropriate and, when prescribed, should have a pre-defined indication, haemostatic control target, expected time to response and stopping date. Accepted first-line regimens include prednisolone at 1-2 mg/kg/day, generally capped at 60-80 mg daily, or high-dose dexamethasone at 40 mg daily for 4 days.
items.author: Gurumurthy G, Morgan M, Provan D, Thachil J.

items.title: Identifying characteristics and behavioral phenotypes of musculoskeletal disorders using wearables in All of Us.
items.summary: Objective Wearable devices provide continuous measures of daily activity, sleep, and heart-rate (HR)-derived characteristics, creating new opportunities for digital phenotyping of musculoskeletal disorders (MSD). However, longitudinal behavioral patterns and heterogeneity among individuals with MSD remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify characteristics associated with MSD and characterize behavioral phenotypes using longitudinal wearable data. Materials and methods We analyzed 2344 participants (MSD = 1036; non-MSD = 1308) from the All of Us Research Program. First, supervised machine-learning models were trained using sociodemographic, physical measurement, and wearable-derived features to distinguish individuals with and without MSD and identify factors associated with MSD status.
items.author: Yan AY, Speed TJ, Taylor CO.

items.title: Advances in 3D-Printed Scaffolds for Regenerative Therapy.
items.summary: Three-dimensional (3D) printing enables precise control over scaffold geometry, porosity, material distribution, and spatial delivery of cells and bioactive cues. However, features intended to improve biological fidelity often increase manufacturing complexity, quality-control demands, and regulatory burden. This review evaluates 3D-printed scaffolds for regenerative therapy using a design-to-translation framework. We compare acellular printing, cell-laden bioprinting, and hybrid fabrication, and examine how material composition, architecture, mechanics, degradation, gradients, vascularization, innervation, and immune integration determine performance. Evidence is synthesized across cartilage and osteochondral repair, bone, skin, neural, and spinal cord repair, skeletal muscle and soft tissues, and cardiac and vascular regeneration. Current evidence places acellular or minimally bioactive patient-specific scaffolds closest to clinical adoption, particularly when anatomical conformity and structural support are the dominant requirements.
items.author: Song S, Guo N, Wang S, Liu W, Wang H, Yan X.

items.title: No impact of gluten-free diet on glycemia, growth, or quality of life in asymptomatic celiac disease with type 1 diabetes.
items.summary: Context Evidence is limited on longitudinal health outcomes with a gluten-free diet (GFD) in patients with type 1 diabetes (T1D) and asymptomatic celiac disease (CD) identified by screening. Objectives To investigate the impact of the GFD on glycemic management, anthropometrics, gastrointestinal symptoms, health-related quality of life (HRQoL), and nutritional intakes in patients with T1D and screen-detected CD. Methods Celiac Disease and Diabetes Longitudinal Follow-up and Evaluation Study (CD-LiFE) was a prospective follow-up study (NCT03122093) whereby 62 participants aged 8-45 years (77% adult, 23% pediatric) with T1D and screen-detected CD were evaluated annually over a 2-year study period.
items.author: Weiman DI, Clarke ABM, Pace K, Assor E, McDonald C, Saibil F, Lochnan HA, Punthakee Z, Marcon MA, Mahmud FH.

items.title: Comprehensive Genomic Landscape Across Histopathological Stages of Lung Adenocarcinoma: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
items.summary: The genomic features associated with the histopathological spectrum from precursor glandular lesions to invasive lung adenocarcinoma remain incompletely characterized. In this retrospective cross-sectional study, we performed targeted sequencing of 823 resected lesions from 823 patients, including 149 precursor glandular lesions (11 atypical adenomatous hyperplasia [AAH] and 138 adenocarcinoma in situ [AIS]), 252 minimally invasive adenocarcinoma (MIA), and 422 invasive adenocarcinoma (IAC). EGFR mutation frequency increased across precursor lesions, MIA, and IAC (44%, 57%, and 65%), whereas ERBB2 decreased (20%, 13%, and 6%); TP53 was markedly enriched in IAC (3%, 6%, and 35%). Cell-cycle and homologous recombination repair (HRR) pathway alterations were likewise more frequent in IAC and in Grade 3 tumors.
items.author: Hu X, Huang Y, Cao Y, Wang W, Wang J, Wang K, Wu D, Fu S, Wang M, Wang K.

items.title: High resolution spatiotemporal modelling of outdoor temperature for assessment of heat-related health inequalities in Accra, Ghana.
items.summary: Urban heat exposure is unevenly distributed within cities, often disproportionately affecting socially and environmentally vulnerable populations. In Sub-Saharan Africa(SSA), where warming is occurring faster than the global average, the lack of high-resolution temperature data constrain efforts to characterize exposure patterns and inform epidemiological research and urban heat adaptation. We developed the first ground-based spatiotemporal outdoor temperature surfaces for a major SSA city using an 18-month measurement campaign across the Greater Accra Metropolitan Area, Ghana. Temperature data were collected from 143 sites using iButton sensors. The field measurement data were combined with satellite-derived and land use predictors within a mixed-effects land use regression framework to model daily mean, maximum, and minimum temperature at 24 h, daytime(6:00-17:59), and nighttime(18:00-5:59) periods.
items.author: Doyle H, Nath V, Nathvani R, Agyei-Mensah S, Hughes AF, Ezzati M, Fecht D, Arku R, Baumgartner J.

items.title: A novel homozygous ITCH nonsense variant causing autoimmune disease, multisystem, with facial dysmorphism: expanding the phenotypic and geographic spectrum.
items.summary: Autoimmune disease, multisystem, with facial dysmorphism (ADMFD) is an ultra-rare autosomal recessive disorder. It is caused by biallelic loss-of-function variants in ITCH , which encodes a ubiquitin ligase that regulates immune homeostasis. Fewer than 15 cases have been reported, all of North American or Western European origin. We describe a girl of Egyptian origin living in the United Arab Emirates. She was first evaluated at age 8 years for severe short stature, delayed puberty, and primary hypothyroidism. Glucagon stimulation testing excluded growth hormone deficiency. At age 15 years, a 145-gene panel identified a novel homozygous ITCH nonsense variant (c.2119C>T; p.Arg707*), supporting a molecular diagnosis of ADMFD.
items.author: Ali NS, Mundi Dhahrabi HA, Abdul Raheem Al Marzooqi L, Tarif Hamza R.

items.title: Changes in dystrophic calcification of the breast associated with abaloparatide therapy.
items.summary: High-risk osteoporosis treatment strategy aims at improving bone mineral density and fracture prevention. Clinicians' awareness of the indications and potential complications associated with osteoporosis treatments is important because it involves caring for patients with comorbidities who experience polypharmacy. We present a case of breast calcification changes after initiation of abaloparatide. A 65-year-old female started abaloparatide therapy and after 8 months of abaloparatide treatment, a significant progression of bilateral breast calcification was noted in screening mammogram prompting a biopsy that showed coarse calcifications without any features of dysplasia or malignancy. After 2 years of abaloparatide therapy, follow-up mammogram revealed stable breast calcifications but that were still significantly increased from baseline prior to abaloparatide.
items.author: Herrera Chancay AM, Bhatnagar A, Foshee SD, Mir M, Soe KK.

items.title: Use of osilodrostat in life-threatening ectopic Cushing syndrome secondary to neuroendocrine tumor.
items.summary: Ectopic adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) syndrome is a rare, severe form of endogenous Cushing syndrome requiring rapid cortisol reduction; experience with osilodrostat in critically ill patients remains limited. A 41-year-old woman with a prior supraglottic neuroendocrine tumor (NET) presented with rapidly progressive proximal weakness, severe hypokalemia, hypertension, and delirium. Adrenocorticotropic hormone-dependent hypercortisolism was confirmed, with a 12 × 10 × 14-cm abdominal mass showing somatostatin receptor uptake as the probable ectopic source. She required intensive care, intubation, and intravenous etomidate, but developed vasoplegic shock and multiorgan failure despite cortisol reduction. Etomidate was replaced by oral osilodrostat, which rapidly achieved stable serum cortisol over 4 weeks.
items.author: Mansour S, Dabbous Z, Elhiday H, Elaffandi A, Mokhtar M, Rohani Z.

items.title: Successful hypertension control in 17-hydroxylase deficiency using crinecerfont.
items.summary: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) due to 17α-hydroxylase/17,20-lyase deficiency (17OHD) is a rare form of CAH characterized by cortisol deficiency, impaired sex steroid production, and excess deoxycorticosterone (DOC), resulting in low-renin hypertension and hypokalemia. Management typically relies on glucocorticoid therapy to suppress adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)-driven steroidogenesis, but adequate disease control may require supraphysiologic glucocorticoid doses and intensive antihypertensive treatment. Crinecerfont, a corticotropin-releasing factor type 1 (CRF1) receptor antagonist approved for classic CAH, has not previously been reported in 17OHD. We describe a 23-year-old woman with 46,XY karyotype and classic 17OHD with severe persistent hypertension despite high-dose glucocorticoids, spironolactone, and multiple antihypertensive agents.
items.author: Herrera Chancay A, Abramowitz J, Ali S, Hamidi O.

items.title: Vertebral fracture cascade in Cushing disease.
items.author: Miyagawa H, Yamazaki T, Takeuchi Y, Takeshita A.

items.title: Thyroid storm induced by palpation thyroiditis after subtotal parathyroidectomy for lithium-induced hyperparathyroidism.
items.summary: Palpation thyroiditis is an inflammatory condition of the thyroid gland that may occur following mechanical manipulation, particularly during parathyroid surgery. While postoperative biochemical thyrotoxicosis is relatively common, most patients remain asymptomatic, and severe presentations such as thyroid storm are rare. We report a 52-year-old man with primary hyperparathyroidism, likely lithium-induced, who underwent subtotal parathyroidectomy. His immediate postoperative course was uneventful; however, on postoperative day 3, he developed anterior neck swelling, followed by systemic symptoms including tachycardia, tremor, and fatigue by postoperative day 5. Biochemical findings confirmed severe thyrotoxicosis, and imaging demonstrated inflammatory swelling and edema around the thyroid without abscess formation.
items.author: Elamin M, Mohamed S, Kaplan F, Patel A, Dimitriadis P, Ilesanmi I.

items.title: Functioning gonadotropinomas with ovarian hyperstimulation and multicystic ovaries: a tale of 2 tumors and 2 organs.
items.summary: Functioning gonadotropinomas are rare pituitary adenomas that secrete biologically active gonadotropins and may present with ovarian hyperstimulation and multicystic ovarian enlargement in premenopausal women, often mimicking primary ovarian disease and leading to delayed diagnosis. We describe 2 women with ovarian manifestations secondary to functioning gonadotropinomas. Case 1 was a 36-year-old woman who presented with a 12-year history of abnormal uterine bleeding and bilateral multicystic ovaries initially suspected to be ovarian neoplasms. Later, she developed progressive visual impairment in the right eye. Laboratory tests showed an elevated follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) level, and pituitary magnetic resonance imaging revealed a macroadenoma. Transsphenoidal surgery confirmed an FSH/luteinizing hormone-positive gonadotroph adenoma, with postoperative regression of ovarian cysts.
items.author: Ghosh J, Mahadevan S, Shah R, Sundaram S, Grossman AB, Dutta P.

items.title: Norepinephrine-dominant pheochromocytoma associated with impaired insulin secretion and insulin resistance.
items.summary: Pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas (PPGLs) are known to cause impaired glucose tolerance through both impaired insulin secretion and insulin resistance driven by catecholamine excess. Previous experimental and clinical studies have suggested that noradrenergic PPGLs induce glucose intolerance predominantly through increased insulin resistance, whereas adrenergic PPGLs induce glucose intolerance primarily through impaired insulin secretion. We report a rare case of sporadic 123 I-metaiodobenzylguanidine-negative adrenal pheochromocytoma with a noradrenergic biochemical profile: while plasma norepinephrine and normetanephrine levels were elevated, plasma epinephrine and metanephrine levels were within the normal range.
items.author: Kubota T, Tagashira A, Nakamura Y, Kitamura Y, Fujita H.

items.title: Correction to: CsML08/11 are required for full susceptibility of cucumber stem to powder mildew and interact with CsCRK2 and CsRbohD.
items.summary: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.1093/hr/uhad295.].

items.title: Trinidadian Killifish ( Anablepsoides hartii ) From Streams With Parasitic Intestinal Nematodes ( Camallanus cotti ) Have Decreased Brain Size and Brain Cell Proliferation.
items.summary: Trinidadian killifish ( Anablepsoides hartii ) live in streams that vary in the presence of parasites, competitors, and predators. This allows for ideal field studies on how biotic factors interact to affect fitness and morphology, including brain size and brain plasticity. Infection rates with parasitic gut nematodes ( Camallanus cotti ) are higher, and survival is lower in sites with competitors (guppies, Poecilia reticulata ) compared to sites without competitors. To assess the possible effect of parasite-induced changes in the brain as a factor contributing to this increased mortality, we collected killifish from streams varying in parasitic infection rates and competitors, and measured their brain mass and brain cell proliferation rate.
items.author: Maggioni Z, Walsh MR, Dunlap KD.

items.title: Hybrid ESD-Assisted Transanal Full-Thickness Excision for Localized Anorectal Malignant Melanoma Achieving 4-Year Recurrence-Free Survival.
items.summary: Anorectal malignant melanoma (AMM) is a rare, aggressive malignancy with controversial surgical management. We report a 65-year-old man with localized AMM above the anal verge who strongly desired anorectal preservation. A hybrid procedure combining endoscopic submucosal dissection-assisted mucosal incision with transanal full-thickness excision achieved R0 resection of an 18 × 20-mm pT2 tumor with venous invasion. The postoperative course was uneventful. Although additional radical surgery was recommended, the patient declined further treatment. He has remained recurrence-free for 4 years. Hybrid ESD-assisted transanal excision may be a feasible organ-preserving option for selected patients with localized AMM.
items.author: Kuwano T, Shimaoka S, Kusumoto H, Ikeda N, Kitazono M, Shimizu T.

items.title: Digital Necrosis as an Initial Manifestation of a Myeloproliferative Neoplasm.
items.summary: Digital necrosis is a clinical presentation of the hand, which may indicate an underlying systemic condition. We report a 76-year-old woman who presented to the hospital with left ring fingertip digital necrosis. Despite prior blunt trauma, significant laboratory abnormalities suggested potential for alternative underlying causes. Inpatient care consisted of allopurinol, intravenous fluids, and broad-spectrum antibiotics. The region of dry gangrene eventually fully declared and autoamputated during outpatient workup. Two months later, the patient presented to the emergency department with idiopathic leukocytosis and was diagnosed with a JAK2 V617F myeloproliferative neoplasm via peripheral blood smear. Unfortunately, the patient died 2 weeks later due to hemorrhagic conversion of an ischemic stroke.
items.author: He AQ, Waitt T, Hernandez NS, Lombana N, Broderick MT, Czerwinski WL.

items.title: Effects of Climate Change on the Population Dynamics of a Long-Lived Fish.
items.summary: Population dynamics of long-lived species can be affected by environmental variation driven by climate change. Predicted climate changes in Western North America include a shift from snowmelt to rainfall driven runoff, increased stochasticity in runoff, and prolonged droughts. We used a matrix population model coupled with predicted changes in climate to project future population dynamics and persistence of a long-lived freshwater fish, June sucker ( Chasmistes liorus ). We evaluated population dynamics of June suckers under four likely climate scenarios: (1) increased stochastic variation in river flow, (2) increased amplitude in cyclic lake level variation from 1 m to 1.5 m, (3) a 0.5 m decline in average lake level, and (4) varying periods in cyclic lake levels from 30 years to 6 years.
items.author: Orocu BM, Peck SL, Richardson RA, Tuckfield RC, Belk MC.

items.title: New trade-restrictive measures surge but WTO members step up trade facilitation efforts
items.summary: The pace of newly-introduced tariffs and other non-facilitating measures rose sharply in the first half of 2026, while the stockpile of such measures reached a record level, according to the WTO Director-General's latest annual overview of developments in the international trading environment. At the same time, WTO members introduced a significant number of trade-facilitating measures, helping to sustain global trade flows despite heightened geopolitical tensions and economic uncertainty.

items.title: Plasma biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease reveal conserved features of age-related neurodegeneration in chimpanzees and humans
items.summary: Aging is a major risk factor for Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (AD/ADRD). Yet, the physiological relationships linking age-related changes in peripheral biomarkers and measures of brain structure have only recently begun to be explored. Nonhuman primates, whose brains naturally express some of the pathologic hallmarks of AD/ADRD, including amyloid-beta (A{beta}) plaques, vascular amyloid, and neurofibrillary tangles, represent a critical translational bridge between rodent models and humans. Here, we utilized ultrasensitive multiplex assays and structural MRI to examine the relationship of plasma AD/ADRD biomarkers with age, sex, and whole brain cortical thickness (CT) and gray matter volume (GMV) in a cohort of chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes), humans' closest extant living relatives.
items.author: Edler, M. K., Mhatre-Winters, I., Sherwood, C. C. et al.

items.title: Nuclear phylogenomics illuminates deep lineage divergence and complex evolutionary histories in Dipsacales
items.summary: Relationships among the five subfamilies of Linnina within Dipsacales remain contentious. Extensive nuclear gene-tree discordance and cytonuclear discordance involving Linnaeoideae complicate reconstruction of their early evolutionary history. We analyzed whole-genome resequencing data from 88 Dipsacales species representing all nine subfamilies and eight outgroups. Using Dipsacales-specific nuclear reference locus sets, we recovered 3,023 orthologous nuclear loci. Nuclear analyses consistently placed (Morinoideae + Zabelioideae) sister to (Linnaeoideae + (Valerianoideae + Dipsacoideae)) across inference methods and character-coding schemes. Despite strong backbone support, extensive gene-tree discordance persisted at deep nodes. Node-level analyses suggested that incomplete lineage sorting (ILS) was a major source of discordance, while evidence for ancient gene flow varied among nodes.
items.author: Wang, h.-f., Jiang, d., Yan, J. et al.

items.title: Revisiting homoploid hybrid speciation in Australian cotton (Gossypium) species
items.summary: One of the earliest described cases of putative homoploid hybrid speciation was 35 years ago for the Australian cotton species, Gossypium bickii. This inference was based on discordance between chloroplast- and nuclear-based phylogenetic reconstructions, a type of incongruence that has become a relatively common observation in plants. Here we reevaluate evidence bearing on the evolutionary history of G. bickii in the context of an expanded sampling of all but one of the 17 described Australian cotton species, using whole-genome resequencing data based on 18,784 single-copy nuclear genes and entire plastome sequences. Genome-wide phylogenomic analyses resolved three well-defined sections (Sturtia, Hibiscoidea and Grandicalyx) and recapitulate the previously reported discordance between nuclear and plastid phylogenies.
items.author: Ning, W., Arick, M. A., Udall, J. A. et al.

items.title: RAMA: a global genome size database of invasive tetrapod species
items.summary: Motivation: Rising numbers of biological invasions have triggered widespread erosion of environmental and socio-economic stability worldwide. To predict and understand the impacts of current and future invasive non-native species (INNS), invasion science has increased collective efforts to elucidate the role of functional traits as drivers of INNS establishments and impacts. Tetrapod vertebrates (reptiles, amphibians, mammals and birds) represent exceptionally well-studied animal lineages with broad data availability, while serving as regular model systems on the predictors of invasion success and impacts. However, while efforts exist to compile data on phenotypic traits, the availability of databases linking phenotypes and genomes remains neglected among animals.
items.author: Miall, A., Bodey, T., Cuthbert, R. et al.

items.title: Genotype and environment shape gene regulatory variation in switchgrass
items.summary: Local adaptation is contingent on genotype-by-environment interactions, which are often mediated by variation in gene expression. The causes and consequences of variation in gene expression are complex, and they are rarely evaluated under the multi-dimensional environmental regimes that occur in the field. Here, we investigate switchgrass gene expression variation in contrasting sites in Michigan and Texas. We examined differentially expressed genes between upland and lowland switchgrass genotypes and found that genes with genotype x environment (GxE) interactions were enriched for GO terms related to phosphorus metabolism. After mapping expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) in a switchgrass diversity panel in both sites, we compared distinct categories of eQTL to investigate their effects on gene expression in contrasting environments and their evolutionary history.
items.author: Berg, C. S., Pereira, C. G., Sreedasyam, A. et al.

items.title: Game structure shapes normative preferences and inter-brain neural synchrony in free-allocation public goods games
items.summary: Threshold public goods games (TPGGs) are generally expected to facilitate coordination more effectively than linear public goods games (LPGGs), because an explicit provision point can support non-zero equilibria and transform a social dilemma into a coordination problem. This prediction, however, is based largely on settings in which group members contribute to a single shared pool. Whether it extends to environments in which individuals freely allocate resources across multiple partners remains unknown. Here, using a three-person ring network and functional near-infrared spectroscopy hyperscanning, we examined how free allocation shaped behavioral and neural signatures in the two game structures. Contrary to conventional expectations, the LPGG produced stronger partner-specific reciprocity and greater alignment to history-dependent contribution standards than the TPGG.
items.author: Li, Y., Xing, W., Wu, Y. et al.

items.title: A field-potential signature of pre-burst dynamics in human higher-order thalamic neurons
items.summary: The aperiodic (1/f) component of the local field potential (LFP), long dismissed as noise, is increasingly being recognized as physiologically meaningful. Its exponent has been proposed to index excitation:inhibition (E:I) balance, with higher exponents (steeper spectra) corresponding to greater inhibition. Yet this hypothesis remains debated and has seldom been tested against single-neuron activity. Here, we used rare concurrent single-neuron and LFP recordings from the human pulvinar during goal-directed behavior and quiet wakefulness. Pulvinar recordings in both states revealed signatures of low-threshold calcium spikes (LTS) bursting. Prior work with intracellular recordings have established that LTS bursts require a sustained, spike-free period of hyperpolarization followed by a triggering depolarization, offering a physiologically-grounded test of the E:I hypothesis.
items.author: Varisa, L., Nester, E., Bhattarai, B. et al.

items.title: Spatial Transcriptomics Reveals Age-Specific Cancer Hallmark Architecture in Pediatric and Adult Brain Tumors
items.summary: Pediatric cancers are fundamentally different from their adult counterparts. Specifically, pediatric cancers carry fewer mutations, interact with developing immune systems, and have active developmental microenvironments. The tumor microenvironment (TME), which includes the surrounding stromal cells, immune cells, blood vessels, and extracellular matrix, plays a crucial role in cancer progression, metastasis, behavior, and treatment response. To better understand the effects of the pediatric tumor microenvironment on tumor gene expression, we acquired spatial transcriptomic data from 17 pediatric brain tumor samples and analyzed it through a Cancer Hallmarks framework. Cancer Hallmarks, as outlined by Hanahan and Weinberg, provide a comprehensive set of 14 biological capabilities that cancers acquire to enable tumor growth and metastasis.
items.author: Moffat, N. T., Tolbert, C. T., Middleton, C. W. et al.

items.title: Bidirectional acetate exchange couples ethanol turnover to acetyl-CoA metabolism in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
items.summary: Overflow metabolism describes the excretion of partially oxidized metabolites into the extracellular environment during rapid sugar utilization. Although these metabolites can later be reused, it remains unclear whether reassimilation also occurs during ongoing sugar consumption, and if so, how. Here, 13C-isotope tracing and metabolic flux analysis of acetate exchange in Saccharomyces cerevisiae during hexose utilization reveal that net acetate overflow is only the small difference between order-of-magnitude larger simultaneous excretion and assimilation fluxes. Unlike ethanol production, acetate exchange is not determined by hexose uptake but depends on metabolic processes downstream of glycolysis. Ethanol oxidation contributes to acetate excretion even during net ethanol production, directly linking the two main overflow pathways.
items.author: Carneiro, A., Koodorut, M. Z., Kulyk, H. et al.

items.title: N- and T-genes framework for pathway deregulation: Taxonomy, progression, and protection in cancer
items.summary: Background. Pathway analysis is widely used to interpret gene expression, but conventional enrichment depends on arbitrary thresholds and does not quantify deregulation magnitude. Recent reformulations based on average log-fold changes remove the threshold but still average over all annotated genes, diluting the signal from the genes that actually drive the normal-to-tumor transition. The N/T framework, which identifies genes with exclusive expression intervals in normal (N) or tumor (T) samples, offers a selective alternative, but it had not been extended to pathway- level quantification, taxonomy, or cross-cancer comparison. Methods. We define effective activation frequencies for Reactome pathways based on N- and T-genes: for each sample and pathway, the effective N (T) frequency is the fraction of annotated N (T) genes active in a normal (tumor) sample.
items.author: Nieves, J., Vazquez-Blomquist, D., Gonzalez, A.

items.title: Scalable biophysical constraints link steady-state and kinetic metabolic modeling
items.summary: Rational metabolic engineering relies on models that connect molecular mechanisms to cellular behavior. Constraint-based metabolic models integrate stoichiometric, thermodynamic, and omics-derived information, but they do not generally constrain whether flux magnitudes are compatible with the corresponding metabolite pool sizes. Metabolite turnover rates, the ratios of total production or consumption flux to pool size, capture this relationship and quantify how rapidly pools are renewed. Without turnover constraints, such models can admit flux-concentration combinations with implausible pool-renewal timescales despite satisfying mass balance and thermodynamics. We present METEOR-K, a scalable framework that couples steady-state fluxes and metabolite concentrations through turnover-rate constraints and turnover-aware sampling.
items.author: Toumpe, I., Weilandt, D. R., Narayanan, B. et al.

items.title: Personalized functional networks scale with brain size beyond anatomy and are altered in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome
items.summary: Anatomically, cortical regions scale differentially with total brain size: some show disproportionate contraction in smaller brains and expansion in larger brains, while others show relative stability. Whether personalized functional networks (PFNs) follow similar areal scaling principles, and how these principles shape functional reorganization in conditions that alter brain size, remain unknown. We investigated PFN scaling in typical development (ages 8-23; n=1,332) and 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22q11DS), a neuropsychiatric genetic disorder with globally reduced brain size (62 cases, 153 matched controls; ages 10-24). In typical development, PFN scaling diverged from anatomy, deviating more from proportional scaling, particularly in association networks. In 22q11DS, accounting for expected scaling with brain size reduction revealed two robust network effects: relative peripheral visual reduction and relative cingulo-opercular enlargement.
items.author: Sun, K. Y., Snyder, W., Tong, T. T. et al.

items.title: Confidence in global motion discrimination is better predicted by perceptual reliability than by stimulus-based heuristics
items.summary: Decision-making requires evaluating the reliability of perceptual estimates, but whether confidence reflects perceptual reliability or stimulus-based heuristics remains debated. We used a multiple-aperture global motion stimulus in which the global direction, and therefore motion coherence, is only available after integrating locally ambiguous signals, so that no simple stimulus statistic can serve as a shortcut. Observers reported the global direction in two successive intervals and then chose which decision was more likely to be correct. Confidence tracked accuracy beyond what coherence alone could explain: observers were more accurate in chosen intervals even at the same coherence level. Observers also frequently reported the direction opposite to the true motion, and, in direct comparisons, were more confident in these errors than in other large errors.
items.author: Oluk, C., Szinte, M., Masson, G. S. et al.

items.title: Neurocognitive signatures of intrinsic motivation in naturalistic information seeking and memory
items.summary: Humans often seek information without direct external reward. Theories distinguish two major dimensions of this intrinsic motivation: wanting, the desire to resolve an information gap, and liking, the enjoyment of the information itself. However, how these motivational dimensions shape self-guided information-seeking behavior, neural activity, and memory formation in realworld contexts remains underexplored. To address this gap, we developed a naturalistic fMRI paradigm in which participants freely browsed the internet, subsequently recalled their browsing experiences, and retrospectively reported their moment-to-moment wanting and liking. We found that both dimensions predicted more stable browsing trajectories but engaged partially dissociable neural systems: wanting recruited regions supporting goal-directed cognition, whereas liking engaged affective regions.
items.author: Su, H., Knight, C., Liu, P. R. et al.

items.title: Acute hypertension causes focal coronary artery perivascular cGAS-, IRF3, and IFNAR-dependent type I interferon responses
items.summary: Hypertension exposes coronary arteries to dynamic mechanical forces that alter the structural integrity and lead to pathologic changes such as aneurysm, dissection, or atherogenesis. Although the effects of chronic hypertension have been extensively studied, the early molecular responses to increased luminal pressure remain poorly understood. Here, we find that acute hypertension in murine coronary arteries induced by transverse aortic constriction (TAC) causes focal perivascular type I interferon (IFN) responses in the vessel wall in contrast to comparatively homogeneous perivascular fibrosis. Spatial transcriptomics and RNAscope independently demonstrate spatially clustered expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) in the walls of pressurized left and right coronary arteries in the first week after TAC.
items.author: Castellanos, G., Wright, S. J., Gunes, B. et al.

items.title: Prim-O-glucosylcimifugin suppresses M2 macrophage polarization via the JAK2-STAT6-PPARγ pathway to alleviate allergic asthma
items.summary: Background: Allergic asthma (AA) is a chronic respiratory disease closely linked to immune-inflammatory responses driven by M2 macrophage polarization. PrimO-glucosylcimifugin (POG), a natural bioactive compound from Saposhnikovia divaricata (SD), alleviates inflammation in acute lung injury mice, but whether it mitigates AA by modulating M2 macrophage polarization remains unclear. Objective: This study investigated POGs effects on AA and its mechanisms in regulating M2 macrophage polarization. Methods: LC-MS profiled the SD/Prunus mume (PM) combination, and network pharmacology predicted its main active components and key anti-AA mechanisms. Ovalbumin (OVA) plus IL-4 established AA models in mice and RAW264.7 cells. Lung protection was assessed by histopathology, lung indices, and type II immune inflammatory cytokine markers.
items.author: Li, C., Zhang, H., Yang, W. et al.

items.title: Carbon allocation strategies across Mucoromycota and the discovery of oxalic acid secretion in Absidia
items.summary: In this work, nine strains representing eight species, seven genera, and five families from the phylum Mucoromycota were studied for their production of biomolecules (lipids, saccharides, phosphates, organic acids, ethanol, and glycerol) under cultivation in media with different carbon-to-nitrogen (low, medium, and high). Although lipid accumulation was a common feature across the species, the results revealed also differences in carbon allocation strategies between families, both in magnitude and nature of the biomolecules produced. In general, members of Mucoraceae allocated carbon and energy toward the production of lipids, polyphosphates, organic acids, ethanol and glycerol; Mortierellaceae toward lipids, saccharides, and to a lesser extent to organic acids; Cunninghamellaceae toward lipids, phosphates, and saccharides; Lichtheimiaceae toward lipids and saccharides; and Umbelopsidaceae toward lipids, phosphates, and slightly to organic acids.
items.author: Bolano-Losada, C., Zimmermann, B., Byrtusova, D. et al.

items.title: Unravelling bacteriochlorophyll biosynthesis in the uncultured Roseilinea
items.summary: Filamentous anoxygenic phototrophs (FAPs) of the Chloroflexota phylum are abundant members of microbial mat communities. All isolated and culturable FAPs are found in a single class within this phylum, but metagenomic studies of hot spring communities from around the world have indicated that phototrophic members of an additional class may exist, which have so far eluded cultivation for study in the laboratory. Metagenome-assemble genomes (MAGs) of these "Candidatus Roseilinea" species all lack genes encoding the central enzymes of bacteriochlorophyll biosynthesis common to all FAPs and to the seven other diverse phyla of anoxygenic phototrophs, which could indicate that these organisms are no longer phototrophic or that they employ a novel set of enzymes to generate chlorophyllide from magnesium protoporphyrin IX.
items.author: Rudling, N. M., Namoon, D., Thiel, V. et al.

items.title: Efficient Method for Estimating the Frequency of Plasmidless Cell Generation per Cell Division
items.summary: Plasmids are self-replicating pieces of DNA that play a major role in the evolution and spread of adaptive genes in bacteria. Plasmids tend to form stable associations with their hosts, including plasmids such as small, multicopy plasmids that typically lack specialized partition and horizontal transfer systems. Using a ColE1 plasmid model, we present a method that quantifies the frequency of plasmid loss over a short, defined time window. This method is based on the transient survival of plasmidless cells in the presence of selecting antibiotic and it has two main advantages over plasmid visualization approaches: (1) it does not require modifications in plasmid sequence, preventing artifactual results linked to sequence alteration, and (2) it can unambiguously resolve plasmidless cells relative to cells with a low plasmid copy number.
items.author: Egami, C., Arora, V., Camps, M.

items.title: Sugar alternatives shift the evolutionary trajectory of fluoride resistance in cariogenic and non-cariogenic dental bacteria
items.summary: Dental caries result from acidogenic biofilms dissolving enamel while growing on fermentable dietary sugars. While fluoride from toothpastes and professional products is widely used for caries control, sugar alternatives with inhibitory effects on some dental microbiota (e.g., erythritol and xylitol) instead reduce the cariogenicity of foods and act as prebiotics, often in combination with of fluoride, to control caries progression. Despite their growing prevalence, we do not understand how frequent exposure to sugar alternatives impacts the evolutionary pressures faced by oral bacteria. Herein, we tested the effects of carbon source (glucose, sorbitol, erythritol, or xylitol) on the modes and effectiveness of evolving fluoride resistant cariogenic (S.
items.author: Shay, M. R., Eakin, M. A., Stockbridge, R. B. et al.

items.title: From CSP7 to CSP5: Development of a soluble, truncated congener for the treatment of obstructive and restrictive lung diseases.
items.summary: Chronic obstructive and restrictive lung diseases (CLDs), represent a substantial worldwide health burden, with curative therapies remaining largely unavailable. Studies from our group and others have identified caveolin-1 (Cav1)-mediated signaling as a critical regulator of cellular processes implicated in the pathogenesis and progression of CLDs, including chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), silicosis and other progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PF) conditions. We have previously demonstrated that Cav1 scaffolding domain peptides (CSP and CSP7), attenuate lung injury and PF across multiple preclinical mouse models and exhibit protective and anti-fibrotic effects in COPD and IPF tissues ex vivo. The mechanism involves concurrent suppression of p53 and its downstream signaling in lung (airway and alveolar) epithelial cells by competitively counteracting excess Cav1, while restoring baseline p53 levels in (myo)fibroblasts persisting in fibrotic lungs, and alternatively polarized alveolar macrophages (AMs) by complementing Cav1 function.
items.author: Balnadupete, A., Mugaranja, K., Shetty, R. et al.

items.title: Docking and SPR identify candidate interactions between Apolipoprotein A-I and chemokine receptors
items.summary: Background: Apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1), the main protein component of high-density lipoprotein, suppresses chemokine-driven leukocyte migration. This effect is usually attributed to indirect mechanisms such as cholesterol efflux, changes in lipid rafts, and altered receptor expression. Whether ApoA1 interacts with chemokine receptors directly is not known. Methods: We combined in silico rigid-body docking of AlphaFold-predicted structures (GRAMM-X, with interface analysis by PDBePISA) and surface plasmon resonance (SPR). In SPR experiments, ApoA1 was immobilized on the sensor, and CCR1, CCR5, CX3CR1, CXCR2, and CXCR4 were incorporated into proteoliposomes and injected as analytes. Mock proteoliposomes lacking any receptor served as a negative control.
items.author: Romel, C., Blanchet, X., Maas, S. et al.

items.title: Pathogenic role of cGAS-STING pathway in Duchenne muscular dystrophy
items.summary: The cGAS-STING pathway is a critical component of the innate immune response to infection and cell stress. Chronic activation underlies human diseases such as lupus and inflammatory bowel disease, but cGAS-STING has not been implicated in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD). Compared to healthy controls, macrophages from DMD patients have high levels of cytosolic DNA and low levels of the DNA exonuclease, TREX1, a scavenger of cytosolic DNA upstream of cGAS-STING. Likewise, cytosolic DNA is elevated in macrophages from dystrophin-deficient mdx mice. Such macrophages over-produce cGAMP and secrete it locally, activating STING in neighboring myoblasts and thereby suppressing myogenesis. TY1, a synthetic non-coding RNA drug that enhances TREX1, attenuates cGAS-STING and restores cellular and tissue homeostasis in mdx mice.
items.author: Rannou, A., Manriquez, N., Chakraborty, S. et al.

items.title: Spatial coordination of filamentous enzymes establishes a redox-balancing metabolon
items.summary: Nutrient scarcity in tumors prompts metabolic adaptations in cancer cells. Here, we identify that glutamine deprivation, a common feature of the tumor microenvironment, induces formation of a proline biosynthesis metabolon to selectively maintain intracellular proline levels. Mechanistically, filament-forming enzymes glutaminase (GLS) and pyrroline-5-carboxylate synthase (P5CS) co-assemble with the downstream reductases PYCR1 and PYCR2 into a physically associated enzyme complex within a spatially segregated mitochondrial subset. This assembly is dynamically regulated by the pathway intermediate glutamate and is membrane-anchored via ATP synthase. Disruption of enzyme spatial coordination compromises pathway activity, while the sustained proline biosynthesis is repurposed to support redox homeostasis under limited glutamine.
items.author: Kutlesic, N., Krivitsky, S., de Ruiter Swain, J. et al.

items.title: Targeted siRNA screening coupled with unbiased proteomics identify potassium signaling as a critical regulator of pigmentation
items.summary: Ion channels are emerging as critical regulators of cellular signaling, influencing diverse pathophysiological processes and offering promising opportunities for therapeutic intervention. However, the contribution of ionic homeostasis to human skin pigmentation remains poorly understood. Here, we identify potassium (K+) dynamics as a critical regulator of pigmentation and uncover K+ channel Kir7.1 as a molecular link between K+ and cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) signaling. A targeted siRNA screen identified six previously unrecognized regulators of pigmentation, which we validated using mouse cell line systems, primary human melanocytes, and an in vivo zebrafish model. Unbiased proteomic analyses of two prominent screening hits, Rhot1 and VDAC3, led us to identify Kir7.1, a plasma membrane-localized K+ channel, as a key determinant of pigmentation.
items.author: Ahuja, K., Panthri, I., Tanwar, A. et al.

items.title: Mechanically coupled proliferation controls notochord geometry during axis elongation
items.summary: The notochord is a central organizing structure in vertebrate development, functioning as a signaling axis that patterns surrounding tissues while undergoing rapid elongation. Despite its importance, how notochord shape is regulated to ensure robust morphogen signaling remains poorly understood. Here, we combine high-resolution 3D imaging of mouse embryos between E8.5 to E10.5 of development with a data-driven biophysical model to investigate the mechanisms underlying notochord morphogenesis. We find that the notochord maintains a remarkably constant cross-sectional area along most of its anterior-posterior extent, a feature that is preserved over time and in mutants with reduced body axis length. To uncover the cellular basis of this geometric robustness, we quantified cell behaviours and their contribution to notochord morphogenesis.
items.author: Kishi, K., Xue, S.-L., Dalla Vecchia, M. et al.

items.title: Taxonomic turnover with phylogenetic conservation in subaerial biofilm (SAB) communities of marble monuments
items.summary: Subaerial biofilms (SABs) colonizing exposed stone surfaces provide natural systems for investigating microbial community assembly under challenging environmental conditions. Although bacterial diversity on stone has been widely described, whether taxonomic variation reflects broader phylogenetic and ecological differences remains unclear. Here, we characterized SAB communities inhabiting two geographically separated historic urban marble monuments, Federal Hall National Memorial (New York) and the Lincoln Memorial (Washington, DC), using SSU rRNA amplicon sequencing. Additional samples from the Merchants' Exchange Building (Philadelphia) were also examined. Bacterial communities exhibited pronounced taxonomic turnover but substantially greater phylogenetic similarity, indicating that community variation primarily reflected replacement among closely related bacterial lineages rather than turnover among distantly related clades.
items.author: Grattepanche, J.-D., Jacob, J. M., Tenore, A. et al.

items.title: Cross-level correlation and temporal dynamics of hierarchical habitat selection
items.summary: Habitat selection is a fundamentally hierarchical process implying that choices made by animals at broad spatial scales constrain those made at finer ones. How selection for the same habitats relates across hierarchical orders remains largely untested empirically. We investigated whether selection for a given habitat at the larger scale reinforces itself, is independent of, or opposes selection for the same habitat at the finer scale. Using GPS-collared European hares (Lepus europaeus, n = 52) in a mid-mountain grassland landscape (French Jura, 2021-2023), we jointly quantified and compared temporal variation in second-order (home range placement within the landscape) and third-order (habitat use within home ranges) selection with generalised linear mixed models, and resource selection functions.
items.author: Berger, L., Henriot, C. P., Powolny, T. et al.

items.title: Environmental and particle trait controls on microbial carbon turnover on fast-sinking particles in the Iceland Basin
items.summary: Microbial remineralisation of sinking particles governs the depth and magnitude of organic carbon sequestration in the ocean. Yet, the combined influence of environmental gradients and particle morphology in regulating remineralisation remains poorly constrained. During spring in the subpolar Icelandic Basin, we estimated microbial carbon turnover, a proxy for remineralization, on fast sinking particles collected at two depths below the mixed-layer using shipboard incubations. Alongside this we used imagery to determine the morphology and complexity of the particles. Microbial carbon turnover exhibited strong depth-dependent variability, with generally higher rates in shallower samples and substantial variability among stations and sampling days. Fast-sinking particle assemblages were dominated by aggregates and detrital material, while faecal pellets comprised only a minor fraction of particles, and particle diversity decreased with depth.
items.author: Roberts, C., Garcia-Martin, E. E., Robinson, C. et al.

items.title: Visual Landmarks Influence Eye-Hand Coordination in Memory-Guided Reaches
items.summary: The human visual system optimally weighs egocentric cues (e.g., object location relative to the eye) and allocentric cues (e.g., object location relative to other landmarks) to aim actions. The neural mechanisms of this process have been studied in the primate gaze system, but it is not known how these results extend to eye-hand coordination and the reach system. Here, reach and gaze (eye-in-space) data were collected from two head-unrestrained Macaca mulatta (M1, M2) trained to reach toward remembered visual targets on a touch screen. During the delay, animals either saw nothing (no-landmark), a pattern of 'dots' around the target (stable landmark), or a similar landmark that reappeared at a shifted position (landmark shift).
items.author: Lin, J., Nacher, V., Karimi, A. et al.

items.title: Arene binding by silazido heavier alkaline earth cations.
items.summary: Reactions of [Ph 3 C] + [Al{OC(CF 3 ) 3 } 4 ] - with [Ae{N(SiMe 3 ) 2 } 2 ] 2 (Ae = Ca, Sr) or [Ba{N(SiMe 3 ) 2 } 2 (THF)] 2 have been studied in benzene, mesitylene and chlorobenzene. Irrespective of Ae identity, interrogation of the bulk constitutions of the resultant systems was complicated by liquid clathrate formation. X-ray diffraction analysis of single crystals, however, identified the formation of bimetallic dications, [(η 6 -C 6 H 6 )Ae-μ-N(SiMe 3 ) 2 ] 2 2+ , and monometallic monocations, [(η 6 -1,3,5-Me 3 C 6 H 3 ) 2 Ae-κ 1 -N(SiMe 3 ) 2 ] + from benzene and mesitylene, respectively.
items.author: Jarvis O, Guntley JT, Hill MS, Mahon MF, Pearce KG, McMullin CL.

items.title: Pulsed hyperfine EPR study of formally divalent rare earth (scandium, yttrium, lanthanum) arene complexes.
items.summary: Pulsed EPR hyperfine spectroscopy of the formal rare earth(II) arene complexes [RE II (NHAr iPr6 ) 2 ] (2M, M = Sc, Y, La; NHAr iPr6 = {N(H)C 6 H 3 -2,6-(C 6 H 2 -2,4,6- i Pr 3 ) 2 }), supported by DFT, reveals extensive delocalisation of spin density to the arene ring bound to the metal (56-73% Mulliken spin population, 42-53% Löwdin orbital population of SOMO, from DFT). Hence, they are RE(II) complexes in a formal sense only.
items.author: Hajdu T, MacKenzie RE, Tuna F, Goodwin CAP, McInnes EJL.

items.title: Electrophysiological Markers in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Enhancing Sudden Cardiac Death Risk Prediction with Index of Cardiac Electrophysiological Balance and Its Corrected Variant.
items.summary: Background Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is characterized by asymmetric left ventricular hypertrophy and myocardial fibrosis, which significantly increases the risk of sudden cardiac death (SCD). Existing risk stratification models are limited in predicting SCD risk in patients within the "gray zone"-those with intermediate risk. This study investigates the prognostic utility of the Index of Cardiac Electrophysiological Balance (ICEB) and its corrected variant (ICEBc) in predicting ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) in HCM. To evaluate the predictive value of ICEB and ICEBc for Life-Threatening Arrhythmias (LTA) and non-sustained ventricular tachycardia (NSVT) in HCM and compare their performance with traditional repolarization parameters and the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) SCD Risk Score.
items.author: Balaban İ, Tanyeri S, Karaduman A, Kültürsay B, Gültekin Güner E, Keten MF, Efe SÇ, Alizade E.

items.title: SCN8A-Related Epilepsy and/or Neurodevelopmental Disorders
items.summary: Clinical characteristics SCN8A-related epilepsy and/or neurodevelopmental disorders (SCN8A-E/NDD) encompass a spectrum of phenotypes. Epilepsy phenotypes include developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) associated with severe developmental delays and usually pharmacoresistant epilepsy with multiple seizure types; mild-to-moderate developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (mild/modDEE) with partially treatable epilepsy; benign familial infantile epilepsy (BFIE, or self-limited familial infantile epilepsy, SeLFIE), with typically normal cognition and medically treatable seizures; neurodevelopmental delays with generalized epilepsy (NDDwGE); and neurodevelopmental disorder without epilepsy (NDDwoE) with mild-to-moderate intellectual disability (though it can be severe in ~10% of affected individuals). Hypotonia and movement disorders including dystonia, ataxia, and choreoathetosis are common in some phenotypes.
items.author: Hammer MF, Hack J, Schreiber JM.

items.title: MPV17-Related Mitochondrial DNA Maintenance Syndrome
items.summary: Clinical characteristics MPV17-related mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) maintenance syndrome presents in most affected individuals as an early-onset encephalohepatopathic (hepatocerebral) disease that is typically associated with mtDNA depletion, particularly in the liver. A later-onset disease, MPV17-related Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 (CMT2EE), characterized by myopathy and neuropathy and associated with multiple mtDNA deletions in muscle, has also rarely been described. MPV17-related encephalohepatopathy is characterized by hepatic manifestations (liver dysfunction that typically progresses to liver failure, cholestasis, hepatomegaly, and steatosis); neurologic involvement (developmental delay, hypotonia, microcephaly, and motor and sensory peripheral neuropathy); gastrointestinal manifestations (faltering growth, gastrointestinal dysmotility, and feeding difficulties); and metabolic derangements (lactic acidosis and hypoglycemia).
items.author: Almannai M, El-Hattab AW, Scaglia F, Craigen WJ.

items.title: PAX2-Related Disorder
items.summary: Clinical characteristics PAX2-related disorder is characterized by abnormal kidney structure or function in up to 92% of affected individuals and ophthalmologic abnormalities in up to 77% of affected individuals. In most individuals, clinically significant kidney insufficiency / kidney failure is reported. End-stage kidney disease requiring kidney transplant is not uncommon. Kidney abnormalities can also be clinically silent. Ophthalmologic abnormalities are typically described as optic nerve dysplasia, although coloboma is also used to describe the optic nerve defect. Ophthalmologic abnormalities may significantly impair vision in some individuals, while others have subtle changes only noted after detailed retinal and visual evaluation. Additional clinical findings include childhood-onset bilateral symmetric high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss.
items.author: Bower MA, Schimmenti LA, Eccles MR.

items.title: Fundamental physics with quantum sensors in space
items.summary: Quantum sensors such as atomic clocks, atom interferometers, and atomic magnetometers can be used as sensitive probes of physics beyond the Standard Model. Space offers microgravity, long baselines, low environmental noise, access to varying gravitational potentials, and unique opportunities involving the Sun, Moon, planets, and asteroids. These proceedings of the Aspen Center for Physics workshop on "Fundamental physics in space with quantum sensors," held February 22-27, 2026, summarize the scientific case, current capabilities, and space mission concepts for investigating dark matter, testing general relativity, and detecting gravitational waves in frequency bands inaccessible from the ground.
items.author: Jason Arakawa, Daniel J. Blumenthal, Oliver Buchmueller et al.

items.title: Perseverance Update: The Ghostly Rocks of ‘Idubi’ — Bright Remnants of Aqueous Systems from Long Ago
items.summary: Written by Candice Bedford, Research Scientist at Purdue University Date: Nov. 16, 2026 During the Perseverance rover’s investigation of “Idubi” — an area of ancient Martian crust exposed in the “Lac de Charmes” region, outside of Jezero crater — the Perseverance rover team has been captivated by a cluster of eerily bright, light-toned rocks in […]

items.title: Photonic Maxwells demon as an energy resource
items.summary: We propose a new realization of Maxwells demon for photons and its use as an energy resource. The starting point is a multilayer dielectric mirror that transmits photons within a certain wavelength band but reflects photons at longer wavelengths, followed by a material that irreversibly converts the wavelength. A 3D box constructed from these one-way mirrors is a self-acting Maxwells demon for photons. The first case considered is a one-way mirror for visible photons, converting blue to red as an example. The next case is a one-way mirror that transmits visible light but reflects infrared light, followed by a perfect blackbody.
items.author: Mark G. Raizen, Aaron Barr, Ahmed Helal

items.title: Bandwidth-tunable thermal emitter via dynamic resonator coupling and loss
items.summary: We demonstrate a dynamically tunable omnidirectional thermal emitter that can be switched from a narrowband emission state to a broadband state. The structure is a metal-backed multilayer with subwavelength thickness across the mid-infrared, which forms an angle-insensitive (up to 60°) optical cavity with one input port. We used an ultrathin VO2 layer to dynamically switch the coupling and loss coefficients of this optical cavity, resulting in narrowband emission from the vibrational mode of a polar dielectric layer that is part of the multilayer stack when the VO2 is in its insulating phase, and broadband emission from a nearly impedance-matched cavity when the VO2 is switched to its lossy metallic phase.
items.author: Jin-Woo Cho, Tanuj Kumar, Joseph A. Andrade et al.

items.title: Spatiotemporal programming of shape memory polymers for tunable vibration responses
items.summary: Stimuli-responsive materials offer a promising route to dynamically tailor material behavior, enabling adaptive functionalities in changing environments. However, simultaneously implementing spatial and temporal control in active material systems remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we present a photothermally programmable shape memory polymer (SMP) metamaterial platform that enables dynamic control of elastic wave propagation through reconfigurable spatiotemporal temperature distributions. By projecting user-defined light patterns onto carbon-doped SMP (C-SMP) surfaces, spatial thermomechanical property landscapes are generated, enabling a wide range of elastic wave functionalities, including tunable transmission spectra and programmable vibrational modes. By treating both space and time as design parameters, we access an expanded design space that allows a bulk C-SMP surface to function as a highly adaptive metamaterial platform.
items.author: Samantha Averitt, Jay Sim, Ruike Renee Zhao

items.title: M 6.6 - 149 km WSW of Tual, Indonesia

items.title: A microscopic revision of the rate equations of a heavily erbium-doped fiber laser
items.summary: Heavily erbium-doped fiber lasers can exhibit self-pulsing induced by interacting ion pairs, which was found in numerous experiments and supported by modeling. However, conventional rate-equation models rely on phenomenological parameters with an unclear microscopic origin. We derive a rate-equation model using a Lindblad master equation describing isolated erbium ions and interacting ion pairs coupled to a single cavity mode, with cooperative upconversion represented by an effective dissipative process. In the strong-dephasing limit, adiabatic elimination of coherences and ensemble averaging yield a closed system of equations for the cavity photon number, isolated-ion inversion, and pair populations. We show that in the same limit the pair-cavity coupling constant reduces to that of two independent ions, without superradiant or subradiant contributions.
items.author: Iaroslav L. Pozdniak, Ivan V. Vovchenko, Evgeny S. Andrianov et al.

items.title: Magnon-Phonon-Polariton Optomechanics in a van der Waals Magnet
items.summary: The layered anti-ferromagnet CrSBr hosts self-hybridized exciton-polaritons that couple parametrically to coherent magnons and phonons. In this work, we explore the tripartite optomechanical interaction between these quasiparticles in suspended CrSBr membranes supporting high-$Q$ breathing-type acoustic phonon modes. Using resonant pump-probe spectroscopy on the polariton state, we resolve the coupled dynamics in the $\simeq 20$ GHz range while sweeping the magnon mode across the phonon resonance with an external magnetic field. We observe an attractive magnon-phonon interaction of strength $V/2π= -43$ MHz, which primarily leads to phonon amplification. At the magnon-phonon resonance, we find predominantly unidirectional energy flow from magnons to phonons while the possible back-action is limited by kinetic losses of coherent magnons.
items.author: Jens-Christian Drawer, Vladislav Yu. Shishkov, Bo Han et al.

items.title: NASA Receives 16th Consecutive ‘Clean’ Financial Audit Opinion
items.summary: For the 16th consecutive year, NASA has received an unmodified, or “clean,” opinion from an external auditor on its fiscal year 2026 financial statements. The rating is the best possible audit opinion, certifying that NASA’s financial statements conform with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles for federal agencies and accurately present the agency’s financial position. “Our responsibility […]
items.author: Lauren E. Low

items.title: Anomaly inflow for simplicial Kähler fermions
items.summary: We study massive Kähler Dirac fermions propagating on finite triangulations of various three dimensional manifolds with one or more boundaries. To probe the anomaly structure of these models we decompose the Kähler field into two reduced Kähler fields and choose boundary conditions that ensure that any edge modes are necessarily massless. We then show how to factorize the Pfaffian of this system into a product of bulk and boundary sectors each of which can separately pick up a phase under a global $Z_4$ transformation of the fermions that simultaneously changes the sign of the mass. These phases are topological, depending only on the index of the lattice Kähler operator in that sector.
items.author: Simon Catterall

items.title: Structure Constants of Planar N=4 SYM at Any Coupling
items.summary: We recast a recent conjecture for structure constants in planar N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory in a separation-of-variables-inspired form suitable for non-perturbative analysis. All state-dependent information enters through the quantum spectral curve. As a showcase, we compute at finite coupling the three-point functions of two half-BPS operators and the spin-two member of the Konishi multiplet. Our results span weak to strong coupling, reproduce the known perturbative and string-theory limits, and are consistent with conformal-bootstrap bounds. We also obtain new six- and seven-loop perturbative coefficients and extract new strong-coupling data from high-precision numerical fits.
items.author: Simon Ekhammar, Alessandro Georgoudis, Nikolay Gromov

items.title: Simple Models of Thermal Order in $2+1$ Dimensions
items.summary: Heating need not destroy order. We show that it persists to arbitrarily high temperatures in simple quantum field theories in $2+1$ spacetime dimensions. In a $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ model of two real scalar fields, a sufficiently negative mixed quartic coupling drives one field to condense, spontaneously breaking its $\mathbb Z_2$ symmetry. When coupled to massless Dirac fermions through a Yukawa interaction, this condensate generates a fermion mass, thereby spontaneously breaking parity and time-reversal symmetries. We extend this construction to a $\mathbb Z_2\times O(n)$ scalar model, in which the Mermin-Wagner theorem precludes spontaneous breaking of the continuous $O(n)$ symmetry at finite temperatures.
items.author: Michael Smolkin, Lev Yung

items.title: Infrared fluctuations and collective entanglement modes in harmonic lattices
items.summary: We investigate how infrared fluctuations and spatial separation shape vacuum entanglement between two finite regions in the relativistic harmonic chain and its Lifshitz generalizations. At fixed lattice spacing and finite geometry, we establish that logarithmic negativity remains uniformly bounded as the mass approaches zero, while mutual information diverges. Infrared-enhanced total correlations therefore do not provide an unbounded distillable-entanglement resource. Using local symplectic consolidation, we identify the collective canonical modes carrying the negativity and follow their evolution with separation. Their participation crosses over from localization near the facing boundaries to a collective distribution within each region. Expansion in the adjacent-state canonical basis connects this evolution to progressively weaker, more extended reference modes, including adjacent-halo directions.
items.author: Mahsa Lezgi, Ali Mollabashi

items.title: A Forecast for Testing the Decreasing $H_0$ Trend in Time-Delay Cosmography
items.summary: In 2019 the H0LiCOW/TDCOSMO collaboration reported a decreasing Hubble constant $H_0$ trend with lens redshift in the flat $Λ$CDM model at low statistical significance ($< 2 σ$). The signal is expected if physics is missing from the $Λ$CDM model in the late universe. In the wake of recent TDCOSMO 2026 results, we revisit the feature. Although the statistical significance of the trend has increased in a like-for-like comparison with earlier studies, propagating mass-sheet transformation (MST) uncertainties reduces the significance to $\sim 1 σ$. As a result, Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) currently favours a constant $H_0$ over a decreasing $H_0$ in the ratio 2.4:1.

items.title: Probing $τ$ lepton dipole moments at multi-TeV muon colliders
items.summary: We investigate the sensitivity of future multi-TeV muon colliders to the electromagnetic and weak dipole moments of the $τ$ lepton within the dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory. We consider $τ^+τ^-$ production through $μ^+μ^-$ annihilation and vector-boson scattering, electroweak-boson-associated $τ$ production, and the radiative Higgs decay $H\toτ^+τ^-γ$. At high energies, the dipole-induced contributions quadratic in the Wilson coefficients become particularly important, with associated Higgs production, $μ^+μ^-\toτ^+τ^-H$, providing the strongest sensitivity through energy-enhanced contact interactions. The remaining channels offer complementary probes of the underlying dipole operators. For a $10$~TeV muon collider with an integrated luminosity of $10\,\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, we obtain combined sensitivities at the nominal $95\%$ confidence level of $|Δa_τ|<1.2\times10^{-5}$, $|d_τ|<6.6\times10^{-20}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$, $|Δa_τ^Z|<1.8\times10^{-5}$, and $|d_τ^Z|<1.0\times10^{-19}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$.
